items.label: Starts Kyokushin karate; father also practiced
items.detail: Krylov grew up in Krasnyi Luch (Luhansk region), Ukraine, and started Kyokushin karate at about age ten after his father introduced him to the sport. He later added hand-to-hand combat and submission fighting. His exact first karate class date is not documented.

items.label: Earns Master of Sports ranks in several disciplines
items.detail: Krylov says he earned Master of Sports of Ukraine designations in Kyokushin karate and hand-to-hand combat and a Master of Sports rank in submission fighting. The award years are not specified in the UFC questionnaire. These amateur martial arts credentials do not alter his professional MMA record.

items.label: AMATEUR LOSS · Akhmedshaikh Gelegaev · armbar
items.detail: Sherdog records an amateur loss to Akhmedshaikh Gelegaev by armbar at 2:26 of round one at Liga Kavkaz 2012. This is one documented amateur MMA result, not evidence that he had only one amateur fight in total. The amateur result is separate from his 31-12 professional record.

items.label: WIN · Alexander Umrikhin · TKO (punches) · R1
items.detail: At West Fight 4, Krylov defeated Alexander Umrikhin by tko (punches) at 0:56 of round 1. Krylov's first professional bout, after one recorded amateur loss earlier that July. The win was the beginning of 12 consecutive first-round finishes in his debut year.

items.label: WIN · Denis Bogdanov · Submission (rear-naked choke) · R1
items.detail: At Cup of West Ukraine 2012, Krylov defeated Denis Bogdanov by submission (rear-naked choke) at 1:31 of round 1.

items.label: WIN · Alexey Artemenko · Submission (guillotine choke) · R1
items.detail: At Big Boys Fights, Krylov defeated Alexey Artemenko by submission (guillotine choke) at 2:20 of round 1.

items.label: WIN · Anatoliy Didenko · Submission (rear-naked choke) · R1
items.detail: At MMA Ukraine Cup 5, Krylov defeated Anatoliy Didenko by submission (rear-naked choke) at 2:08 of round 1.

items.label: WIN · Svyatoslav Scherbakov · Submission (armbar) · R1
items.detail: At MMA Ukraine Cup 6, Krylov defeated Svyatoslav Scherbakov by submission (armbar) at 1:44 of round 1.

items.label: WIN · Alexey Stepanov · Submission (rear-naked choke) · R1
items.detail: At MMA Ukraine Cup 7, Krylov defeated Alexey Stepanov by submission (rear-naked choke) at 0:29 of round 1.

items.label: WIN · Anatoliy Didenko · Submission (Achilles lock) · R1
items.detail: At Oplot Challenge 4, Krylov defeated Anatoliy Didenko by submission (achilles lock) at 0:29 of round 1.

items.label: WIN · Viktor Smirnov · TKO (doctor stoppage) · R1
items.detail: At MMA Lion Cup, Krylov defeated Viktor Smirnov by tko (doctor stoppage) at 0:12 of round 1.

items.label: WIN · Igor Kukurudziak · Submission (kimura) · R1
items.detail: At Kolomyi Cup, Krylov defeated Igor Kukurudziak by submission (kimura) at 2:47 of round 1.

items.label: WIN · Vladimir Gerasimchik · Submission (kimura) · R1
items.detail: At Oplot Challenge 7, Krylov defeated Vladimir Gerasimchik by submission (kimura) at 1:35 of round 1.

items.label: WIN · Valeriy Shcherbakov · Submission (Achilles lock) · R1
items.detail: At Igor Vovchanchyn Cup 2, Krylov defeated Valeriy Shcherbakov by submission (achilles lock) at 1:38 of round 1.

items.label: WIN · Denis Simkin · Submission (keylock) · R1
items.detail: At Gladiators Fighting Championship 1, Krylov defeated Denis Simkin by submission (keylock) at 0:35 of round 1. This was his twelfth consecutive professional first-round finish; his first defeat followed one week later.

items.label: LOSS · Vladimir Mishchenko · Submission (arm-triangle choke) · R1
items.detail: At Oplot Challenge 22, Krylov lost to Vladimir Mishchenko by submission (arm-triangle choke) at 1:47 of round 1. Mishchenko ended Krylov's 12-0 start with a first-round arm-triangle submission; this was his first professional defeat.

items.label: Wins ADCC Ukraine grappling championship
items.detail: Krylov's UFC athlete questionnaire reports he was 2013 ADCC Ukraine champion and held a Master of Sports rank in submission fighting. The listed source does not specify the bracket, division, opponents or exact day, so these details are not inferred.

items.label: Studies at Donetsk Law Institute
items.detail: In his earlier UFC biography, Krylov reported enrollment at the Donetsk Law Institute. The source does not establish a completed degree or graduation date. He told the UFC that he had fought professionally directly after high school.

items.label: WIN · Julian Bogdanov · KO (punch) · R1
items.detail: At Gladiators Fighting Championship 2, semifinal, Krylov defeated Julian Bogdanov by ko (punch) at 1:17 of round 1. This was the semifinal of a two-fight, same-night Gladiators FC heavyweight tournament.

items.label: WIN · Kylychbek Sarkarbaev · TKO (punches) · R1
items.detail: At Gladiators Fighting Championship 2, final, Krylov defeated Kylychbek Sarkarbaev by tko (punches) at 0:49 of round 1. The first-round finish in the final won Krylov the one-night Gladiators FC heavyweight tournament. Both bouts count as separate professional wins.

items.label: Wins one-night Gladiators FC heavyweight tournament
items.detail: Krylov defeated Julian Bogdanov by first-round knockout and Kylychbek Sarkarbaev by first-round TKO on the same date at Gladiators FC 2, winning the four-man heavyweight tournament. Both victories appear separately in his professional timeline.

items.label: LOSS · Vladimir Mishchenko · Submission (arm-triangle choke) · R1
items.detail: At Oplot Challenge 40, Krylov lost to Vladimir Mishchenko by submission (arm-triangle choke) at 0:58 of round 1. Mishchenko again submitted Krylov with an arm-triangle at 0:58 of round one, winning their rematch.

items.label: WIN · Gabriel Tampu · TKO (punches) · R1
items.detail: At M-1 Challenge 38, Krylov defeated Gabriel Tampu by tko (punches) at 4:27 of round 1.

items.label: LOSS · Soa Palelei · TKO (punches) · R3
items.detail: At UFC 164, Krylov lost to Soa Palelei by tko (punches) at 1:34 of round 3. His UFC debut took place at heavyweight. Both heavyweights tired, and Krylov later discussed travel and nerves as contributing factors to the disappointing first UFC performance.

items.label: WIN · Walt Harris · TKO (head kick and punches) · R1
items.detail: At UFC on Fox 10, Krylov defeated Walt Harris by tko (head kick and punches) at 0:25 of round 1. Krylov weighed only about 218 lb as a heavyweight and won in 25 seconds. The result strengthened his decision to cut to light heavyweight.

items.label: Announces drop from heavyweight to light heavyweight
items.detail: Following his 25-second win over Walt Harris as a 218-pound heavyweight, the UFC booked Krylov against Ovince Saint Preux at 205 lb. Krylov said his 6-foot-3 frame was undersized against many UFC heavyweights and that he wanted to avoid giving up large weight differences.

items.label: LOSS · Ovince Saint Preux · Technical submission (Von Flue choke) · R1
items.detail: At UFC 171, Krylov lost to Ovince Saint Preux by technical submission (von flue choke) at 1:29 of round 1. This was Krylov's light heavyweight debut. He applied a guillotine and was put unconscious by Saint Preux's counter Von Flue choke. The official result is a technical submission, not a normal tap-out.

items.label: WIN · Cody Donovan · TKO (punches) · R1
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night 46, Krylov defeated Cody Donovan by tko (punches) at 4:57 of round 1.

items.label: Visa complications delay a Marcos Rogério de Lima fight
items.detail: Krylov had trouble obtaining a U.S. visa for a planned June 2015 UFC booking against Marcos Rogério de Lima. The matchup was later held in Saskatoon on August 23, where Krylov won. This was a visa issue, not a failed weight cut, injury or suspension.

items.label: WIN · Stanislav Nedkov · Submission (guillotine choke) · R1
items.detail: At UFC on Fox 14, Krylov defeated Stanislav Nedkov by submission (guillotine choke) at 1:24 of round 1.

items.label: WIN · Marcos Rogério de Lima · Submission (rear-naked choke) · R1
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night 74, Krylov defeated Marcos Rogério de Lima by submission (rear-naked choke) at 2:29 of round 1.

items.label: Leaves UFC after loss to Misha Cirkunov
items.detail: Krylov and the UFC parted ways following his December 2016 defeat. He later explained that he wanted to gain more experience outside the promotion before competing against top-ranked UFC light heavyweights. His departure was not described as an anti-doping suspension.

items.label: WIN · Francimar Barroso · Submission (rear-naked choke) · R2
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night 87, Krylov defeated Francimar Barroso by submission (rear-naked choke) at 3:11 of round 2.

items.label: WIN · Ed Herman · KO (head kick) · R2
items.detail: At UFC 201, Krylov defeated Ed Herman by ko (head kick) at 0:40 of round 2. This ended a five-fight UFC winning streak heading into his later defeat to Misha Cirkunov.

items.label: LOSS · Misha Cirkunov · Submission (guillotine choke) · R1
items.detail: At UFC 206, Krylov lost to Misha Cirkunov by submission (guillotine choke) at 4:38 of round 1. This submission loss ended Krylov's five-fight UFC winning streak; he subsequently left the UFC temporarily.

items.label: WIN · Stjepan Bekavac · Submission (guillotine choke) · R1
items.detail: At Fight Nights Global 68, Krylov defeated Stjepan Bekavac by submission (guillotine choke) at 0:53 of round 1. This was his first fight after leaving the UFC following the December 2016 Cirkunov defeat.

items.label: WIN · Maro Perak · TKO (punches) · R2
items.detail: At United Donbass Cup, Krylov defeated Maro Perak by tko (punches) at 0:36 of round 2.

items.label: WIN · Emanuel Newton · KO (knee) · R1
items.detail: At Fight Nights Global 77, Krylov defeated Emanuel Newton by ko (knee) at 0:43 of round 1. A 43-second knee knockout of the former Bellator light heavyweight champion was his third win outside the UFC.

items.label: WIN · Fabio Maldonado · KO (punch) · R2
items.detail: At Fight Nights Global 87, Krylov defeated Fabio Maldonado by ko (punch) at 3:33 of round 2. A second-round right-hand knockout won the Fight Nights Global light heavyweight championship, his first widely documented major professional divisional title. He finished all four bouts outside the UFC during the 2017–2018 break.

items.label: Claims Fight Nights Global 205 lb championship
items.detail: Krylov knocked out Fabio Maldonado with a right hand in round two to win the Fight Nights Global light heavyweight title. This was his fourth straight finish during his UFC absence. The victory appears separately among his professional fights.

items.label: Fight Nights Global releases Krylov to rejoin UFC
items.detail: Fight Nights Global president Kamil Gadzhiev confirmed releasing Krylov early from his contract so he could negotiate a UFC return. Krylov reentered the Octagon on September 15, 2018 against Jan Błachowicz in Moscow, after about 21 months outside the UFC.

items.label: LOSS · Jan Błachowicz · Submission (arm-triangle choke) · R2
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night 136, Krylov lost to Jan Błachowicz by submission (arm-triangle choke) at 2:41 of round 2. Krylov's September 2018 return to the UFC ended with an arm-triangle submission loss to the future UFC light heavyweight champion.

items.label: WIN · Ovince Saint Preux · Submission (rear-naked choke) · R2
items.detail: At UFC 236, Krylov defeated Ovince Saint Preux by submission (rear-naked choke) at 2:30 of round 2. Krylov avenged his first UFC light heavyweight loss against Saint Preux by submitting him with a rear-naked choke, rather than the Von Flue choke OSP used against him in 2014.

items.label: LOSS · Glover Teixeira · Decision (split)
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night 158, Krylov lost to Glover Teixeira by decision (split) after 3 five-minute rounds (final round clock 5:00). Krylov lost the three-round bout by split decision; it was his first career decision loss.

items.label: WIN · Johnny Walker · Decision (unanimous)
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night 170, Krylov defeated Johnny Walker by decision (unanimous) after 3 five-minute rounds (final round clock 5:00). The unanimous decision was Krylov's first decision victory after 27 previous professional wins by finish.

items.label: First US camp, including American Top Team
items.detail: Krylov told UFC that he began preparations in Phuket, Thailand, then accepted Yaroslav Amosov's invitation to train at American Top Team in South Florida with Conan Silveira. He described it as his first training camp in the United States. This documents a temporary training block, not necessarily a permanent gym transfer.

items.label: Volkan Oezdemir withdraws with knee injury
items.detail: Krylov was booked to face Volkan Oezdemir on October 18, 2020, but Oezdemir withdrew with a knee problem and a suitable replacement was not secured. They eventually fought on October 22, 2022, when Krylov won by decision. This cancellation does not count toward either man's record.

items.label: LOSS · Magomed Ankalaev · Decision (unanimous)
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night 186, Krylov lost to Magomed Ankalaev by decision (unanimous) after 3 five-minute rounds (final round clock 5:00).

items.label: LOSS · Paul Craig · Submission (triangle choke) · R1
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night 204, Krylov lost to Paul Craig by submission (triangle choke) at 3:57 of round 1.

items.label: WIN · Alexander Gustafsson · KO (punches) · R1
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night 208, Krylov defeated Alexander Gustafsson by ko (punches) at 1:07 of round 1. The first-round knockout of a former UFC title challenger earned a Performance of the Night bonus. This was a key rebound after the March 2022 submission loss.

items.label: WIN · Volkan Oezdemir · Decision (unanimous)
items.detail: At UFC 280, Krylov defeated Volkan Oezdemir by decision (unanimous) after 3 five-minute rounds (final round clock 5:00).

items.label: Foodborne illness cancels Ryan Spann main event
items.detail: Krylov became ill on the day of his scheduled UFC Vegas 70 main event. Medical staff administered IV fluids at the UFC Apex, but he was unable to compete. Reporting subsequently described foodborne illness. The fight was rescheduled for March 11 and went ahead at a 215 lb catchweight. This was a medical withdrawal, not a missed-weight fight result.

items.label: WIN · Ryan Spann · Submission (triangle choke) · R1
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night 221, Krylov defeated Ryan Spann by submission (triangle choke) at 3:38 of round 1. Their original Feb. 25 main event was canceled due to Krylov's illness. The rescheduled fight was a 215 lb catchweight rather than a standard 205 lb contest.

items.label: About 25 months between completed professional bouts
items.detail: After submitting Ryan Spann on March 11, 2023, Krylov did not appear in another completed professional fight until the April 12, 2025 defeat against Dominick Reyes, approximately 25 months later. This gap included canceled bookings; the available sources do not establish a single confirmed medical diagnosis explaining the full period.

items.label: Azamat Murzakanov withdraws from scheduled UFC 309 fight
items.detail: Murzakanov withdrew from the planned November 16 matchup with Krylov. MMA Fighting reported the cancellation without an officially confirmed cause at the time. CSAD subsequently documented Murzakanov's provisional anti-doping suspension beginning November 1, but the initial cancellation report did not explicitly establish the connection. The fight did not occur.

items.label: LOSS · Dominick Reyes · KO (punch) · R1
items.detail: At UFC 314, Krylov lost to Dominick Reyes by ko (punch) at 2:24 of round 1. Reyes knocked Krylov out in the first round, ending an approximately 25-month period without a completed professional fight.

items.label: LOSS · Bogdan Guskov · KO (punches) · R1
items.detail: At UFC on ABC 9, Krylov lost to Bogdan Guskov by ko (punches) at 4:18 of round 1. His second consecutive first-round KO loss in 2025 added concern about his defensive durability.

items.label: WIN · Modestas Bukauskas · KO (punches) · R3
items.detail: At UFC 324, Krylov defeated Modestas Bukauskas by ko (punches) at 4:57 of round 3. Krylov knocked him out just three seconds before the final horn of a scheduled three-round fight, a notably late third-round finish.

items.label: LOSS · Robert Whittaker · TKO (jaw injury) · R3
items.detail: At UFC 329, Krylov lost to Robert Whittaker by tko (jaw injury) at 1:01 of round 3. Former UFC middleweight champion Whittaker was making his light-heavyweight debut. After being hurt by strikes, Krylov reacted to a damaging jaw shot and the bout was stopped at 1:01 of round three. Sherdog records the official finish as TKO (jaw injury), while UFC's fight-history text calls it a stoppage by strikes. Reporting later described a broken jaw; there is no published, definitive full-recovery timeline in the referenced sources.

items.label: Jaw injury during Robert Whittaker fight
items.detail: Krylov appeared to sustain significant damage to his jaw after a hard strike from Whittaker in round three and indicated he could not continue. The official Sherdog result is TKO (jaw injury) at 1:01. Subsequent reporting described the jaw as broken, although the sources reviewed do not publish detailed imaging, surgical treatment or a definite recovery date. The loss is recorded separately as a fight result.
items.sourceLabel: MMA Fighting video and later interview

items.date: Oct. 2026 (gym listings vary; transfer date not verified)
items.label: Fight Club No1 and Raty Team listed training affiliations
items.detail: UFC's athlete profile lists Fight Club No1 in Moscow; Sherdog and other fighter registries currently list Raty Team, with Alexander Sidorin identified as a coach in recent records. Earlier UFC coverage documents temporary American Top Team and Thailand training. These directory entries alone do not establish a dated permanent camp switch or prove specific UFC 333 camp participants.

items.label: UFC 333 · scheduled vs. Abdul-Rakhman Yakhyaev
items.detail: Krylov enters the scheduled light-heavyweight fight against undefeated Abdul-Rakhman Yakhyaev at Etihad Arena, Abu Dhabi with a 31-12 professional record and 12-10 UFC record. UFC 333 prelims start at noon Eastern / 11 a.m. Central / 8 p.m. Abu Dhabi local time; no exact individual walkout time is available. The booking is not a completed bout as of the October 21 audit.

audit.scope: early karate/submission background and 2013 ADCC Ukraine claim; one recorded amateur bout; all 43 professional MMA bouts and finish times; original heavyweight-to-LHW UFC shift; 2013 GFC one-night title; 2017–2018 UFC exit and Fight Nights Global championship; 2020 Thailand/ATT camp, varying 2026 affiliations; illness-related 2023 Spann cancellation, 2024 Murzakanov cancellation, 2023–25 layoff; July 2026 jaw injury with recovery caveat; pending Yakhyaev UFC 333 bout

items.label: Works as a plumber and earns banking degree
items.detail: Before full-time MMA competition, Yakhyaev worked as a plumber and says he attended college and earned a banking degree. No school, diploma year or exact employment period is documented in his UFC questionnaire; these are background details without independently verified dates.

items.label: Combat sambo and MMA training foundation
items.detail: Yakhyaev has described an amateur background in combat sambo and MMA and says he earned Russian Master of Sports designations in both disciplines. His UFC questionnaire does not provide award dates, wrestling tournament names or detailed competition results, so those are not invented.

items.label: AMATEUR LOSS · Kazbek Cheldiev · decision
items.detail: At the Valeri Kokov Memorial 2019 amateur MMA tournament in Nalchik, Yakhyaev lost a three-round unanimous decision to Kazbek Cheldiev. This is the only publicly indexed amateur MMA result identified here, not evidence that it was his sole amateur fight. The loss is separate from his 10-0 professional record.

items.label: Reports NAGA European grappling championship
items.detail: Yakhyaev's UFC questionnaire lists a European NAGA championship as a grappling credential. It does not establish the event edition, division, weight or year, so the title is described as self-reported and is not counted among his MMA victories.

items.label: WIN · Elbek Ravshanov · professional debut, TKO R1
items.detail: Yakhyaev made his professional MMA debut against Elbek Ravshanov at ACA Young Eagles 22, winning by TKO (punches/ground strikes) at 3:00 of round one. This was his first professional win, not a UFC debut.

items.label: WIN · Nazhmudin Yusupov · triangle choke R2
items.detail: At ACA Young Eagles 27, Yakhyaev submitted Nazhmudin Yusupov by triangle choke at 3:09 of round two, his second professional victory. Some databases report 3:05; the Sherdog event page and athlete record list 3:09.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog official ACA Young Eagles 27 results

items.label: WIN · Mouhamadou Lamine · first-round TKO
items.detail: Yakhyaev defeated Mouhamadou Lamine (also spelled Mohamadou Lamine) at Khan Fight 1 in Turkey via first-round TKO (punches/ground strikes). Sherdog's fight record lists 0:24, whereas some secondary databases give 0:37. The exact finish time is disputed, so the conflicting values are noted rather than presented as a universally confirmed clock.

items.label: WIN · Nikolay Kovalenko · KhanFight light heavyweight title
items.detail: Yakhyaev beat Nikolay Kovalenko by unanimous decision after five full rounds at Khan Fight 2 in Bursa, Turkey, winning the vacant light heavyweight championship. This remains his only professional fight to go to a decision through October 2026 and his first recorded professional title victory.

items.label: KhanFight championship becomes his first professional MMA belt
items.detail: The five-round unanimous decision over Nikolay Kovalenko at Khan Fight 2 secured the vacant KhanFight light heavyweight title. It also demonstrated that he had completed a full five-round fight before reaching the UFC, an important contrast with his much shorter recent fights.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog official Khan Fight 2 title bout

items.label: Proposed Arash Mardani ONE Friday Fights bout does not occur
items.detail: Fight-registration sites list a canceled March 3, 2023 bout against Arash Mardani on ONE Friday Fights 7. No completed result is recorded, and the source does not establish why the booking fell through. The canceled bout does not affect his professional record.

items.label: WIN · Paulin Begai · captures ARES light heavyweight championship
items.detail: At ARES FC 23 in Aubervilliers, France, Yakhyaev submitted Paulin Begai with a guillotine choke at 1:32 of round one to win the ARES FC light heavyweight championship, his second professional regional title.

items.label: Claims ARES FC light heavyweight title
items.detail: Yakhyaev captured the ARES FC light heavyweight championship by guillotine submission over Paulin Begai. His professional win and exact 1:32 first-round clock are already recorded separately on this date.

items.label: WIN · Jacky Jeanne · ARES championship defense
items.detail: Yakhyaev defended his ARES FC light heavyweight title at ARES FC 25 in Paris, submitting Jacky Jeanne by rear-naked choke at 2:23 of round one. ARES confirms the result and clock time. This was his single recorded ARES title defense before entering Dana White's Contender Series.

items.label: Makes sole recorded successful ARES title defense
items.detail: The rear-naked choke over Jacky Jeanne retained Yakhyaev's ARES light heavyweight belt. This was his sixth professional victory, and he next fought on the Contender Series nearly eleven months later.

items.label: WIN · Alik Lorenz · DWCS TKO and UFC contract
items.detail: Yakhyaev stopped Alik Lorenz with a knee to the body followed by punches at 0:30 of round one on Dana White's Contender Series Season 9, Week 3, earning a UFC contract. It counts toward his overall professional record but is not one of his three UFC Octagon victories.

items.label: WIN · Raffael Cerqueira · actual UFC debut, RNC R1
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night: Tsarukyan vs. Hooker in Doha, Qatar, Yakhyaev submitted Raffael Cerqueira (occasionally misspelled 'Rafael') with a rear-naked choke just 0:33 into round one. This was his actual Octagon debut and first regular UFC victory.

items.label: MMA Nürnberg base, Fight Sports Deerfield Beach training blocks
items.detail: UFC reported Yakhyaev training with MMA Nürnberg in Germany and also working with JZ Cavalcante at Fight Sports Deerfield Beach in Florida. Training partners mentioned included Marc-André Barriault, Thad Jean and Rafael Tobias. This is a documented two-location training arrangement, not proof of a permanent switch between the gyms.

items.label: Chechen-born fighter representing Turkey
items.detail: UFC describes Yakhyaev as Chechen-born, while athlete databases variously list a Russian birthplace and Turkish sporting affiliation. The UFC interview says he regards both Chechnya and Turkey as homes. These distinctions concern birthplace, residence and representation, not a documented date of nationality change.

items.label: WIN · Brendson Ribeiro · rear-naked choke R1
items.detail: Yakhyaev submitted Brendson Ribeiro by rear-naked choke at 2:52 of round one at UFC Fight Night: Moicano vs. Duncan in Las Vegas. He absorbed eight significant strikes according to UFC's June 2026 report, compared with almost none in his preceding very short UFC/Contender Series fights.

items.label: WIN · Julius Walker · eight-second KO
items.detail: At UFC Baku, Yakhyaev countered Julius Walker with a right hand and followed with punches for an official KO at 0:08 of round one. Sherdog reported it as the second-fastest finish in UFC light heavyweight history at the time. It raised his record to 10-0 and 3-0 in regular UFC bouts, and he received a Performance of the Night bonus.

items.label: Performance of the Night bonus following UFC Baku knockout
items.detail: Yakhyaev received a Performance of the Night award for his 0:08 first-round KO of Julius Walker in Azerbaijan. The bonus was for a completed UFC bout, which appears as an individual fight entry.

items.date: Oct. 2026 (current listing, exact camp dates unreported)
items.label: MMA Nürnberg remains listed affiliation
items.detail: The UFC lists MMA Nürnberg as Yakhyaev's gym, while its June 2026 reporting confirms training sessions under JZ Cavalcante in Florida. No primary source establishes a new permanent home gym or an injury-driven camp change for UFC 333, so one is not invented.

items.label: Discusses Nikita Krylov matchup and willingness to fight longer
items.detail: In a UFC fight-week interview, Yakhyaev described his 3-0 UFC start, the plan to test himself against a much more experienced Krylov, and confidence in his conditioning despite little UFC cage time. He emphasized preparing multiple game plans and training for full rounds. Those are his own statements and do not establish how he will perform in a three-round fight.

items.label: UFC 333 · scheduled light heavyweight fight vs. Nikita Krylov
items.detail: Yakhyaev (10-0 overall, 3-0 in UFC Octagon fights) is scheduled against Nikita Krylov at Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi. UFC 333 prelims begin at noon US Eastern / 8:00 p.m. Abu Dhabi local time, but the individual fight's walkout time is not established. This is a scheduled bout, not a result as of the October 21 audit.

audit.scope: all ten professional fights 10-0 and 3-0 UFC, ACA 2021/22 early bouts with finish-clock discrepancies, KhanFight 2023 and ARES FC 2024 titles, documented 2019 amateur loss, NAGA/combat-sambo credentials with uncertainty, education and prior plumbing work, canceled 2023 ONE booking with no claimed cause, DWCS contract, complete 2025/26 UFC stoppages, June 2026 bonus, Germany and Florida gym affiliations, October 21 UFC fight-week interview and October 24 Krylov booking

items.label: Begins with wrestling and other martial arts in Russia
items.detail: Magomedov has described starting wrestling as a child before later building his kickboxing, Muay Thai and boxing skills. His UFC questionnaire says he trained in martial arts throughout childhood but does not give an exact start age or first gym.

items.label: Moves from Russia to Germany
items.detail: Born in Argun, Chechnya, in 1990, Magomedov moved to Germany with his family during his teenage years and ultimately developed most of his professional MMA career there. The precise move year is not documented in the UFC interview.
items.sourceLabel: UFC interview ahead of Sean Strickland fight

items.label: Develops through Germany's regional MMA circuit
items.detail: Magomedov's early professional fights took place across Germany from 2010 onward. His later base became UFD Gym in Düsseldorf, but the exact date he joined UFD is not verified. No early-career move to a particular German gym is assigned without evidence.

items.label: WIN · Nicola di Loreto · Submission (guillotine choke) · R1
items.detail: At Outsider Cup: Cage Fight Night 6, Magomedov defeated Nicola di Loreto by submission (guillotine choke) in round 1 at 0:30. This was his first recorded professional MMA fight, at welterweight, and he won at age 19.

items.label: WIN · Sjobbe Clymans · TKO (punches) · R1
items.detail: At Outsider Cup: Cage Fight Night 7, Magomedov defeated Sjobbe Clymans by tko (punches) in round 1 at 1:57. Some records show the stoppage at 0:38, while Sherdog/Fight Atlas lists 1:57. The exact clock is disputed, and 1:57 reflects the Sherdog-sourced table.

items.label: WIN · Fahd Jahri · Decision (unanimous)
items.detail: At Kiru: In the Spirit of the Knights, Magomedov defeated Fahd Jahri by decision (unanimous) after 2 rounds.

items.label: WIN · Igor Montes · Decision (unanimous)
items.detail: At Tempel Fight School: Mix Fight Gala XI, Magomedov defeated Igor Montes by decision (unanimous) after 2 rounds.

items.label: WIN · Bjorn Corsis · TKO (doctor stoppage) · R2
items.detail: At Superior FC 6, Magomedov defeated Bjorn Corsis by tko (doctor stoppage) in round 2 at 1:28.

items.label: WIN · Gocha Smoyan · TKO (doctor stoppage) · R2
items.detail: At Superior FC 7, Magomedov defeated Gocha Smoyan by tko (doctor stoppage) in round 2 at 0:15.

items.label: WIN · David Rosmon · Decision (unanimous)
items.detail: At European MMA 1, Magomedov defeated David Rosmon by decision (unanimous) after 3 rounds.

items.label: WIN · Jessin Ayari · TKO (punches) · R1
items.detail: At German MMA Championship 3, Magomedov defeated Jessin Ayari by tko (punches) in round 1 at 1:49. The first-round finish won the vacant German MMA Championship (GMC) welterweight title. Ayari later reached the UFC.

items.label: Wins German MMA Championship welterweight belt
items.detail: Magomedov captured the vacant GMC welterweight title by stopping Jessin Ayari in the first round at GMC 3. He subsequently lost a GMC title fight to Rafal Moks in July 2013; both individual fights appear elsewhere on this timeline.

items.label: LOSS · Andreas Stahl · Submission (rear-naked choke) · R2
items.detail: At Heroes Fighting Championship, Magomedov lost to Andreas Stahl by submission (rear-naked choke) in round 2 (exact stoppage time unavailable). This was his first professional loss; Stahl submitted him with a rear-naked choke. Other databases omit the finish clock, so no time is asserted.

items.label: WIN · Andreas Birgels · TKO (punches) · R1
items.detail: At Superior FC 13, Magomedov defeated Andreas Birgels by tko (punches) in round 1 at 4:44. Magomedov won the Superior FC welterweight championship. The promotion's archived event report confirms the 4:44 first-round stoppage.

items.label: Wins Superior FC welterweight championship
items.detail: Superior FC records his TKO over Andreas Birgels at 4:44 of round one on June 1, 2013, and the UFC credits him with the 2013 Superior FC welterweight title. This is a separate regional championship from the GMC title.

items.label: LOSS · Rafal Moks · Submission (guillotine choke) · R1
items.detail: At German MMA Championship 4, Magomedov lost to Rafal Moks by submission (guillotine choke) in round 1 at 2:53. Moks submitted Magomedov with a guillotine in a GMC welterweight title fight, ending his initial German MMA Championship reign.

items.label: WIN · Rafal Blachuta · Decision (unanimous)
items.detail: At German MMA Championship 5, Magomedov defeated Rafal Blachuta by decision (unanimous) after 3 rounds. Fight listings disagree on whether this unanimous decision was scheduled for three or five rounds. Sherdog/Fight Atlas reports three and a 5:00 final-round clock; the result itself is not disputed.

items.label: WIN · Donovan Panayiotis · TKO (punches) · R1
items.detail: At German MMA Championship 6, Magomedov defeated Donovan Panayiotis by tko (punches) in round 1 at 0:56.

items.label: WIN · Josip Artukovic · TKO (kick to body and punches) · R1
items.detail: At Tempel Fight School: Mix Fight Gala 18, Magomedov defeated Josip Artukovic by tko (kick to body and punches) in round 1 at 1:10.

items.label: WIN · Manuel Garcia · TKO (punches and knee) · R1
items.detail: At Merseburger Fight Night 8, Magomedov defeated Manuel Garcia by tko (punches and knee) in round 1 at 0:40.

items.label: LOSS · Mikkel Parlo · Decision (unanimous)
items.detail: At German MMA Championship 7, Magomedov lost to Mikkel Parlo by decision (unanimous) after 3 rounds. He lost a three-round unanimous decision to the former Bellator middleweight contender, his third professional defeat and last before a six-fight winning streak heading into PFL.

items.label: WIN · Raymond Jarman · TKO (punches) · R1
items.detail: At Superior FC 14, Magomedov defeated Raymond Jarman by tko (punches) in round 1 (exact stoppage time unavailable). Sherdog's event result shows 0:00 as a missing finish time. A genuine clock time cannot be confirmed, so it is omitted.

items.label: WIN · Ivica Truscek · Submission (rear-naked choke) · R2
items.detail: At Final Fight Championship 26, Magomedov defeated Ivica Truscek by submission (rear-naked choke) in round 2 at 4:50.

items.label: WIN · Mathias Schuck · TKO (punch and elbow) · R1
items.detail: At Superior FC 15, Magomedov defeated Mathias Schuck by tko (punch and elbow) in round 1 at 0:53.

items.label: UFD Gym Düsseldorf and striking coach Ivan Hippolyte
items.detail: Magomedov established a long-term home at UFD Gym in Düsseldorf. UFC's 2022 coverage identifies Ivan Hippolyte as an important coach. Magomedov has also described working on boxing with Sükrü Aksu and training alongside Agit Kabayel. Those relationships should not be conflated with a documented transfer date.

items.label: WIN · Aires Benrois · Submission (guillotine choke) · R2
items.detail: At Superior FC 16, Magomedov defeated Aires Benrois by submission (guillotine choke) in round 2 at 2:51.

items.label: WIN · Sergio Souza · Submission (guillotine choke) · R1
items.detail: At Final Fight Championship 29, Magomedov defeated Sergio Souza by submission (guillotine choke) in round 1 at 1:20.

items.label: WIN · Dan Hope · TKO (punches) · R1
items.detail: At Superior FC 18, Magomedov defeated Dan Hope by tko (punches) in round 1 at 2:15. The first-round TKO earned Magomedov Superior FC's middleweight championship, four years after his welterweight title in the same promotion.

items.label: Superior FC middleweight champion before PFL
items.detail: The win over Dan Hope at Superior FC 18 gave Magomedov a middleweight championship in the same promotion where he had held a welterweight title in 2013. The bout itself is recorded separately in his 29-7-1 professional record.

items.label: WIN · Danillo Villefort · TKO (body front kick and punches) · R1
items.detail: At PFL 3, Magomedov defeated Danillo Villefort by tko (body front kick and punches) in round 1 at 3:37. His first PFL regular-season bout ended with a front kick to the body followed by punches, one of two early PFL stoppages in 2018.

items.label: WIN · Anderson Goncalves · KO (punches) · R1
items.detail: At PFL 6, Magomedov defeated Anderson Goncalves by ko (punches) in round 1 at 1:27. His second regular-season knockout secured a leading playoff seed in the 2018 PFL middleweight tournament.

items.label: DRAW · Gasan Umalatov · Draw (majority)
items.detail: At PFL 10: middleweight quarterfinal, Magomedov fought to a draw with Gasan Umalatov by draw (majority) after 2 rounds. The quarterfinal ended in a majority draw (20-18, 19-19, 19-19). Magomedov nevertheless advanced under PFL's first-round tiebreaker. It is a professional draw, not a win or no contest.

items.label: WIN · Sadibou Sy · Decision (unanimous)
items.detail: At PFL 10: middleweight semifinal, Magomedov defeated Sadibou Sy by decision (unanimous) after 3 rounds. Magomedov fought twice on the October 20 PFL playoff card and advanced to the final by unanimous decision over Sy after three rounds.

items.label: Two PFL playoff fights on one night, including a draw
items.detail: Magomedov fought Gasan Umalatov and Sadibou Sy on October 20. He advanced from the quarterfinal despite a majority draw with Umalatov using the PFL first-round tiebreaker, then beat Sy by unanimous decision to reach the middleweight championship final. The draw counts separately in the career record.

items.label: LOSS · Louis Taylor · KO (punch) · R1
items.detail: At PFL 2018 Championship, Magomedov lost to Louis Taylor by ko (punch) in round 1 at 0:33. Taylor knocked him out with a single punch 33 seconds into the PFL middleweight championship final, earning the inaugural 2018 PFL title and million-dollar purse. Magomedov finished runner-up.

items.label: Runner-up in inaugural PFL middleweight season
items.detail: Louis Taylor knocked Magomedov out in 33 seconds in the championship final. Magomedov was the 2018 PFL middleweight runner-up, not the tournament champion. This was the end of his 2018 PFL run.

items.label: WIN · Slavisa Simeunovic · Submission (kimura) · R1
items.detail: At Elite MMA Championship 3, Magomedov defeated Slavisa Simeunovic by submission (kimura) in round 1 at 0:47. A first-round kimura in Düsseldorf was his first completed MMA fight after losing the December 2018 PFL title final.

items.label: WIN · Cezariusz Kesik · Technical submission (guillotine choke) · R2
items.detail: At KSW 57, Magomedov defeated Cezariusz Kesik by technical submission (guillotine choke) in round 2 at 1:53. He won in KSW by a technical guillotine submission. KSW/Tapology report the time around 1:52 to 1:53 of round two; this entry uses the Sherdog/Fight Atlas time of 1:53. It was his last completed professional fight before a series of canceled UFC bookings.

items.label: Approximately 21 months between completed professional fights
items.detail: After the December 19, 2020 win against Cezariusz Kesik, Magomedov did not complete another professional bout until September 3, 2022. Several planned UFC debuts fell through. The gap cannot all be attributed to a specific injury or illness from available evidence.

items.label: Gerald Meerschaert UFC matchup does not happen
items.detail: A UFC booking against Gerald Meerschaert for December 18, 2021 fell through. The fight was not completed, and an independently confirmed medical cause for Magomedov's withdrawal is not established here.

items.label: Makhmud Muradov withdrawal leads to Dustin Stoltzfus debut
items.detail: Magomedov was originally booked against Makhmud Muradov for UFC Paris on September 3; Muradov withdrew and Dustin Stoltzfus became the replacement opponent. The replacement produced Magomedov's first actual UFC appearance, not a fourth canceled event.

items.label: Visa issue cancels Aliaskhab Khizriev bout
items.detail: The UFC announced that visa issues forced Magomedov off a scheduled March 26 matchup with Aliaskhab Khizriev in Columbus, Ohio. Denis Tiuliulin replaced Magomedov. This was a confirmed visa problem, not an MMA defeat, missed weight or doping sanction.

items.label: WIN · Dustin Stoltzfus · TKO (front kick and punches) · R1
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night: Gane vs. Tuivasa, Magomedov defeated Dustin Stoltzfus by tko (front kick and punches) in round 1 at 0:19. The 19-second front-kick-led stoppage in Paris was his actual UFC debut and earned him a Performance of the Night bonus. The previous three UFC fight dates had fallen through.

items.label: LOSS · Sean Strickland · TKO (punches) · R2
items.detail: At UFC on ESPN 48, Magomedov lost to Sean Strickland by tko (punches) in round 2 at 4:20. In only his second UFC appearance, he took a five-round main event against Strickland. He started aggressively but fatigued in the second round and was stopped at 4:20. Strickland later won the UFC middleweight championship.

items.label: First UFC main event arrives in second Octagon appearance
items.detail: After a 19-second UFC debut, Magomedov was booked to headline a five-round fight against Sean Strickland on July 1, 2023. The fight ended in a second-round TKO loss. The event was a large jump in prominence for a UFC newcomer despite extensive regional and PFL experience.

items.label: LOSS · Caio Borralho · Decision (unanimous)
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night: Almeida vs. Lewis, Magomedov lost to Caio Borralho by decision (unanimous) after 3 rounds. He lost a unanimous decision in São Paulo. It was his second consecutive UFC defeat after the Strickland main event.

items.label: Trains at American Top Team in Miami to change camp preparation
items.detail: Following defeats against Strickland and Borralho, Magomedov told Eurosport he traveled to American Top Team in Miami to get more high-level sparring and broaden his preparation for Warlley Alves. He continued describing Sükrü Aksu and his German team as significant past/current coaches, so this is a documented training block, not proof of a permanent split from UFD.

items.label: WIN · Warlley Alves · Decision (unanimous)
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night: Barboza vs. Murphy, Magomedov defeated Warlley Alves by decision (unanimous) after 3 rounds. This unanimous decision ended his two-fight UFC losing streak. Magomedov said he used American Top Team in Florida for this camp and emphasized his original wrestling background.

items.label: WIN · Brunno Ferreira · Submission (arm-triangle choke) · R3
items.detail: At UFC 308, Magomedov defeated Brunno Ferreira by submission (arm-triangle choke) in round 3 at 3:14. His third-round arm-triangle submission in Abu Dhabi was his second consecutive UFC win following the Strickland and Borralho defeats.

items.label: Explains coaching and conditioning changes after UFC setbacks
items.detail: Following his submission of Brunno Ferreira, Magomedov told German outlet tz that he had expanded his coaching team and used a nutritionist and strength-and-conditioning coach. He described doing more camps overseas and improving wrestling and boxing preparation, rather than attributing the turnaround to one new technical skill.

items.label: WIN · Michel Pereira · Decision (unanimous)
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night: Garry vs. Prates, Magomedov defeated Michel Pereira by decision (unanimous) after 3 rounds. Magomedov defeated Pereira by unanimous decision after three rounds in Kansas City, making it three consecutive UFC victories.

items.label: LOSS · Joe Pyfer · Submission (face crank) · R2
items.detail: At UFC 320, Magomedov lost to Joe Pyfer by submission (face crank) in round 2 at 1:46. Pyfer submitted him in round two. UFC and Sherdog label the finish a face crank; some media databases call it a rear-naked choke, and this entry follows the official UFC/Sherdog classification.

items.label: WIN · Michal Oleksiejczuk · Submission (guillotine choke) · R1
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night: Fiziev vs. Torres, Magomedov defeated Michal Oleksiejczuk by submission (guillotine choke) in round 1 at 3:25. A first-round guillotine submission in Baku brought him to 29-7-1 overall and 5-3 in the UFC ahead of his next scheduled fight. UFC published separate post-fight interviews.

items.label: UFC Baku guillotine win and post-fight interview
items.detail: Magomedov defeated Michal Oleksiejczuk by first-round guillotine at 3:25 and spoke to UFC afterward in Baku. The result was his fifth UFC victory. The fight itself appears in a separate entry.

items.date: Oct. 2026 (directory affiliation, current camp details unconfirmed)
items.label: UFD Gym still listed; no confirmed permanent ATT move
items.detail: Sherdog, PFL and third-party gym directories continue to associate Magomedov with UFD Gym Düsseldorf. His 2024 American Top Team work is documented separately. No verified report identifies a permanent new head coach or sole training location for the October 2026 Rowston fight.

items.label: UFC 333 · scheduled middleweight bout vs. Cam Rowston
items.detail: Magomedov (29-7-1 professional, 5-3 UFC) is scheduled to fight Cam Rowston (also listed as Cameron Rowston) at UFC 333 at Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi. The event's early prelims start 10:00 a.m. Eastern, prelims at noon and main card at 2:00 p.m. Eastern; no confirmed individual walkout time or result is available as of the October 21 audit.

items.label: Amateur MMA ranking in Australasia
items.detail: Rowston says he completed his amateur career as the top-ranked middleweight in Australasia. Separate amateur databases list five bouts, four wins and one loss; the ranking is a fighter-reported credential without a verified ranking-publication date.

items.label: WKBF South Pacific middleweight kickboxing title
items.detail: Rowston reports holding the WKBF South Pacific middleweight championship and accumulating more than thirty kickboxing fights. UFC's athlete Q&A does not give the title date, full opponent list or sanctioning documentation; no specific knockout/decision record is inferred.

items.label: Begins martial arts training in Sydney
items.detail: Rowston says he started martial arts in 2013 just after turning 18. He described using regular training to gain confidence and reduce heavy drinking and partying. Early instruction was at Training Ground in Crows Nest, Sydney, before his later move to City Kickboxing in New Zealand.
items.sourceLabel: UFC athlete questionnaire and Apex MMA training account

items.label: Earns sport and exercise management bachelor's degree
items.detail: Rowston attended the University of Technology Sydney and says he earned a bachelor's degree in sport and exercise management. He also worked in pizza preparation, supermarket restocking, landscaping and later personal training and beginner MMA coaching. Neither graduation nor the dates of each job are specified in his UFC profile.

items.label: LOSS · Jacob Malkoun · Decision (unanimous)
items.detail: At BRACE 47, Rowston lost to Jacob Malkoun by decision (unanimous) after 3 five-minute rounds. Malkoun won by unanimous decision in the first loss of Rowston's professional career. They are both booked separately on UFC 333 in October 2026; a rematch between them is not scheduled.

items.detail: At BRACE 51, Rowston defeated Daniel Currie by tko (strikes) in round 1, at 0:38.

items.label: LOSS · Isi Fitikefu · TKO (strikes) · R1
items.detail: At Superfight MMA 8, Rowston lost to Isi Fitikefu by tko (strikes) in round 1, at 3:19. His first professional stoppage defeat came in round one; his only other two professional losses through October 2026 were decisions.

items.label: WIN · Martin Torres · Submission (rear-naked choke) / TKO disputed · R1
items.detail: At New Generation Cage MMA Series 3, Rowston defeated Martin Torres by a first-round finish with disputed method in round 1 (finish clock unavailable). Sherdog and FightMatrix classify this round-one win as a TKO with an unspecified 0:00 finish clock; Tapology, ESPN's secondary bout data and other registries call it a rear-naked-choke submission. The result is a win, but the recorded method conflicts. This entry explicitly preserves the discrepancy, and no clock time is asserted.

items.label: WIN · Leo Diaz · Submission (rear-naked choke) · R1
items.detail: At Superfight MMA 13, Rowston defeated Leo Diaz by submission (rear-naked choke) in round 1, at 1:06.

items.label: WIN · Jayden Eynaud · Submission (technique unspecified) · R2
items.detail: At New Generation Cage MMA Series 4, Rowston defeated Jayden Eynaud by submission (technique unspecified) in round 2 (finish clock unavailable). Databases list a round-two submission but not the choke or lock used, and the 0:00 value is missing data rather than a confirmed time.

items.label: WIN · Eli Taufuiaevalu · KO (method unspecified) · R2
items.detail: At Shuriken Fight Series 8, Rowston defeated Eli Taufuiaevalu by ko (method unspecified) in round 2 (finish clock unavailable). The recorded KO was in round two. Sherdog does not publish a reliable stoppage clock, so no specific time is claimed.

items.label: Relocates to City Kickboxing in Auckland
items.detail: Rowston originally trained at Training Ground in Sydney and later relocated to City Kickboxing in Auckland, working within Eugene Bareman's team. A February 2022 interview already describes him living and training in New Zealand. No exact month of the permanent move was verified.

items.label: Third place in ADCC NZ Open under-100 kg division
items.detail: The ADCC New Zealand Open 2021 official results list Rowston representing Atos Auckland in third place in the men's professional under-100 kg bracket. His separate UFC questionnaire claims an ADCC New Zealand absolute championship, but the exact date of that absolute title is not established and must not be conflated with this bronze result.

items.label: Brazilian jiu-jitsu brown belt and absolute championship reported
items.detail: In his UFC athlete questionnaire Rowston lists a BJJ brown belt and an ADCC New Zealand absolute-title win. The sources reviewed do not establish the dates or draw for that title and belt advancement, and they do not prove that the 2021 under-100 kg third-place result was the absolute championship.

items.label: Wins King in the Ring 86 kg kickboxing tournament
items.detail: Rowston won the eight-man King in the Ring 86 kg tournament in Auckland on February 12, defeating three opponents in one night, including Robert Ngari-Dean in the final. These were kickboxing bouts and are not part of his professional MMA record.
items.sourceLabel: King in the Ring 86V tournament bracket

items.label: MUAY THAI WIN · Connor Woodman · unanimous decision
items.detail: Tapology records a unanimous-decision win over Connor Woodman under Muay Thai rules at Shuriken Fight Series 10. This is separate from his subsequent September 2022 professional MMA submission of Pane Haraki and should not increase his MMA win total.

items.label: Nearly 23 months between completed professional MMA bouts
items.detail: Rowston did not complete a professional MMA fight between the September 23, 2022 win over Pane Haraki and the August 20, 2024 loss to Torrez Finney. The interval included kickboxing activity and canceled MMA bookings, so it should not automatically be attributed to inactivity, a prolonged injury or a suspension.

items.label: WIN · Pane Haraki · Submission (rear-naked choke) · R3
items.detail: At Shuriken Fight Series 12, Rowston defeated Pane Haraki by submission (rear-naked choke) in round 3, at 1:13. This five-round-scheduled fight was contested for the Shuriken Fight Series light heavyweight championship at 205 lb and ended in a third-round choke submission. It was Rowston's last completed professional MMA bout before August 2024.

items.label: Wins Shuriken Fight Series 205 lb MMA championship
items.detail: The Pane Haraki fight at Shuriken Fight Series 12 was scheduled for five rounds at light heavyweight and advertised as the promotion's 205 lb championship. Rowston secured the win by rear-naked choke at 1:13 of round three; the fight result is recorded separately.

items.date: By May 2023 (exact title night not firmly verified)
items.label: Wins second King in the Ring tournament at 92 kg
items.detail: His UFC questionnaire reports winning King in the Ring tournaments at 86 kg and 92 kg. A May 2023 King in the Ring promotional post called Rowston the current cruiserweight champion, establishing the 92 kg achievement by that point, although the exact tournament date and full bracket were not verified. This was kickboxing, not a professional MMA bout.
items.sourceLabel: King in the Ring promotion, May 2023 mention

items.label: Initial 2023 DWCS booking vs. Chad Hanekom fails
items.detail: Fight databases list a planned Contender Series matchup with Chad Hanekom on September 5, 2023 that was canceled. Tapology identifies Rowston as withdrawing, but no independently confirmed medical reason is available. His first completed DWCS appearance came in August 2024.

items.label: Withdraws from scheduled James Craughwell matchup
items.detail: A Shuriken Fight Series 17 fight against James Craughwell on April 20, 2024 was canceled; Tapology lists Rowston's withdrawal, but does not substantiate a specific injury or illness. The fight was not part of his 15-3 professional record.

items.label: LOSS · Torrez Finney · Decision (unanimous)
items.detail: At Dana White's Contender Series, Season 8 Week 2, Rowston lost to Torrez Finney by decision (unanimous) after 3 five-minute rounds. Rowston lost all three rounds on the scorecards in his first Contender Series appearance and did not receive a UFC contract. His record fell to 8-3.

items.label: First completed DWCS chance ends in loss to Torrez Finney
items.detail: Finney defeated Rowston by unanimous decision over three rounds on Contender Series Season 8, Week 2. Rowston went home without a contract and fought three times regionally over the following six months before another invitation.

items.label: WIN · Apaer Aerdake · Submission (calf slicer) · R2
items.detail: At Stealth Fighters League 1, Rowston defeated Apaer Aerdake by submission (calf slicer) in round 2, at 2:59. The second-round calf slicer secured the vacant Stealth Fighters League 190 lb catchweight championship. It was the first of three regional victories between Rowston's 2024 and 2025 Contender Series appearances.

items.label: Wins vacant SFL 190 lb catchweight title
items.detail: Rowston submitted Apaer Aerdake with a calf slicer at 2:59 of round two at SFL 1 in Auckland. The five-round-scheduled bout was for a vacant 190 lb catchweight title. The championship is distinct from an undisputed 185 lb middleweight belt.

items.label: WIN · Blair Bretag · Submission (rear-naked choke) · R2
items.detail: At Eternal MMA 91, Rowston defeated Blair Bretag by submission (rear-naked choke) in round 2, at 3:54. This rear-naked choke was his second consecutive victory after the Torrez Finney defeat.

items.label: Training alongside Hooker and Ulberg; Adesanya later leaves team
items.detail: Rowston has spoken about training around Dan Hooker, Carlos Ulberg and other experienced UFC fighters at City Kickboxing under Eugene Bareman. Israel Adesanya was part of the environment during earlier camps but publicly left City Kickboxing in July 2026; he should not be listed as a current CKB training partner in October 2026 without new evidence.

items.label: WIN · Alfred Stoddart · Decision (unanimous)
items.detail: At Eternal MMA 92, Rowston defeated Alfred Stoddart by decision (unanimous) after 3 five-minute rounds. He won a three-round unanimous decision at Eternal MMA 92 in Sydney, completing his three-fight regional rebound.

items.label: WIN · Brandon Holmes · TKO (elbow and punches) · R1
items.detail: At Dana White's Contender Series, Season 9 Week 2, Rowston defeated Brandon Holmes by tko (elbow and punches) in round 1, at 2:58. Rowston stopped Holmes with punches and elbows in round one, earning a UFC contract on his second completed DWCS appearance. Original opponent Jon Kunneman had withdrawn with a rib injury.

items.label: Earns UFC contract on second completed Contender Series appearance
items.detail: Rowston finished Brandon Holmes in 2:58 of round one and received a UFC contract. He requested the September UFC Perth card in his post-fight comments and was added to the event.
items.sourceLabel: UFC athlete results and Perth feature

items.label: Jon Kunneman withdraws with rib injury; Brandon Holmes replaces him
items.detail: Rowston had been scheduled to fight Jon Kunneman on August 19, 2025, but Kunneman withdrew because of a rib injury. Brandon Holmes replaced him. The injury belonged to Kunneman, not Rowston, and the canceled bout is not an MMA result.

items.label: WIN · Andre Petroski · TKO (punches) · R1
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night: Ulberg vs. Reyes, Rowston defeated Andre Petroski by tko (punches) in round 1, at 2:41. This was Rowston's actual UFC debut, in Perth. He entered as a betting underdog and scored a first-round TKO at 2:41. His UFC record became 1-0.

items.label: UFC debut in Perth follows six-week turnaround
items.detail: Rowston made his UFC debut against Andre Petroski just 39 days after the Contender Series victory. He won by first-round TKO at 2:41, as part of UFC Perth, and trained with his City Kickboxing team.

items.label: WIN · Cody Brundage · TKO (punches) · R2
items.detail: At UFC 325, Rowston defeated Cody Brundage by tko (punches) in round 2, at 4:08. Rowston stopped Brundage with punches from back mount at 4:08 of round two in Sydney, moving to 2-0 in UFC competition.

items.label: WIN · Robert Bryczek · Decision (unanimous)
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night: Della Maddalena vs. Prates, Rowston defeated Robert Bryczek by decision (unanimous) after 3 five-minute rounds. The three-round unanimous decision in Perth took Rowston to 15-3 as a professional and 3-0 in the UFC; it was his first UFC fight to go the distance.

items.label: UFC 333 fight-week interview on continued development
items.detail: UFC published a fight-week interview titled 'Each Fight I Feel Better And Better' on October 20 ahead of Rowston's Abus Magomedov bout. It is an interview appearance, not an independent confirmation of a new gym, injury, or result.

items.label: UFC 333 · scheduled middleweight fight vs. Abus Magomedov
items.detail: Rowston (15-3 professional MMA, 3-0 UFC) is booked to face Abus Magomedov (29-7-1, 5-3 UFC) at Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi on UFC 333's preliminary card. The prelims begin at noon US Eastern / 11 a.m. Central / 8 p.m. in Abu Dhabi, but an individual bout walkout time is not confirmed. No result is recorded as of October 21.
