items.detail: At Victory FC 45, Dawson defeated James Smith by submission (rear-naked choke) at 2:30 of round 1.

items.label: WIN · Chris McDaniel · Submission (rear-naked choke) · R1
items.detail: At RTP/ShoFight Branson Brawl, Dawson defeated Chris McDaniel by submission (rear-naked choke) at 4:07 of round 1.

items.label: WIN · Danny Tims · Submission (rear-naked choke) · R1
items.detail: At KCFA 15, Dawson defeated Danny Tims by submission (rear-naked choke) at 4:15 of round 1. This was the first of two separate victories Dawson recorded at the same KCFA 15 event on August 15, 2015.

items.label: WIN · Andrew Carrillo · Submission (rear-naked choke) · R1
items.detail: At KCFA 15, Dawson defeated Andrew Carrillo by submission (rear-naked choke) at 3:21 of round 1. Dawson won a second fight on the same KCFA 15 card. Each was a first-round rear-naked-choke finish, and both count separately in his professional record.

items.label: WIN · Bryce Logan · TKO (punches) · R2
items.detail: At Victory FC 47, Dawson defeated Bryce Logan by tko (punches) at 3:12 of round 2. This was Dawson's first recorded professional TKO win, after nine straight professional submission victories.

items.label: WIN · Robert Washington · TKO (punches) · R2
items.detail: At Titan FC 37, Dawson defeated Robert Washington by tko (punches) at 2:08 of round 2.

items.label: LOSS · Hugh Pulley · TKO (elbows) · R1
items.detail: At KCFA 18, Dawson lost to Hugh Pulley by tko (elbows) at 0:35 of round 1. Dawson suffered his first professional defeat when Pulley stopped him with elbows 35 seconds into round one at lightweight. He entered the fight 9-0.

items.label: WIN · Christian Camp · TKO (elbows and punches) · R2
items.detail: At Victory FC 52, Dawson defeated Christian Camp by tko (elbows and punches) at 1:43 of round 2.

items.label: WIN · Mike Plazola · Submission (triangle choke) · R1
items.detail: At KCFA 20, Dawson defeated Mike Plazola by submission (triangle choke) at 3:49 of round 1. Dawson won by triangle choke at featherweight, improving to 11-1 ahead of his Contender Series invitation. UFC credits him with a KCFA 145-pound pro title, but the precise title-winning bout has not been established by the archived event listing.

items.date: By Aug. 2017 (exact title fight not established)
items.label: KCFA featherweight professional championship
items.detail: UFC lists a Kansas City Fighting Alliance 145-pound professional title among Dawson's achievements. His 2016 KCFA win over Mike Plazola and a canceled February 2017 featherweight title booking with Chuka Willis are documented, but available primary results do not conclusively identify which fight earned the belt. No exact championship date is invented.
items.sourceLabel: UFC fighter Q&A and Tapology title booking

items.label: WIN · Adrian Diaz · Submission (rear-naked choke) · R2
items.detail: At Dana White's Tuesday Night Contender Series Season 1, Episode 6, Dawson defeated Adrian Diaz by submission (rear-naked choke) at 1:15 of round 2. The second-round submission secured a UFC contract during the first season of Contender Series. This is part of Dawson's overall professional record but is not a regular UFC Octagon appearance.

items.label: Receives UFC contract after Adrian Diaz submission
items.detail: Dawson's rear-naked choke of Adrian Diaz in Season 1 Week 6 of Dana White's Tuesday Night Contender Series earned him a UFC contract. It was his 12th professional MMA victory, while his UFC Octagon record remained 0-0 until March 2019.

items.label: Out-of-competition sample later triggers USADA investigation
items.detail: A sample collected October 18 returned an adverse analytical finding involving the M3 long-term metabolite of DHCMT (oral Turinabol). The sample triggered an anti-doping investigation, not an adjudicated doping violation or completed sanction.

items.label: UFC acknowledges potential anti-doping violation
items.detail: USADA informed Dawson and UFC of the potential violation stemming from the October sample. Dawson was provisionally suspended and was released from UFC days later before making a promotional debut. The adverse finding was subsequently dismissed, so it is incorrect to say he was definitively found guilty or served a final sanction.
items.sourceLabel: UFC original announcement / MMA Fighting investigation

items.label: Dawson pursues anti-doping arbitration after a year of uncertainty
items.detail: Dawson and USADA proceeded toward arbitration on Nov. 3, 2018 while scientific understanding of the persistent M3 metabolite was changing. He chose not to compete elsewhere during the case. No final guilty finding or suspension term was imposed.

items.label: USADA dismisses potential anti-doping violation
items.detail: UFC announced USADA had dismissed the case. USADA concluded it could not show the prohibited substance was ingested after Dawson entered the UFC testing program, given uncertainty over the duration of M3 metabolite detection. This was a dismissed potential violation, not a completed anti-doping ban. Later pre-debut tests in February/March 2019 returned negative.

items.label: WIN · Julian Erosa · Decision (unanimous)
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night: Lewis vs. dos Santos, Dawson defeated Julian Erosa by decision (unanimous) after 3 rounds. This was his first completed UFC Octagon bout, after a long delay stemming from a previously dismissed anti-doping allegation. The fight ended in Dawson's first professional victory by decision.

items.label: Finally makes UFC debut after dismissed USADA case
items.detail: Dawson made his actual UFC debut against Julian Erosa at UFC Wichita, winning a three-round unanimous decision about nineteen months after his Contender Series contract. His debut delay was associated with the USADA investigation and subsequent reinstatement, not a two-year adjudicated doping suspension.
items.sourceLabel: UFC fighter fight history and MMA Fighting

items.label: WIN · Michael Trizano · Submission (rear-naked choke) · R2
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night: dos Anjos vs. Lee, Dawson defeated Michael Trizano by submission (rear-naked choke) at 2:27 of round 2. His rear-naked choke of the former Ultimate Fighter winner earned a Performance of the Night bonus.

items.label: First UFC performance bonus
items.detail: The rear-naked choke victory over Michael Trizano earned Dawson his first Performance of the Night award, in his second completed regular UFC appearance.

items.label: Two booked Chas Skelly fights fail to occur
items.detail: Dawson had bookings against Chas Skelly for Jan. 18 and Feb. 29, 2020. The first booking was pulled amid Nevada licensing/testing review; Skelly later withdrew from the February fight with a reported injury, and Darrick Minner replaced him. The cancellations were not completed professional bouts.

items.label: Misses featherweight limit by 3.5 pounds for Darrick Minner
items.detail: Dawson weighed 149.5 pounds, compared with the 146-pound non-title featherweight limit, and forfeited 30% of his purse. Minner accepted the catchweight bout, and Dawson submitted him the next day. This was an actual UFC weight miss and is separate from later negotiated 150-pound catchweight participation.

items.label: WIN · Darrick Minner · Submission (rear-naked choke) · R2
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night: Benavidez vs. Figueiredo, Dawson defeated Darrick Minner by submission (rear-naked choke) at 1:38 of round 2. The bout proceeded despite Dawson weighing 149.5 pounds, 3.5 above the featherweight non-title limit; he forfeited 30% of his purse. The weigh-in incident is also a separate timeline entry.
items.sourceLabel: MMA Fighting UFC weigh-ins / Sherdog result

items.label: WIN · Nad Narimani · Decision (unanimous)
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night: Figueiredo vs. Benavidez 2 (Fight Island, local Jul. 19), Dawson defeated Nad Narimani by decision (unanimous) after 3 rounds. This fight was contested at a mutually agreed 150-pound catchweight on UFC Fight Island in Abu Dhabi, not a featherweight title bout and not a missed-weight incident. The UAE-local fight date was July 19, while the US UFC/Sherdog event date was July 18.

items.label: Planned 150-pound catchweight against Nad Narimani
items.detail: Dawson and Narimani both officially weighed 150 pounds for an agreed catchweight fight in Abu Dhabi. Their bout went three rounds, with Dawson winning by unanimous decision. This was not a missed-weight violation; the standard UFC featherweight-to-lightweight transition came afterward.

items.label: WIN · Leonardo Santos · KO (punches) · R3
items.detail: At UFC on ESPN: Brunson vs. Holland, Dawson defeated Leonardo Santos by ko (punches) at 4:59 of round 3. After returning to the standard lightweight division (155 pounds), Dawson knocked out Santos with ground strikes at 4:59 of round three, one second before the final horn. He received a Performance of the Night bonus.

items.label: Returns to standard lightweight division
items.detail: Dawson's fight against Leonardo Santos was contested at 155 pounds and marked his transition to the regular lightweight division. He began his UFC career with three featherweight wins and had also fought once at a 150-pound catchweight. Lightweight became his primary UFC division.

items.label: Performance of the Night for final-second Santos finish
items.detail: The KO of Leonardo Santos at 4:59 of round three earned another Performance of the Night award. It was also Dawson's first regular UFC win at 155 pounds after his featherweight and catchweight fights.

items.label: DRAW · Ricky Glenn · Draw (majority)
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night: Costa vs. Vettori, Dawson fought to a draw with Ricky Glenn by draw (majority) after 3 rounds. Dawson controlled the opening two rounds but Glenn rallied for two 10-8 scores in round three. Judges scored it 29-28, 28-28 and 28-28 for a majority draw, Dawson's only professional draw.

items.label: First professional draw against Ricky Glenn
items.detail: Dawson took the first two rounds through sustained grappling control, but Glenn dominated the final round and earned 10-8 scores from two judges. The majority-draw verdict was 29-28, 28-28, 28-28. It was not a loss and it did not end Dawson's undefeated start within the Octagon.

items.label: Leaves Glory MMA for American Top Team in Coconut Creek
items.detail: After a draw with Ricky Glenn, Dawson described feeling burned out at Glory MMA in Missouri, where he had also been coaching. He moved to American Top Team in Coconut Creek, Florida and spoke of learning from Mike Brown, Jorge Masvidal and Thiago Alves. This was a permanent team change, not a brief camp visit.

items.label: WIN · Jared Gordon · Submission (rear-naked choke) · R3
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night: Font vs. Vera, Dawson defeated Jared Gordon by submission (rear-naked choke) at 4:11 of round 3. This was Dawson's first completed bout after moving to American Top Team in Coconut Creek, Florida.

items.label: Misses lightweight limit by 1.5 pounds for Mark Madsen
items.detail: Dawson weighed 157.5 pounds, 1.5 over the non-title 156-pound lightweight limit. The Madsen bout proceeded at catchweight, and MMA Fighting reported a 30% purse penalty. Dawson won by rear-naked choke in round three on Nov. 5, with the exact finish clock listed differently by UFC and Sherdog.

items.label: WIN · Mark Madsen · Submission (rear-naked choke) · R3
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night: Rodriguez vs. Lemos, Dawson defeated Mark Madsen by submission (rear-naked choke) at 2:05 of round 3. Dawson weighed 157.5 pounds, 1.5 over the 156-pound non-title lightweight limit, and the fight proceeded with a 30% purse penalty. UFC lists the submission at 2:04 while Sherdog lists 2:05 in round three; the timeline follows Sherdog's 2:05 and notes the discrepancy.

items.label: BJJ black belt, strong grappling focus
items.detail: UFC's athlete questionnaire lists Dawson as a Brazilian jiu-jitsu black belt; earlier translated UFC entries had described him as a brown belt. The promotion date is not published in the accessible source. His wrestling-to-grappling approach became the defining feature of his career under Krause and at ATT.

items.label: WIN · Damir Ismagulov · Decision (unanimous)
items.detail: At UFC on ESPN: Strickland vs. Magomedov, Dawson defeated Damir Ismagulov by decision (unanimous) after 3 rounds. The unanimous decision against Ismagulov came during Dawson's undefeated stretch as an Octagon fighter before his Bobby Green defeat.

items.label: LOSS · Bobby (King) Green · KO (punches) · R1
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night: Dawson vs. Green, Dawson lost to Bobby (King) Green by ko (punches) at 0:33 of round 1. Dawson was knocked out in 33 seconds in his first UFC main event. It was his first professional loss since April 2016 and his first UFC defeat.

items.label: First UFC main event and first Octagon loss
items.detail: Dawson headlined UFC Fight Night 229 against Bobby Green in Las Vegas and was knocked out in 33 seconds. He came into the main event unbeaten across his first nine regular UFC fights (8 wins, one draw); his last preceding professional loss was to Hugh Pulley in 2016.

items.label: WIN · Joe Solecki · Decision (unanimous)
items.detail: At UFC 302, Dawson defeated Joe Solecki by decision (unanimous) after 3 rounds. This unanimous decision at UFC 302 was Dawson's first completed fight after the 33-second knockout loss to Green. Official judges scored it 29-28, 30-27 and 30-27 in his favor.

items.label: WIN · Rafa García · TKO (elbows and punches) · R2
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night: Royval vs. Taira, Dawson defeated Rafa García by tko (elbows and punches) at 1:42 of round 2. Dawson finished García with elbows and punches on the ground in round two, making it two consecutive wins since the Green loss.

items.label: WIN · Diego Ferreira · Decision (unanimous)
items.detail: At UFC 311, Dawson defeated Diego Ferreira by decision (unanimous) after 3 rounds. Dawson won a unanimous decision at UFC 311, with three 30-27 scorecards. The win extended his post-Green streak to three fights.

items.label: LOSS · Manuel Torres · TKO (punches) · R1
items.detail: At UFC 323, Dawson lost to Manuel Torres by tko (punches) at 2:25 of round 1. Torres hurt Dawson with an uppercut and finished him with follow-up strikes in the first round. This was Dawson's third professional defeat and second UFC knockout loss.

items.label: Second UFC knockout loss against Manuel Torres
items.detail: Manuel Torres stopped Dawson in round one at UFC 323. Dawson had won his previous three fights since the 2023 Bobby Green loss, and his record entering the subsequent Rębecki fight was 23-3-1.

items.label: WIN · Mateusz Rębecki · Submission (rear-naked choke) · R3
items.detail: At UFC 328, Dawson defeated Mateusz Rębecki by submission (rear-naked choke) at 4:42 of round 3. Dawson rebounded with a rear-naked choke at 4:42 of round three at UFC 328. He entered his October 2026 booking with a 24-3-1 professional record, 12-2-1 in regular UFC competition.

items.label: Submits Mateusz Rębecki to rebound from Torres loss
items.detail: Dawson submitted Rębecki with a rear-naked choke at 4:42 of round three at UFC 328, bringing him to 24-3-1 overall and 12-2-1 in regular UFC bouts. The result is also separately listed among the individual fights.

items.label: Discusses Nurullo Aliev matchup and becoming a father
items.detail: In a fight-week media interview published in October, Dawson discussed Aliev's willingness to wrestle, the need for a less aggressive opening, and the added financial responsibility of expecting his first child. These are his statements about preparation and family, not independently observed evidence of new conditioning or a camp move.

items.label: American Top Team remains his listed training base
items.detail: UFC and Sherdog both list Dawson with American Top Team in Coconut Creek, Florida. There is no credible documentation of a permanent 2026 departure from ATT or a new head coach specific to his Aliev fight, so no unsupported gym switch is asserted.
items.sourceLabel: UFC athlete profile and Sherdog affiliation

items.label: UFC 333 · scheduled lightweight bout vs. Nurullo Aliev
items.detail: Dawson (24-3-1 overall, 12-2-1 regular UFC) is scheduled to face undefeated Nurullo Aliev (12-0) at Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi. Preliminary coverage begins at noon Eastern / 11 a.m. Central / 8 p.m. local Abu Dhabi time. No specific cage-walk time or bout result has been announced as of Oct. 21.

audit.scope: 28 professional MMA bouts 24-3-1 (including one 2015 double-fight night and 2017 DWCS), 8 indexed amateur wins vs outdated UFC 5-0 summary, early KCFA featherweight title with acquisition date unresolved, 2017–2018 dismissed USADA M3/Turinabol investigation with no final sanction, two verified UFC weight misses, 2020 150 lb catchweight vs later 155 lb move, 2021 Ricky Glenn majority draw, Feb 2022 Glory-to-ATT move, all 15 regular UFC fight results with available finish times, 2026 Rębecki victory and Aliev UFC 333 booking

items.label: Older brothers introduce Aliev to wrestling
items.detail: Aliev grew up in Dushanbe, Tajikistan and says he began wrestling at around age 12 after his older brothers brought him to training. Because public fighter databases disagree on his birth date, a precise start year is not reliable.

items.label: Reports additional pankration and combat sambo honors
items.detail: UFC credits Aliev with two world pankration championships, two Asian pankration titles and an Asian combat sambo championship. Only the 2017 Sochi pankration result and his 2017 World Youth MMA title are dated separately here; the other honors are reported credentials rather than independently dated professional MMA belts.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Eshpolot Temirov · World Youth MMA selection
items.detail: Aliev beat Kyrgyz opponent Eshpolot Temirov at welterweight in Yaroslavl at the 2017 World Youth MMA championship selection stage. Sherdog does not record method, round or clock time; its zero-time placeholder is missing data, not a finish.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Jan Fajk · World Youth MMA selection
items.detail: Aliev defeated Jan Fajk from the Czech Republic in the same World Youth MMA tournament. Result confirmed; the event register does not specify a legitimate finish time or method. Amateur MMA, not a pro victory.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Alexey Trofimov · wins youth MMA world title
items.detail: Aliev defeated Alexey Trofimov from Russia in the World Youth MMA Championships final at welterweight, completing three recorded wins in the event. The official method and round clock are unavailable; these bouts form his 3-0 indexed amateur MMA record, separate from 12-0 as a professional.

items.label: Wins world pankration cadet title at 75 kg in Sochi
items.detail: United World Wrestling's official results list Aliev (Tajikistan) first in men's cadet (ages 16–17) pankration athlima at 75 kg at the Oct. 27–29, 2017 World Pankration Championships in Sochi. This is a dated youth-category title, not a senior MMA world championship. The UFC credits him with additional pankration and combat sambo honors, but their dates are not verified here.
items.sourceLabel: United World Wrestling official 2017 results, page 1

items.label: Early MMA development in Tajikistan
items.detail: Regional fighter biography describes Aliev training with Akhmat Tajikistan under Rajabali Baenov during his early professional years. The exact dates and exclusive coaching arrangements are not established, and subsequent international training blocks are documented separately.

items.label: WIN · Habib Habibov (Khabib Khabibuloev) · Unanimous decision
items.detail: Aliev made his recorded professional debut at Ismoili Somoni FC in Dushanbe, beating Habib Habibov by unanimous decision after two five-minute rounds (R2 5:00). Sherdog uses Habib Habibov, while Tapology and some other databases list the opponent as Khabib Khabibuloev; both listings refer to this same Feb. 3, 2018 matchup. Sherdog's event page marks it as a lightweight main-event title fight, but no additional title claim is inferred.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog original event card / first professional result

items.label: WIN · Sergey Malykov (Malikov) · Unanimous decision
items.detail: At Battle on the Volga 3, Aliev won a unanimous decision over Sergey Malykov (also spelled Malikov). Result recorded at the end of round three (R3 5:00), March 4, 2018. This was his second professional victory.

items.label: WIN · Rasul Mamedbekov · TKO (corner stoppage) · R2
items.detail: At Battle on the Volga 4, Aliev beat Rasul Mamedbekov by TKO due to a corner stoppage at the end of round two (R2 5:00). The clock indicates that the second round was completed before the corner stopped the fight, not that Aliev scored a knockout at the final bell. It was his first professional stoppage win and was part of his 2018 lightweight tournament run.

items.label: WIN · Makkasharip Zaynukov · Decision (majority)
items.detail: At Battle on the Volga 6, Aliev defeated Makkasharip Zaynukov by decision (majority) after 3 complete rounds (final round at 5:00). He won the Battle on the Volga lightweight grand prix final and was listed as the promotion's inaugural lightweight titleholder in historical title records. Some secondary sites mistakenly date this fight to 2028; the September 23, 2018 date is corroborated by Sherdog.
items.sourceLabel: Historic Battle on the Volga title history

items.label: Wins Battle on the Volga lightweight grand prix
items.detail: After beating Rasul Mamedbekov in May, Aliev defeated Makkasharip Zaynukov by majority decision (R3 5:00) on Sept. 23 to complete the Battle on the Volga lightweight grand prix. A historical title lineage lists him as that promotion's inaugural lightweight champion. This does not prove an additional, separately fought Gorilla Fighting or Eagle FC title bout.
items.sourceLabel: Battle on the Volga historical title lineage

items.label: Battle on the Volga 10 booking against Maksim Trunov canceled
items.detail: A proposed lightweight matchup with Maksim Trunov at Battle on the Volga 10 was canceled. No professional result or round time is recorded.

items.label: GFC 15 fight against Anvar Chergesov canceled
items.detail: A scheduled GFC 15 matchup with Anvar Chergesov did not take place. The same opponent would later be linked to a separate planned GFC 24 title fight in February 2020; these bookings should not be conflated.

items.label: WIN · Ramazan Amirov · Decision (unanimous)
items.detail: At GFC 16, Aliev defeated Ramazan Amirov by decision (unanimous) after 3 complete rounds (final round at 5:00). Aliev competed at welterweight (170 lb). This should not be mislabeled as a lightweight title bout.

items.label: GFC 23 fight against Kuat Khamitov canceled
items.detail: Aliev was listed opposite Kuat Khamitov at GFC 23, but the bout was canceled. It did not count toward his official record.

items.label: Proposed GFC title fight with Anvar Chergesov canceled
items.detail: Aliev was scheduled to meet Anvar Chergesov for a planned GFC lightweight championship at GFC 24 on Feb. 9, 2020. The bout did not occur; historical event listings show Gadzhi Rabadanov instead paired with Joao Paulo de Moura e Silva. It is a canceled opportunity, not a title-winning fight on Aliev's professional record.

items.label: GFC 28 bout with Abdurakhman Alimagomedov does not happen
items.detail: Aliev was listed to face Abdurakhman Alimagomedov at GFC 28, a memorial event scheduled for Sept. 9, 2020. The fight did not take place. A reliable contemporaneous confirmation of the exact cancellation reason has not been found, so no injury diagnosis is assigned to either fighter.

items.label: WIN · Alexander Grebnev · Decision (unanimous)
items.detail: At AMC Fight Nights Global: Winter Cup, Aliev defeated Alexander Grebnev by unanimous decision at welterweight, recorded at the end of round three (R3 5:00) on Dec. 24, 2020. An alternate database lists an impossible R1 3:07 time for a decision; Sherdog's three-round result is used.

items.label: Studies information technology in Tajikistan
items.detail: Aliev told the UFC he was attending university to study Information Technology. Neither a graduation date nor an awarded degree is established by the source; do not describe his enrollment as a completed degree.

items.label: WIN · Kirill Kryukov · Decision (unanimous)
items.detail: At the EFC/AMC Abdulmanap Nurmagomedov Memorial event, Aliev beat Kirill Kryukov by unanimous decision at welterweight, three completed rounds (R3 5:00). Sherdog records Sept. 17, 2021; some event listings use Sept. 18, likely due to event dates or time zones. This was his seventh pro win and was not a separately verified lightweight title defense.

items.date: By Sep. 2021 (title lineage; precise dates unverified)
items.label: Gorilla Fighting and Eagle FC championship claim clarified
items.detail: The UFC describes Aliev as a former Gorilla Fighting (later Eagle FC) lightweight champion. His documented 2018 Battle on the Volga tournament win supplies a concrete 155-pound title achievement, but his GFC 16 fight in 2019 and EFC/AMC fight in 2021 were both at welterweight. No separate lightweight title-winning bout in those promotions is established by the available fight records.

items.label: Trains at Tiger Muay Thai and Kill Cliff FC
items.detail: UFC reported Aliev had trained at Tiger Muay Thai in Thailand and then prepared for Contender Series at Kill Cliff FC in South Florida. These were documented training blocks; the article does not establish that he permanently moved his primary gym.

items.label: Reports BJJ blue belt despite zero MMA submission wins
items.detail: Aliev lists a Brazilian jiu-jitsu blue belt in his UFC questionnaire. The date of promotion is unknown. His professional record contains two TKO/KO victories, ten decisions and no submissions, despite his wrestling-heavy MMA style.

items.label: LFA fight with Thiago Oliveira canceled for DWCS invitation
items.detail: Aliev had an LFA 139 lightweight matchup with Thiago Oliveira scheduled for Aug. 19, 2022, but the fight was canceled before Aliev appeared on Contender Series on Sept. 20. The scheduling sequence is documented; the exact contractual reason for the canceled LFA bout is not confirmed.

items.label: WIN · Josh Wick · TKO (punches) · R1
items.detail: On Dana White's Contender Series Season 6, Week 9, Aliev defeated Josh Wick by ground punches at 4:36 of round one (R1 4:36), earning a UFC contract. This is an official professional MMA victory (his eighth) but is not counted among his four regular UFC Octagon victories through October 2026.

items.label: Wins UFC contract by finishing Josh Wick
items.detail: Aliev stopped Josh Wick at 4:36 of round one on Contender Series Season 6 Week 9. The professional win moved him to 8-0 and earned a UFC contract; he had not yet made his Octagon debut.

items.label: WIN · Rafael Alves · Decision (majority)
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night: Muniz vs. Allen, Aliev defeated Rafael Alves by decision (majority) after 3 complete rounds (final round at 5:00). Aliev won his UFC debut, 29-27, 29-27, 28-28, despite a one-point deduction by referee Mark Smith in round one for an alleged bite. Aliev denied biting intentionally; television replay did not conclusively show the act. The point deduction and majority-decision win are official.

items.label: First Tajikistan-born UFC victor; unusual point deduction
items.detail: Aliev defeated Rafael Alves on his actual UFC debut by majority decision after a point was deducted for a biting foul in round one. Aliev contested the interpretation of the hand-in-mouth exchange; the television replay was inconclusive. Official scorecards were 29-27, 29-27 and 28-28. This was not a doping case or post-fight disciplinary suspension.

items.label: Injured leg forces UFC 295 withdrawal
items.detail: On Nov. 3, eight days before UFC 295, Aliev publicly announced he was withdrawing from his Nov. 11 bout with Mateusz Rębecki because of a leg injury. Roosevelt Roberts took the replacement booking. A precise bone, ligament or muscle diagnosis is not confirmed publicly.

items.label: Leg surgery and rehabilitation
items.detail: After the leg injury that forced his November 2023 UFC 295 withdrawal, Aliev underwent surgery and a long rehabilitation. Following his January 2025 comeback, he said he resumed boxing work roughly six months after surgery. The precise surgery day, procedure and medical clearance date remain unreported; none is assumed.
items.sourceLabel: MMA Junkie post-fight interview (reproduced at Inkl)

items.label: Yanal Ashmouz out; Joe Solecki replaces him
items.detail: UFC announced on Jan. 6 that Yanal Ashmouz withdrew from his planned Jan. 11 lightweight matchup with Aliev due to injury. Joe Solecki replaced him on the card. The UFC notice did not disclose Ashmouz's specific injury.

items.label: WIN · Joe Solecki · Decision (unanimous)
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night: Dern vs. Ribas 2, Aliev returned from an almost 23-month absence and beat Joe Solecki by unanimous decision after three full rounds (R3 5:00). Official scores were 30-27, 29-28 and 29-28. Solecki replaced injured original opponent Yanal Ashmouz.

items.label: Returns after 22 months and 17 days without a fight
items.detail: The interval from Aliev's Feb. 25, 2023 UFC debut to his Jan. 11, 2025 return was 22 months and 17 days (686 days). The 2023 leg injury, subsequent surgery and recovery account for much of the inactivity. It is not linked to any documented anti-doping suspension.

items.label: Successful post-surgery return against Joe Solecki
items.detail: Aliev won a unanimous decision in Las Vegas, 30-27, 29-28, 29-28, almost two years after his previous appearance. He discussed drilling defensive grappling with his jiu-jitsu coach before the match.

items.label: WIN · Shaqueme (Shem) Rock · Decision (unanimous)
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night: Tsarukyan vs. Hooker in Qatar, Aliev beat debuting Shaqueme (Shem) Rock by unanimous decision after three rounds (R3 5:00). The UFC's published judges' scores were 30-27 on all three cards. Aliev reached 11-0 in professional MMA and 3-0 inside the regular UFC Octagon.

items.label: WIN · Mike Davis · Decision (unanimous)
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night: Ankalaev vs. Guskov in Abu Dhabi, Aliev defeated Mike Davis by unanimous decision after all three five-minute rounds (R3 5:00). All three official judges scored it 30-27. UFC Stats credits Aliev with eight takedowns and 12:25 of control time. He improved to 12-0 overall and 4-0 in regular UFC appearances.

items.label: Wins all three rounds against Mike Davis
items.detail: Aliev earned a 30-27, 30-27, 30-27 unanimous decision in Abu Dhabi behind extensive wrestling and top control. Davis later criticized the style and apologized for his remarks. The official outcome was unchanged.

items.label: Kaizen MMA / Kill Cliff FC affiliations
items.detail: Sherdog currently lists Aliev's team as Kaizen MMA / Kill Cliff FC. Separate gym listings name Nima Mazhari at Kaizen, but the available evidence does not establish that he is Aliev's current head coach or that Aliev permanently left his earlier Tajik, Thai and Florida training setups.

items.label: Fight-week interview ahead of Grant Dawson
items.detail: UFC published Aliev's 'Every Fight Is a New Level' interview during UFC 333 fight week. His 4-0 UFC record includes four decisions, and no reliable source confirms a new injury or transfer of primary gym for this fight.

items.label: UFC 333 · scheduled vs. Grant Dawson
items.detail: Aliev (12-0 professional MMA; 4-0 UFC) is scheduled to meet Grant Dawson at lightweight in the UFC 333 preliminary card at Etihad Arena, Abu Dhabi. The prelims begin at noon U.S. Eastern / 11 a.m. Central / 8 p.m. Abu Dhabi time, with no independently confirmed individual cage-walk time or fight result as of Oct. 21.

audit.scope: Re-audited all 12 dated pro bouts (2018–2026), 3 amateur wins, 2017 UWW Sochi cadet 75 kg title, regional cancellations, championship-lineage caveats, major UFC injury and recovery, 2023 biting deduction and official UFC scorecards through July 2026, verified UFC 333 booking; corrected first opponent name variations; all timeline items rearranged chronologically, undated events explicitly labeled.

items.label: Starts wrestling alongside his twin brother
items.detail: Born June 23, 1999, Thicknesse says his father put him and his twin brother into wrestling when they were six because they were constantly fighting at home. The year is calculated from his age, not an independently documented enrollment date.

items.label: Begins long-term training at Joe Lopez's Freestyle Fighting Gym
items.detail: Thicknesse grew up training at Freestyle Fighting Gym under Joe Lopez in the Wollongong/Windang area. In his UFC questionnaire he reported 12 years with Lopez. Exact beginning year cannot be fixed from this retrospective statement.

items.label: Starts coaching children's classes at Freestyle MMA
items.detail: Thicknesse says he began teaching the gym's kids classes at age 15. He also worked as a security guard before making MMA his full-time UFC career; the exact start and end dates of the security work are not published.

items.label: Becomes a regular Alexander Volkanovski training partner
items.detail: Thicknesse says he has been one of Volkanovski's principal training partners since he was 18. This describes an extended gym relationship under Joe Lopez, not a move to a new team. The starting year is approximate, inferred from Thicknesse's June 1999 birthdate.

items.label: WKBF bantamweight and national BJJ credentials
items.detail: The UFC lists a WKBF bantamweight championship and a national Brazilian jiu-jitsu title among Thicknesse's amateur combat-sports accomplishments. Exact tournament dates, opponents and bracket details have not been established; these are not professional MMA wins.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Thomas Riley · Rear-naked choke · R2 (time unavailable)
items.detail: At Superfight MMA 7, Thicknesse submitted Thomas Riley by rear-naked choke in round two. Sherdog does not supply a legitimate stoppage clock. This is an amateur result and is excluded from his professional 9-1 record.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Kristopher Ustijanovski · RNC · R1 2:22
items.detail: At Superfight MMA 8, Thicknesse submitted Kristopher Ustijanovski by rear-naked choke at 2:22 of round one. He later met and defeated the same opponent again in a separate amateur contest.

items.label: AMATEUR LOSS · Chris Soful Thorne · Unanimous decision · R3 3:00
items.detail: Thicknesse lost a three-round amateur unanimous decision to Chris Soful Thorne at Eternal MMA 42. The result is part of his reported 7-1 amateur record, not the one loss in his 9-1 professional record.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Semakadde Kakembo · Decision · R3 3:00
items.detail: At Wollongong Wars 7, Thicknesse beat Semakadde Kakembo by decision in an amateur bout lasting three three-minute rounds. They would meet again in the professional ranks in September 2022.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Kristopher Ustijanovski · RNC · R3 0:54
items.detail: At Superfight MMA 14, Thicknesse defeated Kristopher Ustijanovski again, submitting him by rear-naked choke at 0:54 of round three. This is a second, separately recorded amateur victory over Ustijanovski.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Ali Yaqoob · TKO · R3 1:54
items.detail: In the opening round of the IMMAF Oceania Open on the Gold Coast, Thicknesse defeated Ali Yaqoob of Bahrain by third-round TKO at 1:54 in the 65.8 kg (145 lb) featherweight bracket.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Abdul Mahdawi · Unanimous decision · R3 3:00
items.detail: Thicknesse beat fellow Australian Abdul Mahdawi by unanimous decision after three three-minute rounds to advance to the featherweight final at the 2020 IMMAF Oceania Open. Some secondary results use the first name Abzzy, but IMMAF identifies him as Abdul Mahdawi.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Dylan Thompson · Unanimous decision · R3 3:00
items.detail: Thicknesse beat Britain's Dylan Thompson by unanimous decision in the men's 65.8 kg featherweight final, completing a three-win tournament at the 2020 IMMAF Oceania Open.

items.label: Wins IMMAF Oceania Open amateur featherweight gold
items.detail: The IMMAF federation lists Thicknesse as the 2020 Oceania Open featherweight gold medalist. He won on three consecutive days against Ali Yaqoob, Abdul Mahdawi and Dylan Thompson. This is an amateur championship, not a UFC or professional MMA title.

items.label: PRO WIN · Shaun Johnson · Rear-naked choke · R1 4:54
items.detail: Thicknesse made his recorded professional MMA debut at Eternal MMA 55 on the Gold Coast, submitting Shaun Johnson by rear-naked choke at 4:54 of round one. His professional record became 1-0.

items.label: Eternal MMA 61 bout with Nicholas Kren canceled
items.detail: A professional matchup against Nicholas Kren was listed for Eternal MMA 61 but did not take place. No result is added to Thicknesse's professional record. The precise cancellation reason is not independently established.

items.label: Eternal MMA 64 booking with Anthony Drilich canceled
items.detail: The planned meeting with Anthony Drilich at Eternal MMA 64 was not contested. The card itself is marked canceled in fight registries; no fighter injury or individual withdrawal is inferred.

items.label: Eternal MMA 65 bout with Jarrett Wilbraham canceled
items.detail: Thicknesse was listed against Jarrett Wilbraham at Eternal MMA 65, but the bout did not occur. There is no professional result for this booking.

items.label: Wollongong Wars 8 bout with Mitchell Holden canceled
items.detail: A scheduled matchup with Mitchell Holden did not take place. It is retained as a canceled booking rather than represented as an official fight or a documented injury layoff.

items.label: Earns Brazilian jiu-jitsu black belt
items.detail: Thicknesse's UFC questionnaire says he has held a BJJ black belt since 2022. The day of promotion and the awarding instructor are not specified in that source.

items.label: PRO WIN · Semakadde Kakembo · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: In his second professional bout, Thicknesse beat unbeaten Semakadde Kakembo at Eternal MMA 70 by unanimous decision over three full five-minute rounds. Thicknesse said he was dropped twice in round one before rallying, describing it as his toughest career fight. They had previously met as amateurs in July 2019.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog result and UFC fighter questionnaire

items.label: PRO WIN · Michael Barber · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: At Hex Fight Series 25, Thicknesse defeated Michael Barber by unanimous decision after three completed five-minute rounds. Sherdog dates the event Feb. 24, 2023 (one secondary chronology misplaces it in 2024). He improved to 3-0.

items.label: Hex Fight Series 26 bout with Emre Han Hekimoglu canceled
items.detail: The planned Hex 26 fight with Emre Han Hekimoglu did not happen and is not part of Thicknesse's professional MMA results. Available listings do not establish a definitive cancellation cause.

items.label: PRO WIN · Michael Mannu · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: Thicknesse beat Michael Mannu by unanimous decision at Hex Fight Series 29, completing all three five-minute rounds to advance to 4-0 in professional MMA.

items.label: Scheduled Canggu Fight Night 31 matchup with Jaka Maruba Naibaho canceled
items.detail: A booking against Jaka Maruba Naibaho appears on the canceled-match register for Canggu Fight Night 31. Thicknesse instead has a completed bout with Jufri Gobel on the same event date, but the available source does not establish the replacement sequence.

items.label: PRO WIN · Jufri Gobel · TKO (punches) · R1 1:50
items.detail: At Bali MMA's Canggu Fight Night 31, Thicknesse stopped Jufri Gobel by punches at 1:50 of round one, reaching 5-0. The recorded bout was contested at featherweight rather than his usual professional bantamweight limit.

items.label: PRO WIN · Norman Agcopra · Rear-naked choke · R1 2:38
items.detail: Thicknesse submitted Norman Agcopra (also spelled Agcorpra in some databases) by rear-naked choke at 2:38 of round one at Bali MMA's Canggu Fight Night 32. His professional record moved to 6-0.

items.label: PRO WIN · Marvin Malunes · KO (elbows) · R1 (time unrecorded)
items.detail: At Hex Fight Series 33 in Melbourne, Thicknesse beat Marvin Malunes with elbows in round one. The official fight registry records a knockout but does not give a reliable elapsed clock time; a database placeholder of 0:00 must not be treated as a stoppage time. He improved to 7-0.

items.label: Wins Hex Fight Series bantamweight championship
items.detail: The round-one knockout of Marvin Malunes occurred in a scheduled Hex bantamweight title bout at Hex Fight Series 33. Thicknesse left with the promotional belt, which he also lists in his UFC questionnaire. This was his final recorded fight before joining the UFC.

items.date: Late Jan. 2025 (about ten days before UFC 312)
items.label: Accepts short-notice UFC debut against Aleksandre Topuria
items.detail: While working a security shift, Thicknesse received an Instagram message from Ilia Topuria's manager about an opportunity to fight Aleksandre Topuria at UFC 312. He consulted coach Joe Lopez and training partner Alexander Volkanovski and accepted about ten days out. The precise day of the initial call is not confirmed.

items.label: PRO LOSS · Aleksandre Topuria · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: Thicknesse made his UFC debut at UFC 312 in Sydney, losing a unanimous decision to Aleksandre Topuria after three complete five-minute rounds. All three judges scored it 30-27 for Topuria. His professional record became 7-1. UFC and Sherdog index the bout as Feb. 8, while some Australian event records list Feb. 9.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog fight record / official UFC result

items.label: Describes full training camp for first UFC return
items.detail: Ahead of fighting Josias Musasa in Perth, Thicknesse said he had a complete camp this time rather than the roughly ten days' notice before facing Topuria. He noted he had already been training consistently when the UFC 312 opportunity arrived, so the first fight was not an untrained 'off the couch' appearance.

items.label: PRO WIN · Josias Musasa · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night: Ulberg vs. Reyes in Perth, Thicknesse defeated Josias Musasa by unanimous decision, 29-28 on all three judges' cards, after three rounds. His first official UFC victory took him to 8-1 overall and 1-1 in the Octagon. Sherdog and UFC date the bout Sep. 27 while some Australian-local publications use Sep. 28.

items.label: PRO WIN · Vince Morales · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night: Della Maddalena vs. Prates in Perth, Thicknesse won a competitive three-round unanimous decision over Vince Morales, 29-28 on every official scorecard. His professional record improved to 9-1 and his regular UFC record to 2-1. The date is May 2, 2026, despite a mistaken November 2024 date in one sentence on his UFC athlete Q&A.

items.label: Booked for UFC 333 against undefeated Asaf Chopurov
items.detail: The forthcoming Oct. 24 UFC 333 bantamweight contest with undefeated Asaf Chopurov was reported in September. Thicknesse entered the matchup on consecutive UFC decision wins over Musasa and Morales. This is a confirmed scheduled fight, not a completed result.

items.label: Discusses Chopurov, training with Volkanovski and fight adjustments
items.detail: Thicknesse appeared on the heavywgt MMA podcast for a 19:05 interview discussing the Asaf Chopurov matchup, working with Volkanovski, power-punching mechanics, improving performance late in fights, and his approach to Abu Dhabi. The episode also included discussion of Petr Yan's camp. These are the published interview topics, not proof of a permanent gym move.

items.label: Freestyle Fighting Gym remains listed primary team
items.detail: Sherdog and UFC continue to identify Thicknesse with the Freestyle Fighting Gym/Freestyle MMA team under Joe Lopez. His long-running work with Volkanovski is documented; no reliable source establishes a permanent 2026 departure or a new head coach for UFC 333.
items.sourceLabel: UFC athlete profile and Sherdog affiliation

items.label: UFC 333 · bantamweight vs. Asaf Chopurov
items.detail: Thicknesse (9-1 professional; 2-1 UFC) is scheduled to fight Asaf Chopurov (11-0) at Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi. The early prelims are advertised to start at 10 a.m. Eastern / 9 a.m. Central / 6 p.m. Abu Dhabi time. That is a broadcast segment start, not a confirmed individual cage-walk time. No fight result exists as of Oct. 21, 2026.
items.sourceLabel: UFC 333 official event and fight-by-fight preview

audit.scope: Rebuilt chronological career from early wrestling and Freestyle/Volkanovski affiliation through eight indexed amateur bouts (7-1), March 2020 IMMAF featherweight gold with exact rounds/times, 9-1 full professional record with rounds and clocks, 2021-24 canceled bookings, BJJ black belt (2022), 2024 Hex bantamweight title, short-notice 2025 UFC debut and scorecards, September 2025 and May 2026 unanimous decisions, October 2026 podcast and Abu Dhabi UFC 333 booking. Unknown fight clock times not invented; local vs US date differences flagged; no speculative injury/anti-doping/weight misses.

items.label: Born in Georgia; later represents Azerbaijan
items.detail: Chopurov was born in Georgia, according to his UFC profile and fight databases. He is widely identified as Azerbaijani by nationality/representation and has fought out of Volgograd, Russia. Birthplace, sporting representation and training base are different facts and should not be conflated.

items.label: Inspired by Khabib Nurmagomedov's discipline
items.detail: In an Oct. 2026 Ariel Helwani interview, Chopurov said he became interested in MMA at roughly 14 or 15 after observing Khabib Nurmagomedov's discipline. The approximate year is inferred from his Nov. 2001 birthdate; this is not a confirmed first-training date.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog coverage of Oct. 14, 2026 Ariel Helwani interview

items.label: Trains in Dagestan with Abdulmanap Nurmagomedov
items.detail: Chopurov says he attended a training camp in Dagestan run by Abdulmanap Nurmagomedov, father and coach of Khabib. He has not provided a reliable calendar date for the camp; it necessarily predates Abdulmanap's death in July 2020. Do not describe Abdulmanap as his long-term head coach on the strength of a single camp.

items.label: First successful UAE Warriors championship defense
items.detail: Chopurov submitted Adriano Ramos by rear-naked choke at 2:24 in the first round and retained his bantamweight championship. This improved his professional record to 10-0.
items.sourceLabel: UAE Warriors official fighter bout log

items.label: WIN · Reece McLaren · KO (right punch) · R1 1:03
items.detail: At UAE Warriors 72, Chopurov defeated Reece McLaren by ko (right punch), recorded at 1:03 of r1. A single right hand dropped the former ONE Championship title challenger. The finish was Chopurov's second successful title defense and moved him to 11-0, ten finishes, with five by KO/TKO and five by submission. This was an official professional MMA victory.

items.label: Defends UAE Warriors belt for second time
items.detail: At UAE Warriors 72 in Abu Dhabi, Chopurov knocked out Reece McLaren at 1:03 of round one with a right hand. He had now won six times for the promotion and recorded two successful defenses of its 135 lb championship.

items.label: UFC signing confirmed with 11-0 professional record
items.detail: MMA Junkie reported his UFC signing on Sept. 24; Sherdog followed on Sept. 25. His 11-0 professional record included five knockouts/TKOs, five submissions and one decision. The proposed Oct. 24 UFC 333 debut was part of the signing coverage, not an already fought UFC result.

items.label: Discusses early Khabib influence and Abdulmanap training camp
items.detail: In comments reported from Ariel Helwani's interview, Chopurov recalled being inspired by Khabib around age 14–15 and attending a camp in Dagestan with Abdulmanap Nurmagomedov. The fighter's recollection confirms a training experience but does not provide its exact date.

items.label: Regular Petr Yan training partner entering UFC debut
items.detail: UFC and MMA Junkie describe Chopurov as one of reigning bantamweight champion Petr Yan's principal training partners. They are scheduled to appear on the same UFC 333 card. The reported relationship does not independently establish a new permanent head coach or gym.
items.sourceLabel: MMA Junkie signing coverage / UFC Oct. 2026 feature

items.label: UFC 333 · bantamweight debut vs. Colby Thicknesse
items.detail: Chopurov (11-0 professional, 0-0 UFC) is scheduled to face Colby Thicknesse (9-1 professional, 2-1 UFC) at Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi on UFC 333. This is his scheduled UFC debut, and no bout result or individual walkout time exists as of Oct. 21, 2026. Early preliminary coverage is advertised for 10 a.m. Eastern / 9 a.m. Central / 6 p.m. Abu Dhabi time.

audit.scope: Comprehensive dated rebuild: all 11 Sherdog professional bouts (11-0; 5 KO/TKO, 5 submissions, 1 decision) with rounds, methods and clocks; 35 individually indexed amateur wins and 1 loss including delayed 2021 IMMAF Junior World gold in Jan. 2022; full 2021–2025 amateur tournament history and 34-1 vs 35-1 discrepancy; first Khabib/Abdulmanap inspiration and Dagestan camp, Sambo 34/Chingiz Allazov multi-gym reports, Petr Yan sparring, canceled Tokarev/McLaren bookings, UAE Warriors bantamweight crown and two defenses, UFC signing and Oct. 24 scheduled debut. Sources include IMMAF, Sherdog, UAE Warriors, Tapology, UFC and MMA Junkie. Unknown dates/times explicitly qualified.

items.label: Father enrolls him in boxing for fitness
items.detail: Malkoun has said his father enrolled him in boxing because he was overweight as a teenager. A reported starting age of 16 points to roughly 2011–12, but no precise initial training date is documented.
items.sourceLabel: UFC athlete questionnaire and biographical coverage

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Dean Bradley · KO (punch) · R2 0:43
items.detail: At Superfight MMA 1, Malkoun knocked out Dean Bradley at 0:43 of round two. Recorded as amateur MMA, not professional boxing or professional MMA.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Rhys Savage · Unanimous decision · R3 3:00
items.detail: Malkoun defeated Rhys Savage by unanimous decision after three complete three-minute rounds at Superfight MMA 2. Sherdog indexes two amateur victories; neither belongs in his professional 10-3 total.

items.label: Grant Brechney amateur booking does not occur
items.detail: The planned Urban Fight Night 6 amateur contest was canceled and has no official result.

items.label: Adrian Leaitua booking does not occur
items.detail: An Urban Fight Night 8 middleweight booking against Adrian Leaitua did not take place. It is not his professional debut.

items.label: Develops at Gracie Jiu Jitsu Smeaton Grange
items.detail: Malkoun studied and worked part-time before coach Alex Prates offered him an opportunity to teach MMA classes at the Smeaton Grange gym. The arrangement supported regular training. The exact start date is not established.

items.label: WIN · Cameron (Cam) Rowston · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: BRACE 47 in Sydney. Defeated Cameron (Cam) Rowston by unanimous decision; official recorded round and clock: R3, 5:00. Professional MMA debut; moved to 1-0. Rowston later joined the UFC middleweight division.

items.label: BOXING WIN · Matthew Saville · TKO · R2 2:35
items.detail: Malkoun defeated Matthew Saville by second-round TKO (2:35) in an Australian professional heavyweight boxing match. This is separate from his MMA record.

items.label: Scheduled bout with Duke Didier canceled
items.detail: BRACE 53 and the proposed light heavyweight fight against Duke Didier were canceled. No 205-pound professional fight took place.

items.label: WIN · Ryan Heketa · TKO (punches) · R1 1:32
items.detail: Hex Fight Series 17. Defeated Ryan Heketa by tko (punches); official recorded round and clock: R1, 1:32. Professional MMA record improved to 2-0.

items.label: Wins ADCC Asia & Oceania Trials, under 99 kg
items.detail: ADCC's official Tokyo results list Malkoun of Gracie Humaita first in the men's -99 kg bracket, ahead of Zaid Sad Sami and Harry Grech. This won qualification for the world championships; it is not itself an ADCC Worlds title.

items.label: WIN · Christophe Van Dijck (Van Dijk) · TKO (punches) · R2/R3 disputed 3:31
items.detail: Wollongong Wars 7. Defeated Christophe Van Dijck (Van Dijk) by tko (punches); official recorded round and clock: R2/R3 disputed, 3:31. The result and 3:31 time are consistent, but sources disagree on the round: Sherdog lists round three while ESPN, Tapology and the opponent's record list round two. The round remains flagged as disputed pending original event records.

items.label: Withdraws from ADCC World Championships roster
items.detail: FloGrappling reported that Malkoun, although qualified through the Asia/Oceania trials, was no longer in the -99 kg field for the 2019 ADCC Worlds. He should not be credited with competing in that world championship.

items.label: BOXING WIN · Waikato Falefehi · Unanimous decision · 4 rounds
items.detail: Malkoun won a four-round professional heavyweight boxing decision at ANBF Best of the Best. Biographies report an overall professional boxing record of 3-0, but only this bout and his Nov. 2017 Matthew Saville contest could be verified individually here.

items.label: Reported Pan Pacific jiu-jitsu gold medal
items.detail: Biographical accounts credit a 2019 Pan Pacific BJJ gold medal. Tournament bracket, exact date and belt division remain insufficiently documented; it is not counted as a verified ADCC world title.

items.label: WIN · Sebastian Temesi · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: Eternal MMA 48 in Melbourne. Defeated Sebastian Temesi by unanimous decision; official recorded round and clock: R3, 5:00. Improved to 4-0, his last regional professional MMA fight.

items.label: Becomes long-term Robert Whittaker training partner
items.detail: Malkoun has trained extensively alongside former UFC middleweight champion Robert Whittaker in Sydney. This is a documented sparring and training relationship, not evidence that Whittaker is his only coach.

items.label: Signs UFC contract at 4-0
items.detail: Malkoun entered the UFC with four professional wins in Australia, little MMA experience compared with typical prospects, and a reputation as Robert Whittaker's training partner.

items.label: LOSS · Phil Hawes · KO (punches) · R1 0:18
items.detail: UFC 254 in Abu Dhabi. Lost to Phil Hawes by ko (punches); official recorded round and clock: R1, 0:18. An 18-second UFC debut knockout loss, his first defeat in professional MMA.

items.label: WIN · Abdul Razak Alhassan · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: UFC Fight Night: Whittaker vs. Gastelum. Defeated Abdul Razak Alhassan by unanimous decision; official recorded round and clock: R3, 5:00. His first UFC win, using sustained wrestling over three rounds.

items.label: First AJ Dobson booking shifts from UFC 270
items.detail: The Jan. 22 AJ Dobson pairing at UFC 270 was rescheduled; the same fighters met on Feb. 12 at UFC 271. No result is assigned to the uncompleted original booking.

items.label: Works back from confidence loss after UFC debut
items.detail: Malkoun later described the mental challenge of his UFC debut loss and rebuilding his confidence. This is a fighter interview account, not a documented psychiatric diagnosis or physical injury.

items.label: WIN · A.J. Dobson · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: UFC 271 in Houston. Defeated A.J. Dobson by unanimous decision; official recorded round and clock: R3, 5:00. Second consecutive UFC win; professional record reached 6-1.

items.label: LOSS · Brendan Allen · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: UFC 275 in Singapore. Lost to Brendan Allen by unanimous decision; official recorded round and clock: R3, 5:00. His only professional decision loss as of October 2026. He later said he disagreed with the judges, but the Allen victory is official. Event dates differ by source/time zone.

items.label: WIN · Nick Maximov · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: UFC Fight Night: Grasso vs. Araujo. Defeated Nick Maximov by unanimous decision; official recorded round and clock: R3, 5:00. Wrestling-heavy unanimous decision, professional record 7-2.

items.label: Aliaskhab Khizriev and Robert Bryczek bookings fall through
items.detail: The Sep. 23 UFC card initially advertised Aliaskhab Khizriev vs Malkoun. Khizriev withdrew, Robert Bryczek was booked and then withdrew, leaving Cody Brundage as the actual opponent. Neither earlier bout happened.
items.sourceLabel: UFC announcement and Tapology canceled matches

items.label: Talks about Whittaker and frustration with Brendan Allen result
items.detail: In a gym interview published Sep. 22, Malkoun discussed his partnership with Whittaker and his belief that he should have received the Allen decision. His opinion does not alter that official result.

items.label: LOSS · Cody Brundage · Disqualification (illegal back-of-head elbow) · R1 4:15
items.detail: UFC Fight Night: Fiziev vs. Gamrot. Lost to Cody Brundage by disqualification (illegal back-of-head elbow); official recorded round and clock: R1, 4:15. Referee Mark Smith stopped the fight after a strike to the back of Brundage's head while he was on the mat; Brundage could not continue after medical assessment. Malkoun lost by DQ, not KO or no contest.

items.label: WIN · Andre Petroski · TKO (body soccer kick and strikes) · R2 0:39
items.detail: UFC Atlantic City: Blanchfield vs. Fiorot. Defeated Andre Petroski by tko (body soccer kick and strikes); official recorded round and clock: R2, 0:39. Official fight records use a soccer kick to the body and follow-up strikes. A kick to the body of a grounded opponent is legal in MMA.

items.label: Serious back injury stalls career
items.detail: Malkoun said he developed persistent back problems after the Petroski win and repeatedly aggravated the issue by trying to train and return too early. Exact diagnosis or surgery is not publicly established.

items.label: Withdraws from scheduled Rodolfo Vieira fight
items.detail: The scheduled Feb. 15, 2025 matchup with Rodolfo Vieira was canceled after Malkoun's injury setback. Andre Petroski replaced Malkoun and fought Vieira instead. He did not compete on the card.

items.label: Discusses impatience, injury setbacks and return
items.detail: Ahead of UFC 325, Malkoun acknowledged that attempting a premature comeback had worsened the injury, and said he had questioned when he would be able to compete again.

items.label: Almost 22-month layoff during back recovery
items.detail: Malkoun did not fight between Mar. 30, 2024 and Jan. 31, 2026. The interval was about 22 months; his described back injury and recovery were central to the absence. No anti-doping penalty is documented as the cause.

items.label: WIN · Torrez Finney · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: UFC 325 in Sydney. Defeated Torrez Finney by unanimous decision; official recorded round and clock: R3, 5:00. Official scorecards: 30-27, 30-26, 30-26. Return after nearly 22 months away; U.S. broadcast fight date Jan. 31, Australia local date Feb. 1.

items.label: Gerald Meerschaert misses weight by four pounds
items.detail: Meerschaert weighed 190 pounds versus the 186-pound non-title middleweight allowance, while Malkoun weighed 186. The fight proceeded as a 190-pound catchweight bout, with Meerschaert forfeiting 30% of his purse. This is not a Malkoun weight miss.

items.label: WIN · Gerald Meerschaert · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: UFC Perth: Della Maddalena vs. Prates. Defeated Gerald Meerschaert by unanimous decision; official recorded round and clock: R3, 5:00. Three 29-28 scorecards for Malkoun; he improved to 10-3 overall and 6-3 UFC. Catchweight bout was due to Meerschaert's miss.

items.label: Says Perth performance was below his standards
items.detail: After the decision against Meerschaert, Malkoun publicly expressed disappointment with his own performance despite the win. The official scorecards remained 29-28 on all three cards.

items.label: Smeaton Grange and PMA Super Martial Arts team entries
items.detail: Tapology and ESPN identify Gracie Jiu-Jitsu Smeaton Grange; Sherdog lists PMA Super Martial Arts. Without dated statements establishing a transfer, these affiliations should not be turned into a claimed 2026 permanent gym switch. His Whittaker training partnership is well documented.

items.label: Comments on Vagaev, back recovery and Whittaker sparring
items.detail: In a Fox Sports Australia interview, Malkoun said he was comfortable with Vagaev's wrestling threat, and reported feeling physically better than he had for several years after the back problems. Fox also reports that Malkoun has worked training NRL players for the Penrith Panthers and Canterbury Bulldogs. Malkoun said Whittaker was now much bigger as a sparring partner.
items.sourceLabel: Fox Sports Australia fight-week interview, Oct. 21, 2026

items.label: UFC 333 · middleweight vs. Abubakar Vagaev
items.detail: Jacob Malkoun (10-3 MMA, 6-3 UFC) is scheduled against Abubakar Vagaev (25-4) at Etihad Arena, Abu Dhabi. Early prelim programming starts at 10 a.m. ET / 9 a.m. CT / 6 p.m. local, not a confirmed individual cage-walk time. No result exists as of Oct. 21.

audit.scope: Rebuilt chronological record covering two dated amateur MMA wins; 13 complete pro MMA bouts with results and times (10-3), 2017 and 2019 documented boxing wins within reported 3-0 record; ADCC 2019 under-99kg Trials win and documented Worlds withdrawal; contested Van Dijck fight-round difference; Smeaton Grange / PMA team-listing distinctions; 2022 Dobson rescheduling, 2023 Khizriev/Bryczek replacements, Brundage DQ, 2024 Petroski TKO; 2024-2026 back injury, 2025 Vieira cancellation, 2026 Finney and Meerschaert scores, Meerschaert opponent-only weight miss, and Oct. 21 UFC 333 fight-week interview and booking. Undocumented surgery, doping, exact third boxing bout and gym switch not claimed. Chronological position of retrospective interviews, gym affiliations and layoff-end date normalized after initial commit.

items.label: Born in Russia
items.detail: Sherdog gives his birthday as April 14, 1993; he fights out of Grozny. The more specific place of birth is not established.

items.label: Begins wrestling and MMA; dates disputed
items.detail: His UFC questionnaire says he began wrestling at age 19 and MMA at age 20, but the professional record documents his MMA debut on June 30, 2012, when he was 19. The start date cannot be asserted precisely; the conflict is noted.
items.sourceLabel: UFC fighter Q&A and Sherdog first professional fight

items.detail: A planned WFCA 45 fight against Marcão Santana was canceled; Vagaev actually met Rodrigo Correia on that date. No unverified withdrawal reason is attached.

items.detail: At WFCA 45, Vagaev defeated Rodrigo Correia by unanimous decision. The result was after 3 complete rounds (final bell 5:00).

items.detail: At WFCA 53, Vagaev lost to Murad Abdulaev by ko (punch). Stoppage at 1:25 of round 2. Abdulaev knocked out Vagaev to win the WFCA welterweight title. Their 2021 rematch was a different championship contest.

items.detail: Abdulaev knocked out Vagaev to win the WFCA welterweight title. Their 2021 rematch was a different championship contest.

items.detail: ACA's official report says Vagaev became its NEW welterweight champion by beating Murad Abdulaev. It happened in 2021, not 2022.

items.label: First proposed Gadzhidaudov title defense date falls through
items.detail: The proposed ACA 130 matchup with Ustarmagomed Gadzhidaudov did not take place. It is a canceled booking, not an official MMA result.

items.label: Second proposed Gadzhidaudov title defense date rescheduled
items.detail: The planned ACA 136 fight did not occur; the championship was actually contested March 26 at ACA 138.

items.label: WIN · Ustarmagomed Gadzhidaudov · Split decision · R5 5:00
items.detail: At ACA 138, Vagaev defeated Ustarmagomed Gadzhidaudov by split decision. The result was after 5 complete rounds (final bell 5:00). First successful ACA title defense, a five-round split decision against Gadzhidaudov. The 2022 date should not be incorrectly labeled a new ACA championship win.

items.label: Defends ACA championship against Gadzhidaudov
items.detail: First successful ACA title defense, a five-round split decision against Gadzhidaudov. The 2022 date should not be incorrectly labeled a new ACA championship win.

items.detail: At ACA 149, Vagaev lost to Vitaliy Slipenko by ko (elbow). Stoppage at 0:20 of round 2. Vitaliy Slipenko knocked him out with an elbow just 0:20 into ROUND TWO, taking the ACA welterweight belt. Earlier timeline incorrectly said a fifth-round KO.

items.detail: Vitaliy Slipenko knocked him out with an elbow just 0:20 into ROUND TWO, taking the ACA welterweight belt. Earlier timeline incorrectly said a fifth-round KO.

items.detail: After losing to Slipenko in December 2022, Vagaev was listed for a July 2023 rematch that was canceled. No documented injury diagnosis or official fight result is attached to this booking.

items.label: Regains ACA title against Albert Tumenov
items.detail: Reclaimed the ACA welterweight belt in a five-round decision against Albert Tumenov. This was his second ACA title reign and third major promotional championship including WFCA.

items.label: UFC signing announced; vacates ACA title
items.detail: Vagaev announced signing with the UFC and giving up his ACA title. He publicly credited Khamzat Chimaev for helping secure the deal and also thanked Ramzan Kadyrov for his support. This is a sourced statement about the signing, not evidence of a new gym.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog report of signing and fighter statement

items.label: Makes weight at 171 pounds for UFC debut
items.detail: Weighed 171 lb, legally within the one-pound non-title welterweight allowance. All 26 competitors on the July Abu Dhabi card made weight.
items.sourceLabel: MMA Junkie official Abu Dhabi weigh-in report

items.label: WIN · Saygid Izagakhmaev · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night: Ankalaev vs. Guskov, Vagaev defeated Saygid Izagakhmaev by unanimous decision. The result was after 3 complete rounds (final bell 5:00). Official UFC scorecards were 29-28, 29-28, 29-28. This was his UFC debut at welterweight after about 17 months since the Tumenov fight.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog professional record; promotion cross-check where available

items.label: Wins UFC debut over Saygid Izagakhmaev
items.detail: Official UFC scorecards were 29-28, 29-28, 29-28. This was his UFC debut at welterweight after about 17 months since the Tumenov fight.

items.label: Malkoun fight added to UFC 333 at middleweight
items.detail: The scheduled Oct. 24 matchup with Jacob Malkoun was reported on Sept. 23. UFC described this as Vagaev moving up to 185 pounds for his second UFC appearance, not a permanent commitment to never fight at welterweight again.

items.label: Discusses middleweight preparation and fight booking
items.detail: Vagaev told MMA.Metaratings he had previously been preparing to compete at middleweight at around 100 kg before being booked at 170 lb for his July debut. He said he offered the UFC either division and learned of the 185 lb Malkoun matchup about six weeks before the event. This is his account, not an independently measured fight-week weight.

items.label: Reports mild cold and planned acclimation for UFC 333
items.detail: In another interview, Vagaev said he had a mild cold during training but felt recovered, with another hard week of sparring scheduled before flying to Abu Dhabi to acclimate. He identified Malkoun's pace, striking and grappling as important challenges. Do not interpret a self-reported brief illness as a medically confirmed long-term injury.

items.label: Akhmat Fight Club is still listed as his gym
items.detail: UFC and Sherdog list Akhmat Fight Club / Fight Club Akhmat in Grozny. Although he has a documented professional relationship with Khamzat Chimaev, there is no verified 2026 permanent transfer to a different gym or head coach.

items.label: UFC 333 · middleweight vs. Jacob Malkoun
items.detail: At Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi, Vagaev (25-4, UFC 1-0) is booked against Malkoun (10-3, UFC 6-3) at middleweight. UFC 333 preliminary coverage begins at noon ET / 11 a.m. CT / 8 p.m. Abu Dhabi, not a confirmed cage-walk time. No result is available as of Oct. 21, 2026.

audit.scope: Full audit of all 29 professional MMA fights (25-4) with rounds/clocks from Sherdog and cross-checked promotion sources; 2017 WFCA Ushukov title, 2021 original ACA Abdulaev title, 2022 ACA Gadzhidaudov title defense, December 2022 second-round 0:20 Slipenko KO title loss, 2025 Tumenov recapture; canceled ACA bookings; 2026 signing with acknowledged Chimaev help; July 2026 UFC debut 29-28 x3, 171lb compliant weigh-in; fall 2026 middleweight move, October camp illness and acclimation statements; sources distinguish age-at-debut and 2014 submission method inconsistencies. No unverified amateur wins, doping, surgery, or permanent gym move.

items.label: Born in Jette, Brussels, Belgium
items.detail: UFC identifies Jette in Brussels as his place of birth. Oki represents Belgium and has described a family heritage connected to Nigeria and Zimbabwe; his 'Zulu Warrior' nickname refers to his Zimbabwean ancestry. Avoid inventing a precise ancestry percentage.
items.sourceLabel: UFC athlete biography and September 2025 interview

items.label: Begins combat-sports training for competition
items.detail: Oki says he started training at age 17 because he enjoyed competition and wanted to learn to fight. The calendar range is inferred from his November 1995 birthdate; the exact enrollment day and first gym are not publicly confirmed.

items.label: Muay Thai booking with Hakki Kandis
items.detail: Tapology indexes a Muay Thai appearance against Hakki Kandis at Fight Club Den Haag but does not report a verified result. It is not counted as an amateur MMA win, an MMA loss or a completed professional bout.

items.label: MUAY THAI WIN · Milad Hakimi · Decision (2 rounds)
items.detail: At Fight Club Den Haag, Oki recorded a decision victory over Milad Hakimi in a two-round Muay Thai contest. It is listed separately from his mixed martial arts record and was not a professional UFC/MMA fight.

items.label: AMATEUR MMA WIN · Bassem Zaied · Unanimous decision · R3 3:00
items.detail: Tapology records an amateur MMA victory over Bassem Zaied at 360 Selection #1 after three 3-minute rounds. The amateur result is not included in the 10-4 professional tally.

items.label: AMATEUR MMA DRAW · Alexandru Curcudel · Split draw · R3 3:00
items.detail: At FightStar Championship 13, Oki and Alexandru Curcudel fought to a split draw after three 3-minute rounds. Both Sherdog and Tapology record the result. Sherdog displays only this draw in its indexed amateur record while Tapology also lists the Bassem Zaied win.

items.date: Before Mar. 2018 (work and coaching dates unverified)
items.label: Works at Domino's and teaches at his gym
items.detail: Oki says he previously worked at Domino's Pizza while teaching children's classes and private lessons at his gym. He does not give exact dates for either job, so this is placed before the UFC without claiming that every position ended by 2018.

items.label: LOSS · Sebastien Di Franco · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: European Beatdown 3: Oki lost to Sebastien Di Franco by unanimous decision. The fight went the full 3 rounds; the 5:00 entry is the final bell, not a stoppage. His professional MMA debut was a unanimous-decision loss at a 159-pound catchweight, leaving him 0-1. Some earlier timelines incorrectly called the promotion Strength & Honor.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog professional results; UFC for Octagon scorecards

items.label: WIN · Jordan Beljic · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: European Beatdown 4: Oki defeated Jordan Beljic by unanimous decision. The fight went the full 3 rounds; the 5:00 entry is the final bell, not a stoppage. Earned his first professional win at lightweight and moved to 1-1.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog professional results; UFC for Octagon scorecards

items.label: WIN · Fayad Djoumoi · TKO (punches) · R3 4:20
items.detail: European Beatdown 5: Oki defeated Fayad Djoumoi by tko (punches). The recorded finish was at 4:20 of round 3. First professional stoppage win. He then had no completed professional MMA bout on record until July 2021.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog professional results; UFC for Octagon scorecards

items.label: No documented professional MMA bouts for about 29 months
items.detail: Fight records show a gap from Feb. 2, 2019 through July 25, 2021. The length is observable from the bout dates, but no specific injury, surgery, suspension or exclusive COVID explanation has been established for the whole interval.

items.label: Christopher Jung bout does not occur
items.detail: A planned LFL 2 contest with Christopher Jung was canceled. Oki instead fought Hyram Rodriguez at that event. The reason for the change is not established by the available bout listing.

items.label: WIN · Hyram Rodriguez · Submission (guillotine choke) · R1 1:38
items.detail: Levels Fight League 2: Oki defeated Hyram Rodriguez by submission (guillotine choke). The recorded finish was at 1:38 of round 1. His sole professional submission victory through October 2026. Tapology lists the stoppage at 1:39 rather than Sherdog's 1:38.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog professional results; UFC for Octagon scorecards

items.label: Ole-Jørgen Mandt Johnsen bout does not occur
items.detail: The proposed Levels Fight League 3 bout with Ole-Jørgen Mandt Johnsen was canceled. Oki faced Tudor Dermenji on the same card instead. A specific medical or disciplinary reason should not be inferred.

items.label: WIN · Tudor Dermenji · TKO (punches and knees) · R2 4:12
items.detail: Levels Fight League 3: Oki defeated Tudor Dermenji by tko (punches and knees). The recorded finish was at 4:12 of round 2. Stopped Dermenji late in round two after the previously listed Ole-Jørgen Mandt Johnsen fight did not go ahead.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog professional results; UFC for Octagon scorecards

items.label: European Beatdown 8 booking with Dorval Jordan canceled
items.detail: Oki's scheduled European Beatdown 8 fight with Dorval Jordan did not take place and has no professional fight result.

items.label: LFL 4 / Jan Quaeyhaegens booking canceled amid COVID rules
items.detail: A planned Levels Fight League 4 matchup with Jan Quaeyhaegens was not fought because the event was canceled under new COVID-19 restrictions. This confirms the reason for this specific canceled event, not for all inactivity around that period.

items.label: WIN · Assis Silva · TKO (punches) · R1 1:43
items.detail: Atomic Fighting Championship 1: Oki defeated Assis Silva by tko (punches). The recorded finish was at 1:43 of round 1. Won by punches and ground-and-pound in round one. The event register does not designate this as the lightweight title-winning fight.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog professional results; UFC for Octagon scorecards

items.label: WIN · Nair Melikyan · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: Atomic Fighting Championship 2: Oki defeated Nair Melikyan by unanimous decision. The fight went the full 3 rounds; the 5:00 entry is the final bell, not a stoppage. Won the VACANT Atomic lightweight championship, according to the bout listing. Melikyan was reportedly unbeaten entering the fight. The official UFC questionnaire later calls Oki a two-time Atomic champion.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog professional results; UFC for Octagon scorecards

items.label: Wins vacant Atomic lightweight title against Nair Melikyan
items.detail: The Atomic FC 2 listing identifies the bout against Nair Melikyan as a contest for the vacant lightweight belt, won by unanimous decision. Oki's earlier Assis Silva win at Atomic 1 is not shown as a title bout.

items.label: WIN · Jocimar Ferreira · TKO (knee to body) · R1 2:16
items.detail: Atomic Fighting Championship 3: Oki defeated Jocimar Ferreira by tko (knee to body). The recorded finish was at 2:16 of round 1. Defended the Atomic lightweight championship with a knee to the body/liver. The event lists him as champion coming into this fight, so it is not demonstrably a second distinct title acquisition.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog professional results; UFC for Octagon scorecards

items.label: Successfully defends Atomic lightweight championship
items.detail: Oki beat Jocimar Ferreira by a body-knee TKO at 2:16 of round one in an Atomic FC 3 title fight; the listing shows Oki entered as champion. UFC calls him a two-time Atomic lightweight champion, but available bout-by-bout records establish an October 2022 vacant title win followed by a March 2023 defense, not two separately confirmed title-winning reigns.
items.sourceLabel: Tapology AFC 2 and AFC 3 championship records

items.label: WIN · Dylan Salvador · TKO (punch to body) · R1 2:46
items.detail: Dana White's Contender Series Season 7, Week 4: Oki defeated Dylan Salvador by tko (punch to body). The recorded finish was at 2:46 of round 1. The body shot finish earned Oki a UFC contract. This is an official professional MMA win, moving him to 8-1, but is not one of his five regular UFC appearances through October 2026.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog professional results; UFC for Octagon scorecards

items.label: Earns UFC contract after Contender Series body-shot TKO
items.detail: Oki earned a UFC contract after stopping Dylan Salvador at 2:46 in round one of DWCS Season 7, Week 4. He entered regular UFC competition with an 8-1 professional record, counting the DWCS win but not treating that bout as his official Octagon debut.
items.sourceLabel: UFC Contender Series history and fighter profile

items.date: By Feb. 2024 (team history; date of joining unverified)
items.label: Valon Team / Da Vinci Fighting affiliations
items.detail: UFC lists Valon Team as his training base; Sherdog lists Da Vinci Fighting / Valon Team. The dates of the affiliations and any team change have not been independently verified. Oki describes running and strength work in the morning, with MMA and wrestling technical sessions in the evening.
items.sourceLabel: UFC athlete questionnaire and Sherdog affiliation

items.label: Damir Hadžović removed due to visa issues
items.detail: UFC announced that Hadžović was removed from the Feb. 10 lightweight booking because of visa issues. Timothy Cuamba replaced him with only three days until the event. The visa problem was Hadžović's, not Oki's.

items.label: WIN · Timothy (Timmy) Cuamba · Split decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: UFC Fight Night: Hermansson vs. Pyfer: Oki defeated Timothy (Timmy) Cuamba by split decision. The fight went the full 3 rounds; the 5:00 entry is the final bell, not a stoppage. UFC debut win, with official scores 29-28, 29-28 and 28-29. Cuamba took the short-notice opening when Damir Hadžović encountered visa problems. Oki moved to 9-1 and 1-0 in regular UFC bouts.
