items.sourceLabel: Sherdog professional results; UFC for Octagon scorecards

items.label: LOSS · Chris Duncan · Technical submission (guillotine choke) · R1 3:34
items.detail: UFC Fight Night: Moicano vs. Saint Denis in Paris: Oki lost to Chris Duncan by technical submission (guillotine choke). The recorded finish was at 3:34 of round 1. Duncan rendered Oki unconscious in a guillotine; the technical-submission loss was officially recorded at 3:34 of round one. Tapology lists 3:44, but UFC and Sherdog agree on 3:34.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog professional results; UFC for Octagon scorecards

items.label: Pulls out of Al-Selwady fight with an injury
items.detail: The UFC confirmed that Oki was removed from his scheduled Feb. 1 fight against Abdul-Kareem Al-Selwady in Riyadh due to injury. The source does not disclose the exact diagnosis, surgery or rehabilitation schedule.
items.sourceLabel: UFC official Saudi Arabia card change, Jan. 29

items.label: MarQuel Mederos withdraws with illness; Aswell steps in
items.detail: The UFC reported that MarQuel Mederos was pulled from the May 31 fight because of illness and Michael Aswell replaced him on short notice. The illness belonged to Mederos, not Oki.

items.label: WIN · Michael Aswell Jr. · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: UFC Fight Night: Blanchfield vs. Barber: Oki defeated Michael Aswell Jr. by unanimous decision. The fight went the full 3 rounds; the 5:00 entry is the final bell, not a stoppage. All three official scorecards read 29-28 for Oki. Aswell was a late-notice replacement for ill MarQuel Mederos. Oki improved to 10-2, 2-1 in regular UFC appearances.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog professional results; UFC for Octagon scorecards

items.label: Discusses UFC adjustment and camp with Paris card fighters
items.detail: In a UFC interview published Sept. 3, Oki said he was becoming more comfortable with UFC fight-week pressure and adapting after the Chris Duncan loss. He finished his camp in Paris alongside Nassourdine Imavov, Benoît Saint Denis and William Gomis. The date is September 2025, not February 2025; shared preparation does not prove a permanent transfer from Valon Team.
items.sourceLabel: UFC interview by E. Spencer Kyte, Sep. 3, 2025

items.label: LOSS · Mason Jones · TKO (elbows) · R2 3:18
items.detail: UFC Fight Night: Imavov vs. Borralho in Paris: Oki lost to Mason Jones by tko (elbows). The recorded finish was at 3:18 of round 2. Jones stopped Oki with elbows in the second round at 3:18. The loss followed a camp Oki finished in Paris alongside several fighters from the card.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog professional results; UFC for Octagon scorecards

items.label: LOSS · Manoel Sousa · KO (punch) · R3 4:12
items.detail: UFC Fight Night: Emmett vs. Vallejos in Las Vegas: Oki lost to Manoel Sousa by ko (punch). The recorded finish was at 4:12 of round 3. Sousa knocked Oki out with a right hand at 4:12 of round three. This was Oki's second consecutive finish loss and brought him to 10-4 overall, 2-3 UFC.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog professional results; UFC for Octagon scorecards

items.label: Booked against Daniel Santos at featherweight for UFC 333
items.detail: The newly announced UFC 333 bout was scheduled at 145 lb, marking a move DOWN from Oki's previously documented lightweight fights at 155 lb. Available records do not yet show an official UFC featherweight weigh-in or successful weight cut, and do not establish why he chose to change divisions.
items.sourceLabel: Marcel Dorff report for Heavy, Sept. 29, 2026

items.label: Featherweight debut presents an untested weight-cut question
items.detail: Sherdog's UFC 333 preview described Oki as moving down to featherweight against Daniel Santos. Oki came in with two consecutive stoppage losses and remained 10-4 overall (2-3 in the UFC). Whether the smaller division changes his physical advantages or conditioning is prospective analysis, not a proven fact.

items.label: Valon Team and Da Vinci Fighting still publicly listed
items.detail: The UFC's fighter questionnaire lists Valon Team and Sherdog additionally lists Da Vinci Fighting. No verified statement documents a permanent late-2026 coaching change or a new primary gym for UFC 333.

items.label: UFC 333 · featherweight bout vs. Daniel Santos
items.detail: Oki (10-4 overall; 2-3 UFC) is scheduled to fight Daniel Santos (14-3) at featherweight on UFC 333 at Etihad Arena, Abu Dhabi. The early preliminary broadcast starts at 10 a.m. U.S. Eastern / 9 a.m. Central / 6 p.m. Abu Dhabi. That is not his individual walkout time. No bout result or official UFC 333 weigh-in is verified as of Oct. 21.

audit.scope: Full dated rebuild including all 14 documented pro MMA bouts (10-4), UFC 2-3 and DWCS contract win, precise fight methods/round/clock including UFC-vs-Tapology discrepancy for Duncan's submission; indexed amateur MMA win and draw, separate historic Muay Thai result; 2018 professional debut at European Beatdown 3, 2019–2021 fight-history gap, canceled European and UFC bookings (2021, 2024, 2025), official injury withdrawal Jan. 2025, May 2025 opponent illness correction, Atomic vacant lightweight title won Oct. 2022 and Mar. 2023 defense vs disputed 'two-time champ' shorthand, dated Sept. 2025 Paris training with Imavov/Saint Denis/Gomis, 2026 featherweight cut announcement vs Santos and Oct. 24 event. No unfounded doping suspensions, surgery, permanent camp changes or successful 145lb weigh-in assertions.

items.label: Birth and Minas Gerais background
items.detail: Daniel Gustavo Gonzaga Santos was born in Minas Gerais, Brazil. Sources disagree over the city: a UFC Oct. 2026 feature says Uberaba, while some fighter registries and Brazilian coverage say Uberlândia. No city is presented as settled without resolving that contradiction.
items.sourceLabel: UFC Oct. 2026 profile and Sherdog birth date

items.label: Works in rural agriculture before focusing on fighting
items.detail: Santos told the UFC he previously lived in the countryside and worked in the fields. The interview does not establish exact employment dates or a specific move to São Paulo.

items.label: Starts MMA training after watching Anderson Silva
items.detail: Santos says he began training in 2011 after seeing a televised replay of an Anderson Silva fight and wanting to experience the feeling of competing in the Octagon. He was about 16; the calendar year comes from his UFC answer, not a first gym registry.

items.label: Receives nickname Willycat after exaggerated sprawl
items.detail: Santos told the UFC his coach nicknamed him Willycat after he instinctively performed a high sprawl in early takedown training, comparing the movement to a cat or the ThunderCats character. A specific gym and date of the nickname are unverified.
items.sourceLabel: UFC athlete Q&A and nickname explanation

items.label: Reports ten amateur MMA fights and ten Muay Thai wins
items.detail: His UFC questionnaire mentions ten amateur MMA bouts and ten Muay Thai wins, but does not give a verified opponent-by-opponent ledger or the amateur MMA win-loss record. These numbers should not be converted into an invented 10-0 MMA record.

items.label: Muay Thai black grade and BJJ purple belt reported
items.detail: UFC lists a Muay Thai black grade from Kickboxing Academy and a Brazilian jiu-jitsu purple belt. Dates and belt-awarding instructors are not fully documented; these are training credentials, not professional wins.

items.label: WIN · Caio Forastieri · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: At Warriors of God, Santos defeated Caio Forastieri by unanimous decision. The fight went the full scheduled 3 rounds; 5:00 is the final bell. His recorded professional MMA debut; won three full rounds in Uberlândia, Brazil.

items.label: WIN · Jose Mauro dos Santos · KO (spinning back elbow) · R2 (time unrecorded)
items.detail: At Fatality Arena 6, Santos defeated Jose Mauro dos Santos by ko (spinning back elbow). The round is reported but the precise finish time is missing. Sherdog does not establish a legitimate elapsed stoppage clock, so the time is intentionally unknown. The UFC later reported Santos was a Fatality Arena regional champion, but no independently verified title-bout status is assigned to this fight.

items.label: WIN · Ary dos Santos · Technical submission (anaconda choke) · R3 2:42
items.detail: At Arena Fight Uberlândia 8, Santos defeated Ary dos Santos by technical submission (anaconda choke). The official recorded finish was at 2:42 of R3. Anaconda-choke technical submission, not a traditional KO. First of his two indexed professional submission wins.

items.label: WIN · Irwing Romero Machado · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: At Fighten / Decagon MMA Championship 2, Santos defeated Irwing Romero Machado by unanimous decision. The fight went the full scheduled 3 rounds; 5:00 is the final bell. Three full rounds and a unanimous decision.

items.label: WIN · Lucas Eurico · KO (method unspecified) · R2 0:20
items.detail: At Copa Euro, Santos defeated Lucas Eurico by ko (method unspecified). The official recorded finish was at 0:20 of R2. Sherdog records a knockout at 0:20 of round two without a more specific finishing technique.

items.label: WIN · Jose Alexandre · TKO (punches and knees) · R3 3:30
items.detail: At Thunder Fight 6, Santos defeated Jose Alexandre by tko (punches and knees). The official recorded finish was at 3:30 of R3. Stopped Jose Alexandre with punches and knees in the third round.

items.label: WIN · Cleverson Silva · TKO (spinning back kick to body) · R1 3:10
items.detail: At Fighten / Decagon MMA Championship 3, Santos defeated Cleverson Silva by tko (spinning back kick to body). The official recorded finish was at 3:10 of R1. The finish was a spinning back kick to the body, consistent with his regional striking background.

items.label: WIN · Dukvaha Astamirov · Majority decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: At ACB 80 in Krasnodar, Santos defeated Dukvaha Astamirov by majority decision. The fight went the full scheduled 3 rounds; 5:00 is the final bell. Won a majority decision in a three-round fight listed at flyweight by Tapology.

items.label: LOSS · Murad Kalamov · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: At ACA 91 in Grozny, Santos lost to Murad Kalamov by unanimous decision. The fight went the full scheduled 3 rounds; 5:00 is the final bell. First professional MMA loss, bringing his record to 8-1; not a KO or submission defeat.

items.label: WIN · Henrique Fantini · TKO (spinning back kick) · R1 2:21
items.detail: At Future FC 6, Santos defeated Henrique Fantini by tko (spinning back kick). The official recorded finish was at 2:21 of R1. First-round spinning-kick stoppage and the ninth win in his professional record.

items.label: FFC bout against Guilherme Santos canceled
items.detail: A planned FFC matchup with Guilherme Santos did not occur. It did not affect the professional record; the precise cancellation reason is not established.

items.label: WIN · Nizambek Abdrashitov · Submission (armbar) · R1 2:37
items.detail: At Brave CF 32 / WEF 91, Santos defeated Nizambek Abdrashitov by submission (armbar). The official recorded finish was at 2:37 of R1. Submitted Abdrashitov with an armbar. This was his final completed professional bout before the April 2022 UFC debut, not a UFC appearance.

items.label: Brave CF 35 fight vs. Rany Saadeh canceled amid COVID restrictions
items.detail: Brave CF 35 was canceled during the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic, so the booked bout with Rany Saadeh was not fought. Do not assume this event alone explains the full 2019–2022 activity gap.
items.sourceLabel: Tapology BRAVE CF 35 canceled event record

items.label: First UFC booking disrupted by Valiev withdrawal and Santos withdrawal
items.detail: Fight listings show a canceled UFC Fight Night matchup with Timur Valiev (Valiev withdrew), followed by a canceled booking with Marcelo Rojo (Santos withdrew) on Oct. 16, 2021. Neither was a completed UFC debut, and their separate cancellation reasons should not be conflated.

items.label: More than 27 months without a completed professional fight
items.detail: Between his Dec. 14, 2019 victory over Nizambek Abdrashitov and Apr. 9, 2022 UFC debut, fight registries show no completed professional MMA bouts. Canceled bookings occurred, but one continuous injury diagnosis for the entire gap is not documented.

items.label: Chute Boxe Diego Lima becomes his documented UFC team
items.detail: UFC and Sherdog list Chute Boxe Diego Lima in São Paulo. Santos has trained alongside Charles Oliveira and Allan Nascimento, and has discussed the team's pressure-heavy fighting environment. No precise date of his first arrival at Chute Boxe is confirmed.

items.label: LOSS · Julio Arce · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: At UFC 273 in Jacksonville, Santos lost to Julio Arce by unanimous decision. The fight went the full scheduled 3 rounds; 5:00 is the final bell. Santos lost a full three-round unanimous decision in his UFC debut. He arrived on a 10-1 regional professional record.

items.label: John Castañeda matchup officially moved to 140-pound catchweight
items.detail: UFC announced a 140 lb catchweight before the event. At the weigh-in Santos was 138.5 and Castañeda 139.5, both under that agreed limit. The match was not a 135-pound bantamweight weigh-in.

items.label: WIN · John Castañeda · KO (punches and knee) · R2 4:28
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night: Dern vs. Yan in Las Vegas, Santos defeated John Castañeda by ko (punches and knee). The official recorded finish was at 4:28 of R2. First UFC victory; the fight was officially changed to a 140-pound catchweight before weigh-ins, and Santos weighed 138.5 pounds under that agreement. The back-and-forth bout received UFC Fight of the Night honors.
items.sourceLabel: UFC official 140-lb catchweight announcement; Sherdog official result

items.label: Receives Fight of the Night bonus against John Castañeda
items.detail: Santos won a second-round KO and earned a UFC Fight of the Night award for the back-and-forth bout. This was the first of two documented Fight of the Night bonuses through October 2026.
items.sourceLabel: UFC bout result and awards summary

items.label: First Johnny Muñoz Jr. booking canceled after Santos injury
items.detail: The original UFC 288 bout against Johnny Muñoz Jr. was scratched with Santos listed as injured. The fight was eventually completed June 3, 2023. An exact medical diagnosis is not established.

items.label: WIN · Johnny Muñoz Jr. · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: At UFC on ESPN: Kara-France vs. Albazi in Las Vegas, Santos defeated Johnny Muñoz Jr. by unanimous decision. The fight went the full scheduled 3 rounds; 5:00 is the final bell. Official scorecards were 29-27 for Santos on all three cards. One point was deducted from Santos in round three for repeated low blows. The win was not an undisputed 30-27 score because of that deduction.
items.sourceLabel: RotoWire 2023 UFC judges' scores and penalty

items.label: Withdraws from Daniel Marcos matchup due to injury
items.detail: The scheduled UFC São Paulo fight with Daniel Marcos did not occur after Santos withdrew. Santos later discussed this as one of two post-June 2023 canceled fights connected to his own injuries. It is not a professional loss.

items.label: Withdraws from UFC 308 bout with Said Nurmagomedov
items.detail: UFC canceled the planned bantamweight fight after Santos withdrew for reasons not specified in the contemporaneous report. His later interview grouped the Marcos and Nurmagomedov bookings among injury-affected camps, but no precise diagnosis is documented for the October 2024 withdrawal.

items.label: Discusses repeated injuries, overtraining and borrowing money
items.detail: In an Ag. Fight interview before the Davey Grant booking, Santos said repeated injuries and canceled fights forced him to reconsider high-intensity training close to fight day. He also described financial hardship during prolonged inactivity, borrowing from his manager and relying on friends while supporting his young daughter. These are his own reported experiences.

items.label: Davey Grant fight canceled after weight-cut medical problem
items.detail: One day before UFC Vegas 105, his planned April 5 bantamweight fight with Davey Grant was called off over medical issues with Santos's weight cut. Brazilian reporting specifically connected the issue to the cut; it was not a completed bout or a formal weigh-in loss.

items.label: Ends almost 23-month competition absence
items.detail: The span between his June 3, 2023 win against Johnny Muñoz and May 10, 2025 win over Jeong Yeong Lee was 707 days, nearly 23 months. Multiple withdrawn or canceled fights, training injuries and weight-management problems were publicly discussed; the layoff should not be described as having no known explanation.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog bout dates and Ag. Fight injury account

items.label: WIN · Jeong Yeong Lee · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: At UFC 315 in Montréal, Santos defeated Jeong Yeong Lee by unanimous decision. The fight went the full scheduled 3 rounds; 5:00 is the final bell. Returned after nearly 23 months away and won 30-27 on each judge's official card. This was his first completed UFC appearance at featherweight (146-pound non-title limit), after earlier bantamweight outings and canceled bookings.

items.label: Returns at featherweight after difficult bantamweight years
items.detail: His UFC 315 fight against Jeong Yeong Lee was at featherweight, the 145-pound division, rather than his prior UFC bantamweight class. Santos made the 146-pound non-title limit and won a unanimous decision, all three cards 30-27.

items.label: Dooho Choi withdraws from originally planned Perth bout
items.detail: Santos was scheduled to fight Dooho Choi at UFC Perth on Sep. 27, but Choi withdrew with a knee injury. Santos was rescheduled for UFC 320 against Joo Sang Yoo, then met Choi in May 2026.
items.sourceLabel: Tapology canceled bout listing and MMA Fighting interview

items.label: Serious weight-cut incident prompts 153-pound catchweight
items.detail: Santos said he experienced major water retention while traveling, then collapsed or lost memory while cutting weight after standing up too quickly. A doctor told him to stop the cut. Coach Diego Lima secured a 153-lb catchweight with Joo Sang Yoo; Santos officially weighed 151 lb, Yoo 152.5. It was a medically disrupted attempted featherweight cut, not a formally recorded miss of the renegotiated limit.

items.label: WIN · Joo Sang Yoo · TKO (punches) · R2 0:21
items.detail: At UFC 320 in Las Vegas, Santos defeated Joo Sang Yoo by tko (punches). The official recorded finish was at 0:21 of R2. Stopped previously unbeaten Joo Sang Yoo with a left hook and follow-up punches. Their bout was renegotiated during fight week to a 153-pound catchweight after Santos's serious weight-cut problem. Santos officially weighed 151 lb and Yoo 152.5 lb, both within the revised agreed limit, not the originally scheduled featherweight limit.
items.sourceLabel: UFC official UFC 320 weigh-in record; Sherdog result

items.label: LOSS · Dooho Choi · TKO (punches, body shot sequence) · R2 4:29
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night: Allen vs. Costa at the Meta APEX, Santos lost to Dooho Choi by tko (punches, body shot sequence). The official recorded finish was at 4:29 of R2. Dooho Choi ended Santos's four-fight UFC winning streak with a body shot and follow-up attack at 4:29 of round two. The bout was awarded UFC Fight of the Night. This was Santos's first professional stoppage loss.
items.sourceLabel: UFC Fight of the Night May 2026 recap and result

items.label: Second UFC Fight of the Night award despite loss to Choi
items.detail: The UFC awarded Fight of the Night to Dooho Choi and Santos. Santos outlanded Choi in the first round but Choi's body-shot finishing sequence ended the fight late in the second.

items.label: Longtime teammate and cornerman Allan Nascimento dies
items.detail: Chute Boxe teammate Allan Nascimento died on Aug. 3, 2026, aged 34. The UFC reported that he was found unresponsive after an apparent heart attack. Nascimento had cornered Santos and trained with him, as Santos later confirmed in October. This is included as a significant change in his fight-team environment, not as an injury to Santos.

items.label: UFC 333 featherweight matchup with Bolaji Oki reported
items.detail: Heavy reported the Oki-Santos bout for the Oct. 24 Abu Dhabi card at featherweight. Santos enters 14-3, 4-2 UFC, and Oki moves down from 155 lb. The booking does not establish a result or a successful Oct. 23 weigh-in.

items.label: UFC previews Brazilian contingent at UFC 333
items.detail: UFC Brazil confirmed Santos as a 14-3 featherweight representing Chute Boxe Diego Lima for UFC 333 against Bolaji Oki, looking to rebound from May's loss to Dooho Choi. An official published fighter profile identified Uberaba as his hometown despite contradictory Uberlândia reports.

items.label: Remembers Allan Nascimento ahead of first fight without him
items.detail: In a Rádio Itatiaia interview, Santos discussed his close friendship with late teammate Allan 'Puro Osso' Nascimento, who had helped him in camps and worked in his UFC corner. Santos spoke about entering UFC 333 without that support following Nascimento's Aug. 3 death. No new head coach or permanent camp change was confirmed.

items.label: Offers views on Volkanovski and UFC 333 featherweight division
items.detail: In a separate Itatiaia interview, Santos argued that Alexander Volkanovski's achievements put him above José Aldo in the UFC featherweight discussion, and named Jean Silva as a dangerous potential challenger. These are Santos's opinions about the division, not confirmed future matchups.

items.label: Chute Boxe Diego Lima still his documented primary gym
items.detail: UFC and Sherdog continue to list Chute Boxe Diego Lima in São Paulo as Santos's team. His long-term association with Charles Oliveira remains documented. No reliable October 2026 evidence proves he has permanently transferred to another camp or changed head coaches.
items.sourceLabel: UFC athlete profile and Sherdog association

items.label: UFC 333 · featherweight vs. Bolaji Oki
items.detail: Santos (14-3 overall, 4-2 UFC) is booked to face Bolaji Oki (10-4, 2-3 UFC) at Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi at featherweight. The early prelims are scheduled for 10 a.m. U.S. Eastern / 9 a.m. Central / 6 p.m. Abu Dhabi local time. This is the segment's start, not a confirmed cage-walk time. No fight result or official UFC 333 weigh-in is known as of Oct. 21, 2026.
items.sourceLabel: UFC official Oct. 19 UFC 333 fight preview

audit.scope: Reconstructed all 17 professional MMA fights 14-3, UFC 4-2, with dates, methods, rounds and verified clocks (2014 spinning-back-elbow time unavailable), UFC Castaneda first win and Fight of the Night, Johnny Munoz point deduction, May 2025 30-27 x3 Lee return and May 2026 Choi Fight of the Night; reported early amateur/Muay Thai background, Chute Boxe Diego Lima/Oliveira affiliation and team member Allan Nascimento death Aug 3 and Santos Oct 21 tribute; all key canceled matchups Oct 2021, 2023, 2024, Apr 2025 weight-cut medical cancellation and Sep 2025 Choi withdrawal; 2023–2025 layoff explained by firsthand April 4 2025 interview on injuries/overtraining/finances; 2025 UFC 320 153-lb catchweight after medical cut disruption vs reported official weighed 151/152.5, not mislabeled as missed revised weight; Sept 29 booking and Oct 24 2026 UFC 333 early prelim. UFC Oct 2026 Uberaba birthplace vs other outlets Uberlandia contradiction qualified; no unsupported drug bans, surgery dates, exact amateur record, Oct 2026 successful weigh-in or verified camp move.

items.label: Born in Port Angeles, Washington
items.detail: Steele was born in Port Angeles and grew up in the Port Angeles/Sequim area of Washington state. He later moved to Texas before settling in Las Vegas during his professional MMA development.
items.sourceLabel: BJJ Heroes biography / UFC birth city

items.label: Begins wrestling during middle school
items.detail: BJJ Heroes reports that Steele began wrestling around 13 after earlier participation in baseball and football. He competed in folkstyle, freestyle and Greco-Roman wrestling before shifting his focus to jiu-jitsu. The year is inferred from his birthday and reported age.

items.label: Moves to Texas and starts Brazilian jiu-jitsu
items.detail: After relocating to Texas in 2013 and having less access to his earlier wrestling programs, Steele began jiu-jitsu at Brazilian Fight Factory with Rodrigo Cabral ('Brucutu'), the coach who eventually awarded him his black belt.

items.label: Wins IBJJF Austin and Dallas Open titles
items.detail: BJJ Heroes documents purple-belt victories at the 2017 IBJJF Austin and Dallas Opens, including no-gi divisions. These are jiu-jitsu achievements, not amateur MMA fights.

items.label: Finishes second at IBJJF No-Gi Worlds as a purple belt
items.detail: BJJ Heroes lists a silver medal at the 2017 IBJJF No-Gi World Championships at purple belt. This should not be confused with an ADCC Trials silver medal or an ADCC World Championship medal.

items.label: Wins Marianas Open and places at American Nationals
items.detail: BJJ Heroes records Steele winning the 2018 Marianas Open at brown belt and finishing third at the IBJJF American Nationals in the same belt grade. Specific bracket match clocks are not reliably documented.

items.label: Wins 170-pound Combat Jiu-Jitsu Worlds title
items.detail: At the EBI-run Combat Jiu-Jitsu Worlds welterweight tournament in Los Angeles, Steele won four matches, beating Khalil Fadlallah, Jean-Paul Lebosnoyani, Bobby Emmons and Nathan Orchard. He beat Orchard in the final by overtime control/ride time, taking the 170-pound world title. This is a grappling championship, not professional MMA.
items.sourceLabel: Combat Press complete Aug. 18, 2019 tournament results

items.label: Earns another IBJJF No-Gi Worlds silver medal
items.detail: BJJ Heroes lists a 2019 IBJJF No-Gi World Championships second place at brown belt, a separate result from his 2017 purple-belt runner-up finish.

items.label: Promoted to BJJ black belt by Rodrigo Cabral
items.detail: Steele received his black belt in January 2020 from Rodrigo Cabral, who had taught him since he started jiu-jitsu after moving to Texas. Later MMA affiliation listings should not erase this long-term Checkmat/Brazilian Fight Factory lineage.
items.sourceLabel: BJJ Heroes detailed coach and promotion biography

items.label: Competes with black-belt-level opponents
items.detail: BJJ Heroes lists Steele's professional grappling wins over Andy Varela at Submission Underground and Alec Baulding at Who's Number One, with other wins on Fight 2 Win and regional submission-grappling shows. These are not included in his professional MMA record.
items.sourceLabel: BJJ Heroes verified grappling bout history

items.label: Beats UFC welterweight Phil Rowe in grappling match
items.detail: At the Who's Number One: Craig Jones vs. Tye Ruotolo card, Steele defeated UFC welterweight Phil Rowe by judges' decision in a submission-grappling match. A grappling win, not an Octagon or MMA result.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Kane Lewis · TKO (punches) · R3 1:33
items.detail: At Fury FC 49, Steele stopped Kane Lewis with punches 1:33 into round three, winning his first recorded amateur MMA fight. The amateur victory is separate from his 8-1 professional record.

items.label: Takes bronze at ADCC North American Trials, 77 kg
items.detail: The official ADCC 2021 East Coast/North American Trials results place Steele THIRD in the men's under-76.9-kg category: Kade Ruotolo won gold and William Tackett silver. Steele lost to Tackett in the semifinal and beat PJ Barch in the third-place contest. This corrects the unspecific 'silver at ADCC trials' claim in UFC's athlete questionnaire, which does not identify a tournament or date.
items.sourceLabel: ADCC official 2021 North American Trials final standings

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Keith Ford · KO (punch) · R1 0:13
items.detail: Steele knocked out Keith Ford with a punch after 13 seconds of round one at Fury FC 54, winning the amateur welterweight title. His indexed amateur MMA record stood at 2-0, both wins by strikes.
items.sourceLabel: Fury FC 54 results at MMA Sucka

items.label: Competes against Jason High and Gregory Rodrigues in FPI grappling
items.detail: At UFC Fight Pass Invitational 1, Steele faced veteran MMA fighters Jason High and Gregory Rodrigues in grappling matches. Databases disagree about one of the individual decisions, so the event participation is noted without assigning both contests unverified wins or defeats.

items.label: Roughly 200 grappling matches reported entering pro MMA
items.detail: A UFC Fight Pass pre-debut profile estimated Steele had already competed in about 200 grappling matches before his first professional MMA contest. This was an approximate retrospective count, not a complete verified fight-by-fight ledger.

items.label: WIN · Jessee Gengler · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: At Fury FC 56, Steele defeated Jessee Gengler by unanimous decision. The match ran 3 complete rounds; 5:00 is the final bell. First official professional MMA bout, contested at welterweight. Steele completed three full rounds to start his pro career at 1-0.

items.label: Training injury forces Fury FC 60 withdrawal
items.detail: While visiting Glory MMA for training, Steele was injured in a grappling exchange with a heavier partner. He withdrew from an Apr. 24 Fury FC 60 bout against Johnny Pantoja. UFC Fight Pass did not establish a precise anatomical diagnosis or surgery date; no specific ligament injury is assumed.
items.sourceLabel: UFC Fight Pass Apr. 19, 2022 firsthand interview

items.label: Johnny Pantoja fight does not occur
items.detail: The planned Fury FC 60 professional fight with Johnny Pantoja was canceled following Steele's reported training injury. This was not a professional loss.

items.label: Kenan Jackson Fury FC 63 booking canceled
items.detail: Fight registries also list a canceled Fury FC 63 bout against Kenan Jackson. The specific reason is not reliably established from the archived listing; no injury or bout result is inferred.

items.label: WIN · Brakenden Freeman · Submission (rear-naked choke) · R2 1:30
items.detail: At Fury FC Challenger Series 1, Steele defeated Brakenden Freeman by submission (rear-naked choke). The recorded finish came at 1:30 of round 2. First professional MMA submission win. Sherdog dates the event Oct. 22; Tapology and some other fight databases date it Oct. 23. The round and 1:30 finish time agree.

items.label: WIN · Sam Kilmer · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: At Fury FC 73, Steele defeated Sam Kilmer by unanimous decision. The match ran 3 complete rounds; 5:00 is the final bell. Moved to 3-0 as a pro after three completed rounds; the bout was booked at a 160-pound catchweight.

items.label: Tedrick Macklin Fury FC 76 fight canceled
items.detail: A scheduled fight against Tedrick Macklin did not take place. Tapology lists a Steele withdrawal, but the available record does not specify a verified medical reason.

items.label: WIN · Nick (Nicholas) Whitehead · KO (punch) · R1 4:35
items.detail: At Fury FC 81, Steele defeated Nick (Nicholas) Whitehead by ko (punch). The recorded finish came at 4:35 of round 1. Scored a first-round knockout, his first recorded professional KO, and improved to 4-0.

items.label: Chris Pecero booking replaced with Nico Echeverry
items.detail: The fight registry shows that Chris Pecero withdrew from their originally planned Fury Challenger Series 7 matchup. Steele fought Nico Echeverry on the event instead; no separate bout with Pecero took place.
items.sourceLabel: Tapology Fury FC September 2023 bout listings

items.label: WIN · Nico Echeverry · KO (knee and punches) · R2 3:32
items.detail: At Fury FC Challenger Series 7, Steele defeated Nico Echeverry by ko (knee and punches). The recorded finish came at 3:32 of round 2. Steele finished Echeverry late in round two to advance to 5-0. In a subsequent UFC Fight Pass interview, Steele described absorbing several heavy shots before finding his own finish.

items.label: Faces Micael Galvão in Who's Number One grappling match
items.detail: Steele lost a submission-grappling match to Micael Galvão by rear-naked choke at the WNO 21 event. The result is not part of his professional MMA record.
items.sourceLabel: BJJ Heroes recorded grappling bout results

items.label: Faces Ronaldo Souza Jr. at Fight Pass Invitational 6
items.detail: Steele lost a grappling decision to Ronaldo Souza Jr. at UFC Fight Pass Invitational 6, another high-level submission-grappling appearance during his MMA development. No official MMA loss resulted.

items.label: Adam Smith bout at Fury FC 88 canceled
items.detail: A Fury FC 88 matchup with Adam Smith fell through. Another bout with Smith was later listed for April 21 before Steele fought Alejandro Martinez instead. The two canceled bookings should not be counted as fights.

items.label: Adam Smith rematch booking again fails to materialize
items.detail: The April 21 Fury FC 89 bout with Adam Smith was canceled after Smith withdrew. Steele instead fought Alejandro Martinez in a contest listed at 165 pounds.

items.label: WIN · Alejandro Martinez · TKO (punches) · R3 2:09
items.detail: At Fury FC 89, Steele defeated Alejandro Martinez by tko (punches). The recorded finish came at 2:09 of round 3. Third-round finish improved his pro record to 6-0. Tapology lists the actual bout as a 165-pound catchweight rather than a standard 155-pound lightweight fight.

items.label: Relocates to Las Vegas and joins Syndicate MMA
items.detail: In his Contender Series era UFC questionnaire, Steele said he had moved to Vegas a few months earlier and was newly combining regular striking and full MMA training with his grappling base. UFC currently lists Syndicate MMA as his Las Vegas camp, but this does not negate his long-standing BJJ connection to Rodrigo Cabral in Texas.
items.sourceLabel: UFC athlete Q&A and Syndicate MMA team listing

items.label: Quemuel Ottoni withdraws minutes before scheduled DWCS fight
items.detail: Steele was ready to fight Quemuel Ottoni on Dana White's Contender Series Season 8 Week 5, but Ottoni withdrew on the night before the contest began. Dana White said Steele received show and win pay and a promised later opportunity. No specific psychiatric or medical diagnosis for Ottoni is substantiated in the official statement, and no result was recorded on Steele's MMA record.
items.sourceLabel: MMA Junkie Sep. 11, 2024 report and UFC press remarks

items.label: WIN · Chasen Blair · TKO (punches) · R2 4:07
items.detail: At Dana White's Contender Series Season 8 Week 9, Steele defeated Chasen Blair by tko (punches). The recorded finish came at 4:07 of round 2. Returned four weeks after the aborted Ottoni booking and finished Blair in round two, earning a UFC contract. DWCS counts among his seven pre-UFC professional victories, not as a regular UFC Octagon result.

items.label: Secures UFC contract through Contender Series
items.detail: Steele's second-round stoppage of Chasen Blair on DWCS Week 9 earned a contract with the promotion. He was 7-0 overall at the time and had not yet made his regular UFC debut.
items.sourceLabel: UFC athlete record and DWCS results

items.label: Discusses repeated cancellations and approaching UFC debut
items.detail: In a UFC interview before UFC 312, Steele described the frequency of regional cancellations, particularly Ottoni's fight-night withdrawal, and his expectations for entering the UFC. The report also characterized him as a grappler who had become increasingly comfortable with aggressive striking.

items.label: LOSS · Rongzhu (Zhu Rong) · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: At UFC 312 in Sydney, Australia, Steele lost to Rongzhu (Zhu Rong) by unanimous decision. The match ran 3 complete rounds; 5:00 is the final bell. First UFC fight and first professional MMA defeat. All three judges scored it 30-27 for Rongzhu. Many Australia-local event pages use Feb. 9 while Sherdog and UFC show Feb. 8.

items.label: Receives Fight of the Night award despite losing
items.detail: Rongzhu and Steele shared the UFC 312 Fight of the Night bonus, reported at $50,000 apiece. Their bout remained an official unanimous-decision victory for Rongzhu, not a contested scorecard result.

items.label: About 15 months without a completed fight
items.detail: Steele did not make another official MMA appearance between UFC 312 in February 2025 and his return against Dom Mar Fan in May 2026. Sherdog's October 2026 preview refers to an injury-related absence, but a precise diagnosis, surgical procedure or comprehensive explanation for the entire layoff is not established.

items.label: Booked for UFC Perth against Dom Mar Fan
items.detail: Steele's return was reported for the May 2 Perth event against Australian prospect Dom Mar Fan. Steele entered at 7-1 overall (0-1 UFC) with no MMA action since February 2025.

items.label: WIN · Dom Mar Fan · Submission (inverted heel hook) · R1 3:56
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night: Della Maddalena vs. Prates in Perth, Steele defeated Dom Mar Fan by submission (inverted heel hook). The recorded finish came at 3:56 of round 1. First UFC win; Steele finished Mar Fan with a heel hook late in round one, bringing his MMA record to 8-1 and UFC record to 1-1.

items.label: Scheduled to meet Gauge Young at UFC Sacramento
items.detail: Reports announced a lightweight pairing with Gauge Young for Aug. 22 at UFC Sacramento, following Steele's May 2 heel-hook victory. The future fight did not take place.

items.label: Gauge Young contest canceled; reason undisclosed
items.detail: Steele was removed from the Aug. 22 Sacramento card and replaced by Stan Dorsainvil opposite Gauge Young. RotoWire labels the removal as an undisclosed injury but explicitly states the reasons for the withdrawal are unclear; no specific medical diagnosis, surgery or recovery timetable is verified.

items.label: Syndicate MMA continues as listed training camp
items.detail: The UFC lists Steele as training at Syndicate MMA in Las Vegas and competing at lightweight. There is no verified late-2026 announcement of a permanent change of head coach or primary training base.

items.label: UFC 333 previews confirm Noah Gugnon matchup
items.detail: UFC's Oct. 19 fight-by-fight preview and Sherdog's Oct. 21 analysis list Steele (8-1) against Noah Gugnon (10-2) at lightweight. Both entered off UFC submission victories. These sources establish the scheduled fight but do not document a new confirmed injury or fight result.

items.label: UFC 333 · lightweight bout vs. Noah Gugnon
items.detail: At Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi, Kody Steele (8-1 overall; 1-1 UFC) is booked to fight Noah Gugnon (10-2) in the UFC 333 early prelims. The early preliminary broadcast begins at 10 a.m. ET / 9 a.m. CT / 6 p.m. Abu Dhabi time, not a verified individual cage-walk. No weigh-in result or fight outcome is established as of Oct. 21.
items.sourceLabel: UFC official October 2026 card and broadcast schedule

audit.scope: Rebuilt dated profile with all 9 professional bouts (8-1, four KO/TKO, two subs, two decisions) and clocks, two amateur KO/TKO wins plus 2021 Fury amateur welterweight title; 2008 wrestling and 2013 Texas BJJ switch under Rodrigo Cabral, 2017/2019 IBJJF No-Gi silver, Aug 18 2019 EBI Combat Jiu-Jitsu world 170lb title and Nathan Orchard final, Jan 2020 black belt, 2021 ADCC North American Trials third-place per official results (not a verified Trials silver), major grappling matches including Phil Rowe, 2022 Glory MMA training injury without speculative diagnosis, regional canceled bouts, mid-2024 Las Vegas Syndicate MMA move, Sep 10 DWCS Ottoni fight-night cancellation, Oct 8 Chasen Blair contract win, 2025 UFC 312 Rongzhu 30-27 x3 loss and Fight of the Night, 2025-26 layoff not medically overinterpreted, May 2026 inverted heel hook vs Dom Mar Fan, August 2026 Gauge Young cancellation with reason unknown, Oct 19–21 UFC 333 Gugnon booking. No unsupported doping, weight miss, surgery or unverified gym transfer.

items.label: Born in Forbach, Moselle, France
items.detail: Gugnon was born in Forbach, in northeastern France near the German border, and grew up in nearby Spicheren. UFC identifies Spicheren as his hometown. Born in Forbach and raised in Spicheren are not conflicting claims, nor are living in Moselle and later training in Lyon.
items.sourceLabel: Greyball biographical listing and UFC hometown

items.label: Follows older brother into judo and boxing
items.detail: Gugnon told the UFC that he started combat sports by following his brother to the gym, first taking up judo and later boxing. Exact start dates and competition records for the two disciplines are not documented.

items.label: Follows brother into MMA in eastern France
items.detail: He began MMA around 15 after following his brother once more. Initially he trained in a small club near home, then joined coach Eddy Carda at Old Dog Fight Team in Sarrebourg, developing wrestling and grappling alongside amateur MMA and pancrace. Date approximated using Oct. 2000 birth.
items.sourceLabel: UFC and La Sueur regional MMA interview (Jun. 25, 2026)

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Marco Wowra · unanimous decision · R2 3:00
items.detail: Sherdog's indexed amateur MMA ledger records Gugnon defeating Marco Wowra at Integra FC 6 by unanimous decision over two three-minute rounds. This is one confirmed amateur bout, NOT a comprehensive amateur record; his amateur pancrace and grappling results lack a unified fight-by-fight database.

items.label: National pancrace championship; BJJ and Luta Livre progress
items.detail: Gugnon's UFC questionnaire credits him with a French national pancrace championship and purple belts in both BJJ and Luta Livre. He also reports amateur pancrace, MMA, wrestling and grappling tournaments while training with Eddy Carda. An exact championship date, bracket or official total is not established.
items.sourceLabel: UFC athlete questionnaire and La Sueur June 2026 interview

items.date: Before UFC signing (job dates not publicly verified)
items.label: Runs e-commerce business and works nightclub security
items.detail: After high school, Gugnon chose to start an e-commerce business rather than attend university. He also worked in nightclub security and has described the UFC contract as the start of his full professional fighting career. Sources do not establish when he stopped either job.

items.label: Yann Risacher matchup canceled with HFC 22 event
items.detail: Fight listings contain a scheduled Hard Fighting Championship 22 bout against Yann Risacher, but the event was canceled and there is no completed result. This predates Gugnon's documented Oct. 2021 professional debut.

items.label: WIN · Jessy Chateauneuf · Submission (rear-naked choke) · R2 1:53
items.detail: At 100% Fight 44 in France, Gugnon defeated Jessy Chateauneuf by submission (rear-naked choke). The recorded finish was 1:53 of round 2. Professional MMA debut. Submission in round two after previously competing in amateur MMA.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog official MMA results and event details

items.label: WIN · Sofiane Belaïd · Submission (rear-naked choke) · R1 1:50
items.detail: At Warrior Fight Night 1, Gugnon defeated Sofiane Belaïd by submission (rear-naked choke). The recorded finish was 1:50 of round 1. Second consecutive professional submission victory.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog official MMA results and event details

items.label: Nacim Belhouachi regional booking does not occur
items.detail: A proposed MMA Event 10: X-PLOSIF bout against Nacim Belhouachi appears as canceled; no professional fight result or specific withdrawal cause is verified.
items.sourceLabel: Archived fight schedule and cancellation register

items.label: WIN · David Hawker · KO (punches) · R1 1:33
items.detail: At Bushido Fighting Championship 88, Gugnon defeated David Hawker by ko (punches). The recorded finish was 1:33 of round 1. First recorded professional knockout; the contest was listed at featherweight (145 lb), while later bouts were mainly lightweight.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog official MMA results and event details

items.label: Jeremy Cochet bout replaced by Kadimagomaev
items.detail: Gugnon's proposed Kingdom Fighting 1 matchup with Jeremy Cochet did not occur; on the same card he beat Dukwach Kadimagomaev. The register does not establish the reason for the switch.

items.label: WIN · Dukwach Kadimagomaev · TKO (punches) · R2 2:02
items.detail: At Kingdom Fighting 1 in Grenoble, Gugnon defeated Dukwach Kadimagomaev by tko (punches). The recorded finish was 2:02 of round 2. Improved to 4-0. He fought Kadimagomaev rather than the initially listed Jeremy Cochet.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog official MMA results and event details

items.label: LOSS · Mark Ewen · TKO (elbows and punches) · R2 3:51
items.detail: At Bellator 299 in Dublin, Gugnon lost to Mark Ewen by tko (elbows and punches). The recorded finish was 3:51 of round 2. First professional loss. Bellator was the highest-profile promotion of his career to that point; the bout ended from ground strikes in round two.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog official MMA results and event details

items.label: Jonathan Carlos bout scrapped at UFL 9
items.detail: Gugnon was booked against Jonathan Carlos for UFL 9, but the event was canceled. No professional loss, injury or submission is assigned to the planned bout.

items.label: LOSS · Samvel Vardanyan · Decision (unanimous per Sherdog; split per Tapology) · R3 5:00
items.detail: At Fight Parc Championship in Tarbes, Gugnon lost to Samvel Vardanyan by decision (unanimous per sherdog; split per tapology). Completed 3 five-minute rounds; 5:00 is the final bell, not a stoppage. The fight went the full 15 minutes. Sherdog lists a unanimous decision, while Tapology/NextKnockout call it a split decision; the discrepancy is not resolved by official judges' scorecards. The defeat left Gugnon 4-2, following back-to-back losses.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog official MMA results and event details

items.label: Moves to Lyon to train with Fatah Menane at Ghost Arena
items.detail: After back-to-back Bellator and Fight Parc defeats, Gugnon relocated to Lyon and joined Ghost Arena. Coach Fatah Menane told L'Équipe that he and the team worked on Gugnon's tactical decision-making and gave him access to a full coaching staff, professional training facilities and twice-daily training. This is a documented career move, unlike undated directory labels.
items.sourceLabel: L'Équipe Aug. 1, 2026 interview with coach Fatah Menane

items.label: First scheduled Jacson Carvalho meeting canceled
items.detail: A proposed Kingdom Fighting 2 matchup with Jacson Carvalho was canceled after its April 20 event was postponed. This did not count as a professional fight.

items.label: Second Jacson Carvalho booking falls through
items.detail: Gugnon was again listed against Jacson Carvalho at Kingdom Fighting 2, but the June 8 matchup did not take place. No specific injury or withdrawal cause is verified.

items.label: Third Carvalho booking not contested; faces Bruno Nunes
items.detail: The planned Jacson Carvalho pairing at Coliseum Fighting Championship 1 was canceled. Gugnon instead fought Bruno Nunes on October 3 and submitted him. These were not two separate completed MMA fights.
items.sourceLabel: Archived canceled pairing / actual Sherdog result

items.label: WIN · Bruno Nunes · Submission (rear-naked choke) · R1 4:20
items.detail: At Coliseum Fighting Championship 1, Gugnon defeated Bruno Nunes by submission (rear-naked choke). The recorded finish was 4:20 of round 1. Resumed winning following two straight losses, competing at a listed 161-lb catchweight. A Jacson Carvalho bout had been indexed for this same date but did not occur.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog official MMA results and event details

items.label: WIN · Nicolas Di Franco · TKO (elbows) · R2 3:24
items.detail: At The King of Fighters 11 in Amiens, Gugnon defeated Nicolas Di Franco by tko (elbows). The recorded finish was 3:24 of round 2. Second victory of the comeback streak. Elbow ground strikes produced the second-round stoppage.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog official MMA results and event details

items.label: Ghost Arena, Old Dog Fight Team and Bulgarian Top Team listings
items.detail: L'Équipe identifies Fatah Menane and Ghost Arena in Lyon as the specific post-2024 coaching relationship. La Sueur documents his formative Old Dog Fight Team coach Eddy Carda in Sarrebourg. UFC and Sherdog list Bulgarian Top Team in 2026, while Tapology carries Old Dog Fight Team. Manager Guillaume Peltier founded Bulgarian Top Team. These entries must not be treated as proof of three sequential, permanently exclusive gyms.
items.sourceLabel: L'Équipe interview / UFC listed training affiliation

items.label: WIN · Ioan Harris · KO (punch and elbows) · R1 1:02
items.detail: At ARES FC 31 in Marseille, Gugnon defeated Ioan Harris by ko (punch and elbows). The recorded finish was 1:02 of round 1. First ARES FC appearance and a one-minute knockout that Gugnon later identified as a career turning point. Some French coverage describes this as a performance-bonus night, but payout is not presumed from the KO alone.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog official MMA results and event details

items.label: First ARES FC appearance becomes turning point
items.detail: Gugnon later singled out his one-minute KO of Ioan Harris at ARES 31 as the fight that raised his public profile in France. This was a promotional breakthrough after two consecutive regional stoppage wins, not a win of the ARES lightweight championship.

items.label: WIN · Adrian Prisceanu · TKO (punches) · R1 3:33
items.detail: At ARES FC 35 in Strasbourg, Gugnon defeated Adrian Prisceanu by tko (punches). The recorded finish was 3:33 of round 1. Stopped Prisceanu in his second ARES FC appearance on his 25th birthday.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog official MMA results and event details

items.label: WIN · Bruno Matos de Sousa · TKO (elbows and punches) · R1 3:08
items.detail: At ARES FC 39 in Bordeaux, Gugnon defeated Bruno Matos de Sousa by tko (elbows and punches). The recorded finish was 3:08 of round 1. Third ARES FC victory and fifth consecutive finish. Sherdog lists 3:08 while Tapology and NextKnockout list 3:09; the one-second timing discrepancy remains flagged.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog official MMA results and event details

items.label: Third consecutive first-round ARES FC finish
items.detail: Gugnon beat Bruno Matos de Sousa at ARES 39, following first-round finishes of Ioan Harris and Adrian Prisceanu at ARES 31 and 35. At 9-2, he had finished all nine pro wins and won five consecutively since February 2024.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog pro record and ARES events

items.label: Signs with UFC at 9-2 after French regional winning streak
items.detail: French outlet La Sueur reported his UFC signing June 25, 2026 at 9-2, following five consecutive stoppage wins. His debut was set for August 1 against Miloš Janičić in Belgrade. Neither his Oct. 2025 birthday nor his 2026 signing should be presented as a separate fight.
items.sourceLabel: La Sueur UFC signing announcement, Jun. 25, 2026

items.label: Credits Eddy Carda and discusses MMA resources in Lorraine
items.detail: Gugnon said Spicheren and the surrounding Moselle region remained important to him. He credited former coach Eddy Carda with developing MMA locally and argued that eastern France needed better facilities, despite a strong base of promising fighters. He also cited professional training work outside Lorraine.

items.label: Makes UFC lightweight limit at 155 pounds in Belgrade
items.detail: At the official UFC Belgrade weigh-ins, Gugnon weighed 155 pounds for a non-title lightweight contest. Opponent Miloš Janičić weighed 156, also within the permitted non-title allowance. Both officially made weight.

items.label: WIN · Miloš Janičić · Submission (rear-naked choke) · R1 1:21
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night: Medić vs. Rodriguez in Belgrade, Gugnon defeated Miloš Janičić by submission (rear-naked choke). The recorded finish was 1:21 of round 1. Official UFC debut and 81-second RNC. A powerful early low kick appeared to compromise Janičić's lead leg before Gugnon followed him down, advanced position and took the back. UFC confirms the 1:21 finish. His record reached 10-2, six straight wins.

items.label: UFC debut win extends finish streak to six
items.detail: The first-round rear-naked choke of Janičić in Belgrade was Gugnon's tenth professional win, fourth RNC finish and sixth consecutive stoppage victory since his 4-2 start. The UFC describes a low kick that damaged Janičić's lead leg before the transition to dominant ground positions and the choke.
items.sourceLabel: UFC official Belgrade results and fight recap

items.label: Discusses declined short-notice Farès Ziam offer for UFC Paris
items.detail: Gugnon told the RMC Fighter Club that the UFC offered him a Sept. 5 Paris fight with Farès Ziam soon after his Belgrade debut. Gugnon was interested, but his manager Guillaume Peltier declined to protect his longer-term progression; Ziam instead faced Axel Sola. This was an informal offer, NOT a scheduled and subsequently canceled professional bout.
items.sourceLabel: RMC Fighter Club Aug. 26 podcast and Karate Bushido report

items.label: Booked at lightweight against Kody Steele for UFC 333
items.detail: UFC 333 added Gugnon versus Kody Steele to the Oct. 24 card in Abu Dhabi. Gugnon entered 10-2 with six straight wins and one UFC bout. The announced three-round fight is at lightweight, not featherweight.
items.sourceLabel: MMA Knockout / Sports Illustrated Oct. 5 report

items.label: Describes growing recognition after Belgrade UFC victory
items.detail: Discussing the response to his 81-second submission win, Gugnon said his social-media following had roughly tripled and that he felt more accepted by French fans. This is his own estimate of his audience, not a verified platform analytics figure.
items.sourceLabel: ActuMMA October 6 retrospective on RMC interview

items.label: Turns 26 during preparation for UFC 333
items.detail: Gugnon turned 26 on Oct. 18, six days before his booked bout with Kody Steele. Some UFC pre-fight materials continued to show his previous age of 25; his verified Oct. 18, 2000 birthday resolves the age.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog date of birth and UFC bout schedule

items.label: Discusses Steele's grappling and two-a-day training routine
items.detail: In French media coverage, Gugnon acknowledged Steele's extensive grappling background but stressed that grappling in MMA differs because ground strikes are permitted. He said he grapples regularly and trains twice daily throughout the year, adjusting nutrition more than overall training volume for scheduled bouts. This reflects his preparation statements, not proof of a particular fight result.

items.label: Explains UFC's financial and public-profile impact
items.detail: A French-language article summarizing an RMC Sport interview reported Gugnon saying that people now recognize him in public and that sponsorship interest and fight purses have increased since signing with the UFC. He emphasized managing his spending and that sustaining a living from fighting still depends on booking frequency and remaining healthy.
items.sourceLabel: MMA Official Oct. 21 report of RMC Sport interview

items.label: UFC 333 preview compares striking and grappling paths
items.detail: Sherdog's Oct. 21 preview describes Gugnon as a powerful striker still refining his broader MMA approach and identifies Steele as the stronger proven specialist in grappling. These are an analyst's matchup opinions and are not recorded as an injury, camp change, or proven future result.

items.label: UFC 333 · lightweight vs. Kody Steele
items.detail: Gugnon (10-2 professional; 1-0 UFC) is scheduled against Kody Steele (8-1; 1-1 UFC) at Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi. UFC 333's early preliminary broadcast is scheduled for 10 a.m. Eastern / 9 a.m. Central / 6 p.m. Abu Dhabi time, which is NOT a confirmed individual cage walk. There is no official weigh-in or fight result as of Oct. 21, 2026.

audit.scope: Fully rebuilt chronological profile with all 12 professional fights (10-2, 6 KO/TKO and 4 RNC wins) including round and stoppage clocks, one verified 2016 amateur MMA win (not claimed complete amateur record), dated regional cancellations from 2020 through Oct 2024, Bellator Ewen TKO and Vardanyan decision (Sherdog unanimous vs Tapology split discrepancy), move after Feb 2024 loss from Old Dog/Eddy Carda background to Lyon Ghost Arena under coach Fatah Menane, roster Bulgarian Top Team and Old Dog listings as distinct from confirmed training history, first ARES June 2025 KO followed by three first-round ARES finishes, April 2026 one-second stoppage discrepancy, June 2026 UFC signing, July 31 UFC Belgrade official compliant 155lb weigh-in, Aug 1 debut RNC at 1:21 with low kick mechanism, Aug 26 rejected Farès Ziam offer (not recorded as booked fight), Oct 6 and Oct 20–21 interviews, Oct 24 scheduled UFC 333 Kody Steele contest. No unverified doping, surgery, permanent gym move or claimed UFC 333 weigh-in.

items.label: Born in Fortaleza, Ceará, Brazil
items.detail: Iasmin Lucindo Bezerra was born in Fortaleza, Ceará. She grew up in the Genibaú neighborhood and has spoken about supporting her family through her fighting career. Her birth date establishes that she was 15 at her May 2017 professional debut.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog fighter biographical record and Brazilian interviews

items.label: Intervenes during violence against her mother
items.detail: Lucindo and her mother described experiences of domestic violence at home, including an incident in which Lucindo tried to protect her mother when she was about 12. Lucindo has said her wish to protect herself and her relatives led her to martial arts. The 2014 year is inferred from age, not a dated police or court record.
items.sourceLabel: Globo Esporte July 12, 2022 firsthand family interview

items.label: Begins kickboxing for self-defense
items.detail: Lucindo told MMA Fighting she began martial arts at 13 after witnessing domestic abuse, then went 4-0 in kickboxing matches during her first year. The approximate 2015 date derives from her January 2002 birth and reported age.

items.date: Early martial arts years (exact date unknown)
items.label: Begins at Genibaú youth program, later joins Marcos Maju gym
items.detail: Lucindo initially trained in a neighborhood project offering two classes a week, then saved wages from market work to attend coach Marcos Maju's gym in Fortaleza. She and her early staff identified strength coach Cleiton Domingos as another important influence. The precise dates of these early affiliations are not published.
items.sourceLabel: Globo Esporte July 2022 interviews with Lucindo and coaches

items.label: Sells goods at market and delivers meals for her mother
items.detail: While attending school and training, Lucindo worked as a market saleswoman and delivered prepared meals for her mother, Vaneide. She has cited helping her mother buy a house as an early financial motivation for pursuing professional MMA.

items.label: Asks coach to arrange first professional MMA bout
items.detail: According to her 2021 interview, at 14 Lucindo requested her first professional fight. The completed bout was not until May 10, 2017, when she was already 15. Headlines describing her as 'turning pro at 14' appear to refer to the decision or booking phase, not her age on her documented pro debut.

items.label: WIN · Alline Khyra · TKO (punches) · R3 4:12
items.detail: At Big Fight in Maracanaú, Lucindo defeated Alline Khyra by tko (punches). The recorded finish came at 4:12 of round 3. Professional MMA debut at age 15; first recorded win.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog bout registry cross-checked against UFC athlete profile

items.label: WIN · Jardiane Cardoso · TKO (punches) · R2 4:14
items.detail: At 1º Round Combat 4, Lucindo defeated Jardiane Cardoso by tko (punches). The recorded finish came at 4:14 of round 2. Sherdog records R2 4:14; some alternate MMA summaries report R1 1:55. Original local commission video/clock has not resolved the discrepancy.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog bout registry cross-checked against UFC athlete profile

items.label: WIN · Ana Jeize Silva · TKO (punches) · R2 1:45
items.detail: At Coronel Combate 9, Lucindo defeated Ana Jeize Silva by tko (punches). The recorded finish came at 1:45 of round 2. Sherdog gives round two at 1:45 while another widely repeated database lists round one at 2:10. This is their first professional meeting.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog bout registry cross-checked against UFC athlete profile

items.label: LOSS · Sthefanie Jessika Oliveira · Split decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: At Action Fight 7 in Fortaleza, Lucindo lost to Sthefanie Jessika Oliveira by split decision. The bout reached the final bell after 3 rounds; 5:00 is the completion time. First career defeat, coming after three straight stoppage wins. She met Oliveira again a year later and was submitted.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog bout registry cross-checked against UFC athlete profile

items.label: LOSS · Gabriella Fernandes · TKO (punches) · R1 3:20
items.detail: At Parelhas Fight Combat 5, Lucindo lost to Gabriella Fernandes by tko (punches). The recorded finish came at 3:20 of round 1. Her only recorded professional TKO defeat through UFC 333.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog bout registry cross-checked against UFC athlete profile

items.label: WIN · Jéssica Coelho da Cruz Nepomuceno · Submission (armbar) · R2 0:54
items.detail: At Action Fight 9, Lucindo defeated Jéssica Coelho da Cruz Nepomuceno by submission (armbar). The recorded finish came at 0:54 of round 2. First pro submission win. They had a second pro meeting in June 2019.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog bout registry cross-checked against UFC athlete profile

items.label: WIN · Ana Jeize Silva · TKO (method unspecified) · R2 3:47
items.detail: At Punch Fight in Mossoró, Lucindo defeated Ana Jeize Silva by tko (method unspecified). The recorded finish came at 3:47 of round 2. Second professional victory over Ana Jeize; Sherdog shows a second-round TKO at 3:47 while some summaries give first-round punches at 1:35. Don't assign a more precise finish than the indexed registry supports.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog bout registry cross-checked against UFC athlete profile

items.label: LOSS · Sthefanie Jessika Oliveira · Submission (armbar) · R2 2:53
items.detail: At Ita Fight 4, Lucindo lost to Sthefanie Jessika Oliveira by submission (armbar). The recorded finish came at 2:53 of round 2. Second career loss to Oliveira, this time by armbar in round two.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog bout registry cross-checked against UFC athlete profile

items.label: WIN · Ana Nicoly · Submission (armbar) · R1 4:58
items.detail: At Caucaia Fight Champions, Lucindo defeated Ana Nicoly by submission (armbar). The recorded finish came at 4:58 of round 1. Second professional armbar victory.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog bout registry cross-checked against UFC athlete profile

items.label: LOSS · Barbara Acioly · Submission (guillotine choke) · R3 4:00
items.detail: At Invictus Kombat 1, Lucindo lost to Barbara Acioly by submission (guillotine choke). The recorded finish came at 4:00 of round 3. Her fourth loss and last before a subsequent seven-fight regional winning streak.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog bout registry cross-checked against UFC athlete profile

items.label: WIN · Jéssica Coelho da Cruz Nepomuceno · TKO (punches) · R1 4:50
items.detail: At Victorious Fighting Championship 2, Lucindo defeated Jéssica Coelho da Cruz Nepomuceno by tko (punches). The recorded finish came at 4:50 of round 1. Second victory over Jéssica Coelho, this time by first-round stoppage.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog bout registry cross-checked against UFC athlete profile

items.label: WIN · Layze Cerqueira · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: At BrazilMMA 1 in Salvador, Lucindo defeated Layze Cerqueira by unanimous decision. The bout reached the final bell after 3 rounds; 5:00 is the completion time. Sherdog reports a three-round unanimous decision. This win impressed coach Renato Velame and prompted an invitation to his Fight House team.

items.label: Renato Velame invites her to Fight House after Cerqueira victory
items.detail: After Lucindo beat Layze Cerqueira, Cerqueira's coach Renato Velame invited Lucindo to join his Fight House gym in Feira de Santana, Bahia. She became a sparring partner for Virna Jandiroba. This is the best documented camp change in her career, more meaningful than a generic undated Fight House association.

items.label: WIN · Tainá Serena Maia dos Santos · TKO (punches) · R3 2:24
items.detail: At Action Fight 16 in Fortaleza, Lucindo defeated Tainá Serena Maia dos Santos by tko (punches). The recorded finish came at 2:24 of round 3. First completed professional fight after more than 14 months away.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog bout registry cross-checked against UFC athlete profile

items.label: WIN · Sarah Frota · Split decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: At Future MMA: Road to Future 3 in Goiânia, Lucindo defeated Sarah Frota by split decision. The bout reached the final bell after 3 rounds; 5:00 is the completion time. Defeated former UFC competitor Sarah Frota in a close split decision, a meaningful step toward her eventual UFC signing.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog bout registry cross-checked against UFC athlete profile

items.label: WIN · Beriuzka Canelon · TKO (punch) · R2 2:13
items.detail: At Samurai Fight House 1 in Feira de Santana, Lucindo defeated Beriuzka Canelon by tko (punch). The recorded finish came at 2:13 of round 2. Won the inaugural Samurai Fight House women's flyweight championship. Lucindo was not yet a UFC fighter.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog bout registry cross-checked against UFC athlete profile

items.label: WIN · Sharolayne Almeida · TKO (punches) · R1 1:08
items.detail: At Natal Fight Championship 21, Lucindo defeated Sharolayne Almeida by tko (punches). The recorded finish came at 1:08 of round 1. Recorded as a catchweight bout around 143 pounds, not a 115-pound UFC strawweight fight.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog bout registry cross-checked against UFC athlete profile

items.label: WIN · Lucrezia Ria · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: At Cage Fight Series 10 in Graz, Austria, Lucindo defeated Lucrezia Ria by unanimous decision. The bout reached the final bell after 3 rounds; 5:00 is the completion time. Her first documented international professional MMA bout and her seventh consecutive victory before joining the UFC. Overall record reached 13-4.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog bout registry cross-checked against UFC athlete profile

items.label: Explains transition from Fortaleza to Bahia and earning UFC opportunity
items.detail: Globo Esporte reported that Lucindo was training at Academia Fight House in Feira de Santana under Renato Velame. Coach Marcos Maju and strength trainer Cleiton Domingos had played major roles in her earlier career; exact dates of their transition out of daily coaching are not verified.

items.label: Replaces Istela Nunes against Yazmin Jauregui
items.detail: Lucindo, then 13-4, entered UFC San Diego opposite another debutant after Istela Nunes withdrew due to injury. This was Lucindo's first UFC fight; the precise signing day is not independently documented.

items.label: LOSS · Yazmin Jauregui · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: At UFC San Diego: Vera vs. Cruz, Lucindo lost to Yazmin Jauregui by unanimous decision. The bout reached the final bell after 3 rounds; 5:00 is the completion time. UFC debut at strawweight. Lucindo was a replacement for injured Istela Nunes, and both women went the distance in their first UFC appearance. Overall 13-5, UFC 0-1.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog bout registry cross-checked against UFC athlete profile

items.label: Melissa Martinez bout falls through; Brogan Walker replaces her
items.detail: Lucindo was initially scheduled at strawweight against Melissa Martinez, who withdrew. Brogan Walker was booked instead and the fight went ahead at flyweight. This was an opponent change, not a professional loss or cancellation of Lucindo's eventual appearance.
items.sourceLabel: UFC matchup history / Tapology canceled bouts

items.label: WIN · Brogan Walker · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night: Pavlovich vs. Blaydes, Lucindo defeated Brogan Walker by unanimous decision. The bout reached the final bell after 3 rounds; 5:00 is the completion time. First UFC victory, in a 125-pound flyweight bout after a planned strawweight fight with Melissa Martinez fell through. Reached 14-5, UFC 1-1.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog bout registry cross-checked against UFC athlete profile

items.label: WIN · Polyana Viana · Submission (arm-triangle choke) · R2 3:42
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night: Luque vs. dos Anjos, Lucindo defeated Polyana Viana by submission (arm-triangle choke). The recorded finish came at 3:42 of round 2. Second UFC win, first UFC finish. The arm-triangle choke earned the UFC Performance of the Night bonus. Reached 15-5, UFC 2-1.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog bout registry cross-checked against UFC athlete profile

items.label: Collects $50,000 Performance of the Night bonus
items.detail: The UFC awarded Lucindo a $50,000 Performance of the Night bonus for submitting Polyana Viana by second-round arm triangle. Do not miscategorize it as a Fight of the Night award.

items.label: Withdraws from planned Josefine Lindgren Knutsson bout with injury
items.detail: A Sept. 16 UFC card originally included Elise Reed vs Lucindo; Reed was replaced by Josefine Lindgren Knutsson, but then Lucindo withdrew due to an undisclosed injury and Marnic Mann replaced her. No diagnosis or operation is established. Neither planned fight counts toward her record.

items.label: Receives training advice from Amanda Nunes
items.detail: Lucindo said she met former two-division UFC champion Amanda Nunes after her 2022 UFC debut. Nunes subsequently visited during a training camp and offered advice on decision-making, fight IQ and professionalism. A precise visit date is not established, so this is bounded before the May 2024 UFC interview rather than invented as a 2023 bout-week event.

items.label: WIN · Karolina Kowalkiewicz · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: At UFC 301 in Rio de Janeiro, Lucindo defeated Karolina Kowalkiewicz by unanimous decision. The bout reached the final bell after 3 rounds; 5:00 is the completion time. Beat the veteran former title challenger by unanimous decision, improving to 16-5 and UFC 3-1.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog bout registry cross-checked against UFC athlete profile

items.label: WIN · Marina Rodriguez · Split decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: At UFC 307 in Salt Lake City, Lucindo defeated Marina Rodriguez by split decision. The bout reached the final bell after 3 rounds; 5:00 is the completion time. Won a split decision, 29-28, 28-29, 29-28, for a fourth straight UFC victory. Reached 17-5, UFC 4-1.

items.label: LOSS · Amanda Lemos · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: At UFC 313 in Las Vegas, Lucindo lost to Amanda Lemos by unanimous decision. The bout reached the final bell after 3 rounds; 5:00 is the completion time. Lemos ended Lucindo's four-fight UFC winning streak by unanimous decision, 29-28 on all three judges' cards. Reached 17-6, UFC 4-2.

items.label: WIN · Angela Hill · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night: Dolidze vs. Hernandez in Las Vegas, Lucindo defeated Angela Hill by unanimous decision. The bout reached the final bell after 3 rounds; 5:00 is the completion time. Won official scorecards of 30-27, 29-28 and 30-27, bringing her to 18-6 overall and 5-2 UFC. This was her last completed professional fight before UFC 333.

items.label: Out-of-competition sample later tests positive for mesterolone
items.detail: Lucindo provided a sample in Feira de Santana on Sept. 24, 2025, which later tested positive for low-level mesterolone, a prohibited anabolic agent. CSAD subsequently reported a negative August 2025 sample and a negative October 2025 sample, and concluded evidence did not indicate intentional performance enhancement. The source does not give a precise date that Lucindo was notified of the adverse finding.

items.label: Follow-up anti-doping sample in Abu Dhabi is negative
items.detail: CSAD reported that an October 2025 test in Abu Dhabi was negative and came before Lucindo learned of the September positive finding. The exact October sample day is not documented. A negative subsequent result did not annul the September finding.

items.label: Removed from December 13 fight with Gillian Robertson
items.detail: After officials notified the UFC of the positive test, Lucindo was removed from her scheduled December 13, 2025 Las Vegas bout against Gillian Robertson. The date of notification is not specified in the official account; reports initially described a temporary Nevada suspension. She did not fight Robertson.
items.sourceLabel: CSAD formal case narrative and MMA Fighting coverage

items.label: CSAD issues nine-month anti-doping sanction
items.detail: CSAD announced a nine-month UFC Anti-Doping Policy suspension retroactive to Sept. 24, 2025, with an end date of June 24, 2026. It found no evidence that Lucindo intentionally took mesterolone for a performance benefit; she cooperated and provided documents from a Brazilian pharmacy that compounded the substance. Accidental supplement contamination could not be definitively proven, and her failure remains a recorded anti-doping violation. The nine months are not an additional period starting Jan. 27.

items.label: Nevada Athletic Commission also imposes nine-month sanction
items.detail: At its February 18 meeting, Nevada's athletic commission imposed a nine-month suspension aligned with the CSAD period and ordered Lucindo to pay $250 in legal fees. This was a separate commission action but not nine EXTRA months beyond the UFC/CSAD sanction.
items.sourceLabel: MMA Junkie account of Nevada commission action, Feb. 18

items.label: CSAD and Nevada suspension periods conclude
items.detail: The nine-month sanction was measured from Sept. 24, 2025 to June 24, 2026, with Nevada's ruling matching the same end date. Its expiration restored eligibility under the sanctions described; it does not mean that Lucindo fought in June.
items.sourceLabel: CSAD official ineligibility dates and Nevada ruling

items.label: UFC 333 return booked against Nicolle Caliari
items.detail: MMA Junkie reported the all-Brazilian strawweight pairing for Oct. 24 in Abu Dhabi. Lucindo enters 18-6 and 5-2 UFC; Caliari enters 9-4 and 1-2 UFC. This is Lucindo's first scheduled fight since the December 2025 cancellation; it is not a completed result.

items.label: UFC announces Caliari bout will open UFC 333
items.detail: The UFC event preview lists Lucindo vs Nicolle Caliari as the opening bout in Abu Dhabi at 115 pounds. Its early prelim broadcast is scheduled for 10 a.m. Eastern / 9 a.m. Central / 6 p.m. local, which is not an exact confirmed individual cage-walk time.

items.label: More than 14 months without a completed MMA fight
items.detail: Her most recent recorded fight is the Aug. 9, 2025 decision over Angela Hill. By her scheduled Oct. 24, 2026 return she will have been out of MMA competition for about 14½ months. The CSAD and Nevada sanctions ended in June 2026, but a UFC Oct. 21 interview says finding a new booking remained difficult after she was eligible.

items.label: Discusses comeback, training during layoff and difficult booking
items.detail: In a UFC fight-week interview from Abu Dhabi, Lucindo said this was the first year-long stretch without competition of her career. She described adjusting to the inactivity, developing new habits, staying in training without a booked fight and having difficulty securing a matchup after her suspension ended. She predicted improvement but made no medically verified claim about increased strength or specific new camp.

items.label: Acknowledges Caliari's explosive game and her own finishing goals
items.detail: Lucindo called Caliari explosive and well rounded, said she is comfortable striking or grappling, and emphasized seeking a finish wherever the fight goes. These are her pre-fight statements, not evidence of the eventual UFC 333 result.

items.label: Fight House / Renato Velame remains documented camp
items.detail: Sherdog lists Fight House, and Brazilian reporting documents head coach Renato Velame in Feira de Santana and a long-running working relationship with Virna Jandiroba. A specific new 2026 coach or permanent gym transfer has not been confirmed; Amanda Nunes's earlier mentorship was not a documented change of team.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog current team listing and Globo Esporte coaching report

items.label: UFC 333 · women's strawweight vs. Nicolle Caliari
items.detail: Lucindo (18-6 professional; 5-2 UFC) is scheduled to face Nicolle Caliari (9-4; 1-2 UFC) at Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi. This is the advertised opening bout; early prelims start at 10 a.m. ET / 9 a.m. CT / 6 p.m. Abu Dhabi. No weigh-in or fight result is verified as of Oct. 21, 2026.
items.sourceLabel: UFC official Oct. 19 event preview and Oct. 21 fighter interview
