items.label: Born in Curitiba, Paraná, Brazil
items.detail: Nicolle Angélica Caliari was born Nov. 4, 1996 in Curitiba. She is 29 as of Oct. 21, 2026 and fights out of Florianópolis, Santa Catarina after relocating during her regional MMA career.
items.sourceLabel: UFC roster biography and Sherdog birthdate

items.label: Begins karate at her father's suggestion
items.detail: Caliari says her father enrolled her in karate for physical activity and self-defense. Initially reluctant, she grew to enjoy training after placing in youth competitions. The calendar range follows her Nov. 1996 birthday; the exact enrollment date is unknown.
items.sourceLabel: UFC athlete questionnaire and 2024 firsthand interview

items.label: Wins Brazilian, Paraná and world karate competitions
items.detail: Caliari's UFC questionnaire lists Brazilian and Paraná state karate championships and a karate world title, but not the event editions, age categories, exact dates or opponents. These are karate credentials, not professional MMA titles.

items.label: Switches from karate toward Muay Thai and later BJJ
items.detail: Seeking more full-contact competition, Caliari took up Muay Thai as a teenager and added Brazilian jiu-jitsu as she moved toward MMA. UFC lists a brown karate belt, Muay Thai ranks and a purple BJJ belt, without belt-award dates.
items.sourceLabel: UFC fighter questionnaire / Globo 2017 athlete interview

items.label: Studies law but later leaves during final year
items.detail: Caliari says she attended law school and quit in the final year when she had to choose between a legal career and professional fighting. The UFC questionnaire confirms the decision but does not date the withdrawal precisely.

items.label: WIN · Morgana de Cassia Silva · TKO (punches) · R1 time not officially recorded
items.detail: At Imortal FC 2: Kamikaze in Curitiba, Caliari defeated Morgana de Cassia Silva by tko (punches). The event lists round one, but no reliable stoppage clock is available. Her official professional MMA debut. The win made her 1-0; the stoppage clock is not reliably provided.

items.label: LOSS · Syuri Kondo · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: At Pancrase 279 in Japan, Caliari lost to Syuri Kondo by unanimous decision. The fight went the scheduled 3 rounds; 5:00 is the final bell. Caliari traveled to Japan for her second pro fight; Kondo handed her first loss and brought her to 1-1.

items.label: WIN · Edna Oliveira Ajala · TKO (punches) · R2 4:56
items.detail: At Adventure Fighters Tournament 9, Caliari defeated Edna Oliveira Ajala by tko (punches). The finish came at 4:56 of round 2. Returned to winning and improved to 2-1.

items.label: WIN · Thuany Valentim Fernandes · KO (punches) · R1 4:05
items.detail: At Curitiba Top Fight 11: Girls' Night, Caliari defeated Thuany Valentim Fernandes by ko (punches). The finish came at 4:05 of round 1. A first-round KO in Curitiba, professional record 3-1.

items.label: Discusses Muay Thai, female representation and becoming a fighter
items.detail: A Globo Paraná feature discussed Caliari as a professional MMA athlete with a background in karate and Muay Thai. The source confirms her public involvement in women's combat sports in this period, not a specific championship outcome.
items.sourceLabel: Globo Paraná profile of Nicolle Caliari

items.label: WIN · Itzel Esquivel · TKO (punches) · R2 3:56
items.detail: At LFA 26 in Houston, Texas, Caliari defeated Itzel Esquivel by tko (punches). The finish came at 3:56 of round 2. First Legacy Fighting Alliance bout and third straight KO/TKO victory. She improved to 4-1.

items.label: Almost 23 months between completed MMA fights
items.detail: No completed professional MMA bout appears between her November 2017 LFA victory and October 2019 Invicta return. She later spoke more broadly about the challenge of finding sustainable progress in the sport; no specific diagnosed injury explains this entire interval.

items.label: LOSS · Kay Hansen · Submission (guillotine choke) · R3 1:14
items.detail: At Invicta FC 37 in Kansas City, Kansas, Caliari lost to Kay Hansen by submission (guillotine choke). The finish came at 1:14 of round 3. Caliari returned after 23 months and lost to Hansen. MMA Fighting and Sherdog record a guillotine choke; Tapology calls the same finish a neck crank from mount. The method is recorded as disputed across databases, with the official Invicta event report favoring guillotine.
items.sourceLabel: Original promotion report / corroborating fight record

items.label: Invicta names Hansen vs. Caliari Fight of the Night
items.detail: Invicta FC later released the complete Oct. 4, 2019 Hansen vs. Caliari fight as a Fight of the Night selection. That accolade is separate from the official loss by submission and is not a UFC bonus.
items.sourceLabel: Invicta official full-fight archive, published Apr. 2023

items.label: Two-year inactivity period after Invicta loss
items.detail: The records show no completed professional fight between the Oct. 4, 2019 Kay Hansen loss and Oct. 23, 2021 victory over Midian Fernandes Vicente. Archived 2021 bookings were canceled, but there is no verified single injury diagnosis or anti-doping suspension accounting for the whole period.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog professional bouts / Tapology scheduling archive

items.label: Nação Cyborg 8 booking with Vanessa Guimarães does not occur
items.detail: The planned Nação Cyborg 8 matchup with Vanessa Guimarães was canceled with the event. This is a booking, not another loss or a recordable professional bout.

items.label: Considers quitting MMA because the sport is not financially sustainable
items.detail: In a 2024 interview, Caliari recalled that by 2021 she had considered abandoning MMA after extensive work and little financial return. This was a career decision point she described in retrospect, not evidence of a medical or disciplinary absence.

items.label: Proposed Bruna Brasil and Mayara Thays matchups canceled
items.detail: Nação Cyborg 10 archives list canceled proposed matchups with both Bruna Brasil and Mayara Thays. Neither was fought on Oct. 21. The same card's two opponent listings must not be added as completed fights or counted as multiple withdrawals without evidence.

items.label: WIN · Midian Fernandes Vicente · TKO (punches) · R1 3:45
items.detail: At Face the Danger 23 in Brazil, Caliari defeated Midian Fernandes Vicente by tko (punches). The finish came at 3:45 of round 1. Caliari returned to competition, improving to 5-2 after roughly two years away.

items.label: Almost 22-month gap before returning in Fight Music Show
items.detail: The record contains no completed MMA bout between Oct. 23, 2021 and Aug. 26, 2023. In later interviews she discussed almost leaving the sport, limited financial return, and seeking a new coaching plan. It would be inaccurate to attribute the entire period to an unverified physical injury.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog bout history and 2024 profile interview

items.label: Angela Rosa bout does not take place
items.detail: A proposed MF promotion matchup with Angela Rosa appears among canceled regional bookings. No opponent replacement, health condition or fight result was confirmed by the archived match listing.

items.label: Coaches women's Muay Thai and helps manage a gym
items.detail: Caliari says she taught Muay Thai classes for women through 2022 and worked on the administrative/operational side of a gym in which she was a partner. The work accompanied her fighting career and explains the obligations she later left when relocating.

items.label: Moves from Curitiba to Florianópolis for Thai Brasil camp
items.detail: After seriously considering leaving MMA, Caliari accepted a plan from coach Márcio Malko and relocated from Curitiba to Florianópolis, joining Thai Brasil. Malko identified needed technical improvements and targeted a route to the UFC within about one year. She left her previous business routine and felt isolated away from family, according to her 2024 interview. No exact moving day is confirmed.

items.label: Focuses on aggressive finishes to improve UFC prospects
items.detail: Malko told Caliari that emphatic finishes, rather than merely winning decisions, would improve her chance of receiving a Contender Series opportunity. She completed an intensive camp program in Florianópolis. This explains the change in how she approached fight opportunities; it is not a separate MMA win.
items.sourceLabel: UmDois Esportes interview with fighter, Oct. 15, 2024

items.label: WIN · Carolina Jiménez · Submission (armbar) · R2 4:50
items.detail: At Fight Music Show 3 in Brazil, Caliari defeated Carolina Jiménez by submission (armbar). The finish came at 4:50 of round 2. Her first completed fight after moving in 2023. The win moved her to 6-2. Tapology gives 4:51, while Sherdog lists 4:50; the one-second discrepancy has not been conclusively resolved.

items.label: WIN · Daniella Antonelli · Submission (rear-naked choke) · R2 3:34
items.detail: At Fight Music Show: Fight Night 2, Caliari defeated Daniella Antonelli by submission (rear-naked choke). The finish came at 3:34 of round 2. A second consecutive round-two submission victory, taking her to 7-2. Some databases refer to this opponent as Daniella Oliveira or Daniella Oliveira Antonelli; Sherdog uses Daniella Antonelli.

items.label: Receives DWCS opportunity with roughly three months to prepare
items.detail: Caliari said in an October 2024 interview that her Sept. 10 Contender Series invitation arrived roughly three months in advance. She trained two to three sessions daily and worked on the mental side of preparation, while acknowledging pre-fight nerves. June is approximate, not a verified invitation day.

items.label: WIN · Corinne Laframboise · Submission (armbar) · R1 4:45
items.detail: At Dana White's Contender Series Season 8, Week 5, Caliari defeated Corinne Laframboise by submission (armbar). The finish came at 4:45 of round 1. Finished her Canadian opponent in the closing seconds of round one to reach 8-2. The DWCS win counts in the professional MMA record but precedes her official Octagon debut.

items.label: Earns UFC contract from Contender Series victory
items.detail: Dana White awarded Caliari a UFC contract after the first-round armbar over Corinne Laframboise. She reached the promotion on three straight submission wins following her 2023 relocation. Contract date tracks the broadcast, not an unspecified private signing day.
items.sourceLabel: UFC athlete career summary and 2024 firsthand interview

items.label: Discusses difficult move, loneliness and prior retirement thoughts
items.detail: In a lengthy Brazilian interview, Caliari described having nearly quit MMA, feeling isolated from her family after moving to Florianópolis, and becoming emotional during the uncertain road to UFC qualification. She explained that the training plan under Márcio Malko was what changed her direction. These are self-reported personal experiences, not diagnoses inferred from the fight record.

items.label: LOSS · Ernesta Kareckaitė · Split decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night: Dern vs. Ribas 2 in Las Vegas, Caliari lost to Ernesta Kareckaitė by split decision. The fight went the scheduled 3 rounds; 5:00 is the final bell. Official UFC debut at flyweight, ending her submission winning streak. Sherdog, fight-by-fight databases and contemporaneous UFC media report a SPLIT decision, despite one UFC fighter-summary line incorrectly saying unanimous.

items.label: Disputes judging and discusses difficulties making strawweight
items.detail: Caliari said she thought she won rounds one and three against Kareckaitė, and questioned why two apparent fence grabs drew no point deduction. In the same interview, she explained she had previously struggled to reach 115 pounds while maintaining adequate energy, which was why she chose flyweight. These are her post-fight claims, not official overturned results.

items.label: LOSS · Carli Judice · TKO (knee to body and punches) · R3 1:30
items.detail: At UFC 318 in New Orleans, Caliari lost to Carli Judice by tko (knee to body and punches). The finish came at 1:30 of round 3. Judice landed a damaging knee to the liver/body and follow-up punches for the stoppage. Caliari fell to 8-4 overall and 0-2 in regular UFC fights.

items.label: Rebuilds body composition to make strawweight
items.detail: After two UFC flyweight losses, Caliari and her support team spent about six months preparing to move back to 115 pounds. In her May 14 interview she said the program reduced strength-training loads, altered protein intake and focused on reducing muscle mass under professional supervision. No exact program start day is documented.

items.label: Undergoes breast implant removal to facilitate 115-pound cut
items.detail: Caliari told Ag. Fight she had breast implants removed because the added weight complicated her move from 125 to 115 pounds. The procedure occurred before the May 14, 2026 interview; the exact surgery date and postoperative details are not public. This was an intentional career/body-composition decision, not a reported fight injury.
items.sourceLabel: Ag. Fight firsthand interview on implant removal, May 14

items.label: Withdraws from scheduled March 28 fight with Carol Foro
items.detail: Ag. Fight reported the replacement by Stephanie Luciano on Jan. 29, well before the March 28 Seattle event. UFC's Mar. 25 recap later stated Caliari had been injured and withdrawn. No precise body part, medical diagnosis, surgery or rehabilitation timetable is established; the bout was never contested. The Jan. 29 announcement corrects timelines that date the withdrawal itself to March.
items.sourceLabel: Ag. Fight Jan. 29 replacement report / UFC Mar. 25 injury description

items.label: Explains 115-pound switch and implant-removal decision publicly
items.detail: Ahead of the Shauna Bannon fight, Caliari explained the roughly six-month program and said she believed the smaller opponents at strawweight would allow her to compete with greater strength and less physical disadvantage. These are her expectations rather than evidence of a performance outcome.

items.label: Successfully weighs 115.5 pounds for first UFC strawweight fight
items.detail: Caliari officially weighed 115.5 lb for Shauna Bannon at UFC Vegas 117, within the 116-pound non-title strawweight allowance. Bannon also weighed 115.5 lb. This confirms a successful weigh-in at the NEW class, not an October UFC 333 weigh-in.

items.label: WIN · Shauna Bannon · Submission (arm-triangle choke) · R3 3:08
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night: Allen vs. Costa (UFC Vegas 117), Caliari defeated Shauna Bannon by submission (arm-triangle choke). The finish came at 3:08 of round 3. First UFC victory and first UFC bout at strawweight, improving to 9-4 overall and 1-2 UFC. It was her fourth pro submission and her ninth consecutive stoppage win in nine career victories, with five other wins by KO/TKO.

items.label: Credits Ronda Rousey for influencing her judo throws
items.detail: After beating Bannon, Caliari described using the harai goshi-style hip/leg sweep she had admired watching Ronda Rousey's UFC run. She secured takedowns before eventually finishing Bannon with a third-round arm triangle (katagatame). This is a technical influence she acknowledged, not evidence Rousey was her personal coach.

items.label: Maintains Thai Brasil Floripa affiliation
items.detail: UFC and Sherdog list Thai Brasil Floripa, with Márcio Malko as a key coach. Caliari's 2023 move to Florianópolis is documented; no verified permanent 2026 return to Curitiba or new training team has been reported.
items.sourceLabel: UFC current athlete profile and Sherdog team listing

items.label: Lucindo vs. Caliari scheduled for UFC 333
items.detail: MMA Junkie reported the all-Brazilian Oct. 24 strawweight contest in Abu Dhabi on Oct. 1, citing sources close to matchmaking. Caliari enters 9-4 (1-2 UFC) off the May arm-triangle win and Lucindo enters 18-6 (5-2 UFC).

items.label: UFC Brazil confirms 29-year-old strawweight on Abu Dhabi card
items.detail: UFC's Brazilian fighter overview lists Caliari as born in Curitiba, 29 years old, a 9-4 professional record, and newly established at 115 pounds following her win over Bannon. This confirms her roster division and scheduled opponent, not the Oct. 24 result.
items.sourceLabel: UFC Brazil Oct. 17 UFC 333 fighters overview

items.label: UFC preview confirms Lucindo matchup as opening bout
items.detail: The UFC's official fight-by-fight preview describes Caliari vs Iasmin Lucindo as the opening fight at UFC 333, an all-Brazilian women's strawweight pairing. The entire early preliminary segment begins at 10 a.m. Eastern / 9 a.m. Central / 6 p.m. Abu Dhabi local time; no independently fixed individual walkout time is published.

items.label: Enters UFC 333 with nine finishes and first strawweight win
items.detail: Caliari enters Abu Dhabi with 9 wins from 13 professional fights, five KO/TKOs and four submissions, all victories inside the distance. Her most recent fight was May 16 at strawweight, so no October injury status, successful UFC 333 weigh-in or fight result is independently verified yet.

items.label: UFC 333 · women's strawweight vs. Iasmin Lucindo
items.detail: Nicolle Caliari (9-4 overall, 1-2 UFC) is scheduled against Iasmin Lucindo (18-6 overall, 5-2 UFC) at Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi on Saturday, Oct. 24. The UFC advertises it as the opening bout; early prelims begin at 10 a.m. ET / 9 a.m. CT / 6 p.m. UAE local. This is a segment start, not a confirmed personal cage-walk clock. No result is recorded as of Oct. 21.

audit.scope: Full 13-bout professional chronology 9-4 with all dated matches, methods, rounds and verified clocks (2015 debut finish time unavailable), 5 KO/TKO and 4 submission wins, conflicting 2019 Hansen guillotine vs neck crank classification, 2023 Carolina Jimenez one-second clock difference, three documented near-two-year inactive spans not assigned fabricated injury diagnoses; karate age nine, youth titles without unverified medal dates, Muay Thai age 15 and BJJ credentials, unfinished law degree, women's Muay Thai teaching and gym administration through 2022, 2021 near-retirement, exact 2023 Curitiba-to-Florianopolis Thai Brasil relocation under Marcio Malko and Fight Music Show rebound, Sept 2024 DWCS armbar and UFC signing; Jan 2025 UFC debut split-decision loss to Ernesta Kareckaite (UFC Q&A typo says unanimous), post-fight scoring reaction, Jul 2025 Judice TKO; six-month body-composition restructuring and reported implant removal before May 14 2026; Jan 29 cancellation of March 28 Carol Foro fight with generic UFC injury statement but no diagnosis; May 15 2026 compliant 115.5-lb official weigh-in for first strawweight bout; May 16 first UFC victory Shauna Bannon R3 3:08, Ronda Rousey inspired harai goshi and May 18 interview; Oct 1 UFC 333 booking, Oct 17/19 UFC event confirmation, Oct 24 scheduled Lucindo fight without pre-emptive weigh-in/outcome. Team remains Thai Brasil Floripa, no verified doping suspension or permanent new coach.
